name: Ace Trainer
flavorText:
Strength, Focus, Ingenuity 
 The Ace Trainer is an expert battler, using wit and 
strength to maneuver the battlefield and power through 
any forces that might stand in their way with their 
Pokémon. Many Ace Trainers love the league circuit and 
do everything in their power to join championships and 
fight for first place. When further developing their battle 
prowess, Ace Trainers delve into specific expertise having 
to do with various specialties ranging from Pokémon 
types, to Pokémon technical stratagem, or even the stage 
of development a Pokémon might be.

features.name: Affirmation
features.description: Whenever your Pokémon knock out an opposing Pokémon, or whenever they score a critical hit, they gain temporary hit points equal to your Attack or Special Attack modifier.

features.name: Improved Attacks
features.description: Whenever your Pokémon hits with an attack, they deal additional damage equal to your Attack or Special Attack modifier, depending on which Attack or Special Attack modifier your Pokémon is adding to their attack respectively.

features.name: Intimidate
features.description: Ace Trainers can cause opposing Pokémon to question their aggressiveness by glaring intensely at them. 3/day, as an action, give target Pokémon Attack▼ or SpAttack▼. You need a line of sight to the target within 40ft.

features.name: Stat Increase and Advanced Class
features.description: Choose two different Trainer Stats to increase by 1, then gain 1d4 max HP. You only gain new stats at levels 3, 7, and 11. Choose an Ace Trainer Advanced Class or a different base Class. You can only ever gain a single Class or Advanced Class at a time, when leveling up.

features.name: Constructive Criticism
features.description: You can discern why you Pokémon’s attacks are failing to get through an opposing Pokémon’s defenses. Whenever your Pokémon misses with an attack, the next time they use that attack on the same target add 2 to their Accuracy Check. This bonus can stack with itself, if your Pokémon continues to miss against the same target with the same Move. Once your Pokémon hits, with that Move against the same target, Constructive Criticism’s bonus is reset.

features.name: Press
features.description: You can push your Pokémon harder through intense motivation. As an action, one of your Pokémon within line of sight gets Attack▲, SpAttack▲, Defense▲, or SpDefense▲. That Pokémon takes X damage, where X is 8 minus either your Attack or Special Attack modifier. Be careful, the repeated use of Press on your Pokémon may push them too far and you could begin to negatively affect their loyalty to you.

features.name: Pokémon Master
features.description: You become a master commander to your Pokémon. As long as it’s your Pokémon, they cannot disobey commands regardless of their loyalty. This does not improve their relationships with you, your Pokémon simply cannot disobey your commands.

features.name: Stat Increase and Advanced Class
features.description: Choose two different Trainer Stats to increase by 1, then gain 1d4 max HP. You only gain new stats at levels 3, 7, and 11. Choose an Ace Trainer Advanced Class or a different base Class. You can only ever gain a single Class or Advanced Class at a time, when leveling up.

features.name: Taskmaster
features.description: You learn how to best to push your Pokémon to their limits without causing them any distress. Whenever you use any Press actions, cure your Pokémon of being Dazed, Confused, or Entranced and then remove any Stat▼ afterwards. Your Pokémon’s loyalty is not negatively affected by repeated uses of any Press actions.

features.name: Battle Frenzy
features.description: You know when enemy Pokémon are nearing their limits and your Pokémon begin to mirror your excitement during battle. As an action, you can identify whether or not a target Pokémon is at or below half of its full HP. If a target is, one of your active Pokémon can move +10ft per turn long as it is pursuing or attacking that Pokémon.

features.name: Break Through
features.description: You see every weakness in every Pokémon just by studying them for a couple of seconds and specify the point while instructing your Pokémon. 3/ day, as an action, you can target a Pokémon with Break Through! For the remainder of the encounter, your Pokémon can use both their Attack or Special Attack against either of the target’s Defense or Special Defense in order to hit during accuracy check regardless of the attack’s preference. In addition, after using Break Through, the target’s Defense and Special Defense values are revealed to you.

features.name: Stat Increase and Advanced Class
features.description: Choose two different Trainer Stats to increase by 1, then gain 1d4 max HP. You only gain new stats at levels 3, 7, and 11. Choose an Ace Trainer Advanced Class or a different base Class. You can only ever gain a single Class or Advanced Class at a time, when leveling up.

features.name: Press On
features.description: You can urge your Pokémon to make one more desperate attack. 1/day, you can issue a command to one of your Pokémon who was just knocked out during the last round of combat. If it does, you must immediately return it to its Poké Ball during your turn after it acts. If the Pokémon is further damaged to -100% HP, you may still need to roll a death saving throw if the foe had lethal intent.

features.name: Battle Experience
features.description: You have enough battles behind you that you have a good idea of what to expect, or when to expect the unexpected. As an action, you may target an opposing Pokémon and identify whether or not the Pokémon has a super-effective Move against any of your active Pokémon. If they do, you are informed of what attacks they are.

features.name: Finish It
features.description: Your Pokémon’s attacks have more power in them as a foe gets nearer to being knocked out. If a target of one of your Pokémon’s damaging attacks are lowered to 6 or less HP, it is knocked out or set to 1 HP (you decide).

features.name: Grand Master
features.description: Your Pokémon’s strength is inspired by your presence to push out a little more with every attack. Whenever your Pokémon hits with an attack, they deal additional damage equal to twice your Attack or Special Attack stat, regardless of which Attack or Special Attack modifier your Pokémon is adding to their attack respectively. Your Pokémon may also add either your twice your Attack or Special Attack modifier to attacks without a Damage value, to deal damage with those attacks (this feature does not replace Improved Attacks).

name: Stat Ace
flavorText:
Fine tuning specific traits to defeat opponents. 
 The Stat Ace obsesses over one trick. Whether it’s 
building a team of the ultimate offensive strikers, or a wall 
of unbreakable defenders, they will enable each Pokémon 
on their team to do the best at what the Stat Ace wants 
them to do.

features.name: Specialist Training
features.description: You need something very specific from your Pokémon and they have matched that urgency, honing themselves to match your favored stat. Add half of your Attack or Special Attack modifier to the favored stat of each of your Pokémon that you’ve owned for at least a week. In addition, your Pokémon’s stats can’t get ▼ for your favored stat.

features.name: Favorable Recruitment
features.description: Something about your personality is picked up and mirrored by wild Pokémon. Whenever you capture or obtain a new wild Pokémon, or hatch a Pokémon egg, roll the Pokémon’s Nature twice. If either nature positively influences your favored stat, you may choose that nature. If neither do, the Pokémon’s nature is the second rolled nature.

features.name: Stat Press
features.description: Your motivation may be harsh, but your Pokémon have the same goals as you when it comes to your favored combat style. 3/day, when you use Press on your Pokémon to temporarily raise your favored stat, you do not negatively affect your Pokémon’s loyalty and choose from Attack▲▲, SpAttack▲▲, Defense▲▲, SpDefense▲▲, or Speed▲▲, instead.

features.name: Affliction Resistance
features.description: Your specialized training has created a natural resistance to hardships that your Pokémon face in battle. Depending on your favored stat, Pokémon you’ve owned for at least one week have the following immunities that apply to different afflictions. Favored Stat Effect Attack: Your Pokémon are immune to being Drowsy. Defense: Your Pokémon are immune to being Burned. Sp. Attack: Your Pokémon are immune to being Confused. Sp. Defense: Your Pokémon are immune to being Poisoned. Speed: Your Pokémon are immune to being Paralysis.

features.name: Field Tactics
features.description: Your Pokémon’s aptitudes come into play on the field of battle, edging out every advantage possible during battle. Depending on your favored stat, your Pokémon’s attacks, or reactions when attacked have additional effects. Favored Stat Effects Attack: Your Pokémon’s moves that use the Attack stat have the following ability: “On hit, you may push the targets up to 10ft away from you.” Defense: When an opponent attempts to hit your Pokémon using a move that uses the Attack stat and misses, your Pokémon may push the attacker 20ft away from them. Special Attack: Your Pokémon’s moves that use the Special Attack stat have the following abilities: “On hit, you may push the targets up to 10ft away from you.” Special Defense: When an opponent attempts to hit your Pokémon using a move that uses the Special Attack stat and misses, your Pokémon may push the offender 20ft away from them. Speed: After using a Move, your Pokémon can move 15ft, before the end of their turn.

features.name: Attitude Adjustment
features.description: Your supervision can influence your Pokémon’s behavior. 1/day, after one hour of work with one of your Pokémon, you may reroll that Pokémon’s nature until you roll a nature that positively influences your favored stat.

features.name: Honed Skill
features.description: Your specialized training has become a part of your Pokémon, even without you near them. If your Pokémon have been with you for at least a week, you may teach them the following Passives after one hour of additional training. The added Passive must still follow the Passive limit of four. Favored Stat Passive Attack: Mighty (+2 Attack) Defense: Fortified (+2 Defense) Special Attack: Amplified (+2 Special Attack) Special Defense: Invulnerable (+2 Special Defense) Speed: Volant (+2 Speed)

features.name: Desperate Measures
features.description: You weigh the needs of a battle to make desperate measures and win with your chosen strategies. 1/day, after two hours of work you can tutor the following moves to your Pokémon depending on your favored stat. Favored Stat Move Attack: Belly Drum - 3/day Self Normal Effect. Stance: When you attack, you lose half of your current HP, then you get Attack▲▲▲. Defense: Unbreakable Armor - 3/day Normal Self Effect. Stance: You take -12 damage from Physical attacks. When you use an attack, if you don’t have any ▼ you get Attack▼ and SpAttack▼. Special Attack: Migraine - 3/day Self Normal Effect. Stance: When you attack, you lose half of your current HP, then you have SpAttack▲▲▲. Special Defense: Unbreakable Barrier - 3/day Normal Self Effect. Stance: You take -12 damage from Special attacks. When you use an attack, if you don’t have any ▼ you get Attack▼ and SpAttack▼. Speed: Mach Speeds - 3/day Normal Style. You may lose half of your current HP to give your moves Priority and have +25 movement on your turn this round.

features.name: Stat Affirmation
features.description: The fruit of your labors is coming forth. Every time your Pokémon succeed with your favored stat, they are energized by their efforts. Depending on your favored stat, your Pokémon have the following bonuses during combat. Favored Stat Effect Attack: Whenever your Pokémon hits with a Physical attack, they gain temporary HP equal to your Attack or Special Attack modifier. Defense: Whenever your Pokémon is attacked with a Physical move and the attack misses or deals less than 10 damage, they gain temporary HP equal to your Attack or Special Attack modifier. Special Attack: Whenever your Pokémon hits with a Special attack, they gain temporary HP equal to your Attack or Special Attack modifier. Special Defense: Whenever your Pokémon is attacked with a Special move and the attack misses or deals less than 10 damage, they gain temporary HP equal to your Attack or Special Attack modifier. Speed: Whenever your Pokémon is attacked with an Effect move and the attack misses, they gain temporary HP equal to your Attack or Special Attack modifier.

features.name: Stat Tactics
features.description: You employ greater efforts to tutor your Pokémon, or your ally’s Pokémon, finding even better uses for their skills. Once per week, you may spend three hours tutoring your Pokémon to learn a move depending on which favored stat you’ve chosen. If you tutor an ally’s Pokémon it take six hours. Favored Stat Move Attack: Giga Impact - 1/day Physical Melee(10ft burst): Normal 4d12. If you have used at least 3 other Normal-type moves this combat, Giga Impact has +2d power. Giga Impact must Recharge. Defense: Detect - 1/day Self Fighting Effect. Reaction [When you are hit by an attack]. The attacker must reroll their AC at disadvantage. If the attacker still hits, you do not lose your next action. Special Attack: Hyper Beam - 1/daySpecial Ranged(35ft beam): Normal 4d12. If you have used at least 3 other Normal-type moves this combat, Hyper Beam has +2d power. Hyper Beam must Recharge. Special Defense: Protect - Self Normal Effect: 1/day. Reaction [When you are hit by an attack]. Roll 1d20 and add your Defense or SpDefense. If you got more than 20, you take no damage from the attack. If the attacker still hits, you do not lose your next action. Speed: Double Team - 1/day Self Normal Effect. Spend 12 HP, then create three DT Hazards with 1 HP within 20ft. Stance: At the start of your turn, you may move each DT Hazard up to 10ft or swap places with one of them within 30ft.

features.name: Superior Aura
features.description: Your glaring presence disparages enemy Pokémon and causes them to underperform during battle. 3/day, once per turn as a free action, you may remove a target(50ft) Pokémon’s ▲.

name: Strategist
flavorText:
Creating openings and tricky advantages in battle.
 The Strategist prefers to set up a field of battle in their 
favor, instead of relying solely on power to push through 
an opponent’s plans.

features.name: Field Scout
features.description: The field of battle is not always fair to your Pokémon, so you’ve focused your basic training on making the field much fairer. 1/day you may spend half an hour teaching any Pokémon the move Rapid Spin. Rapid Spin - At-Will Physical Melee: Normal 1d6. While you move around this turn, you may destroy Coats on any adjacent targets you pass, free adjacent Bound allies, and/or destroy any Hazards.

features.name: Terrain Mastery
features.description: You spend time every week training your Pokémon to navigate rough terrains and complex environments. Your Pokémon that you’ve had for at least one week are not affected by difficult terrain while moving.

features.name: Quick Set
features.description: Your Pokémon are training in order to quickly set the stage of battle in order to maximize your chances of victory. 3/day you can have one of your Pokémon during their turn use two effect moves as one action if they are both Coat, Hazard, Stance, Terrain, Weather, and/or Zone moves.

features.name: Adaptive Boost
features.description: After Spending time with your Pokémon, you’ve been able to urge more diverse tactical advantages out of the moves they already know. 3/week, after an hour of work with one of your Pokémon, you may permanently alter one of their Pokémon moves to add one of the following effects to the move. - “You get Attack▲.” - “You get Defense▲.” - “You get SpAttack▲.” - “You get SpDefense▲.” - “You get Speed▲.” If a Pokémon has any moves that has already been altered by Adaptive Boost, replace the previously added effect with the new effect.

features.name: Healthy Priorities
features.description: You've worked with your Pokémon to time their healing- precisely at the moment when enemies aren't prepared to stop them. After an hour with one of your Pokémon who has a move that recovers HP, heals a target’s HP, cures afflictions, or grants temporary HP, that move permanently gains Priority. If a Pokémon has any moves that has already been altered by Healthy Priorities, replace the previously added effect with the new effect.

features.name: Hazardous Intent
features.description: Your Pokémon have really seen the advantages you’ve taught them pay off and have begun to ready themselves to set up a field of battle with little to no instruction. After half an hour with one of your Pokémon who has a Coat, Hazard, Stance, Terrain, Weather, and/or Zone move, that move permanently gains Priority for that Pokémon. Moves given Priority this way can be used during a Quick Set simultaneously if both have Priority. If a Pokémon has two moves that have already been altered by Hazardous Intent, replace one of the previously added effects with the new effect.

features.name: Move Recognition
features.description: Your training has influenced how your Pokémon perceive and study battle. Whenever your Pokémon are targeted by an attack that they’ve already been hit with during the same encounter, regardless of the who the attacker was, they have +2 Defense, Special Defense or Speed during the offender’s accuracy check. This effect is doubled if your Pokémon has been hit by the same attack twice during the same encounter. If your Pokémon is hit any further times, Move Recognition does not give higher than a +4 bonus to its relevant defense or speed during accuracy check.

features.name: Terrain Shift
features.description: Your Pokémon have been taught to mold the field of battle physically in order to create blocking, hindering, or difficult terrain. 3/day you may issue a “Terraform” command to have one of your Pokémon with Fountain, Freezer, Groundshaper or Sprouter change the field of battle as that Pokémon’s action. Terraforming Effect Fountain A Pokémon with Fountain can make a pool of water, or make a pool of water larger as its action. The pool of water can be up to 20ft in diameter about 5ft deep, or increase the size of a body of water by 8 contiguous 5x5ft squares, or change 8 contiguous 5x5ft squares of dirt or sand covered terrain into special muddy terrain. Freezer A Pokémon with Freezer can make up to 8 contiguous 5x5ft squares of floor into icy difficult terrain, or create up to 20ft of wall 20ft high of icy blocking terrain with 80 Hit Points and a weakness to Fighting, Fire, Rock and Steel type attacks. Groundshaper A Pokémon with Groundshaper can create tunnel equal to its movement speed big enough for large beings to pass through while moving, or can turn up to 8 contiguous 5x5ft squares of floor into difficult sandy terrain, or create up to 20ft of wall 20ft high of rocky blocking terrain with 80 Hit Points and a weakness to Fighting, Grass, Ground, Steel, and Water type attacks. Sprouter A Pokémon with Sprouter can make up to 8 contiguous 5x5ft squares of floor into brush covered difficult terrain, or 8 contiguous 5x5ft squares of thicket covered hindering terrain, or create up to 20ft of walls 20 ft high of vine blocking terrain with 80 Hit Points and a weakness to Bug, Fire, Flying, Ice, and Poison type attacks.

features.name: Weather Vortex
features.description: You train your Pokémon to manipulate the local climate and mingle effects on the field of battle to create powerful maelstroms that your Pokémon command to their benefit. Whenever your Pokémon uses a Terrain move and it overlaps another Terrain effect on the field of battle, you may choose for the previous terrain effect to remain while the new Terrain effect is also active. The same is true of Weather and Zone Field Conditions. A third instance of Terrain, Weather, or Zone overlapping either areas affected by Weather Vortex will dismiss the other two Terrain, Weather, or Zone effects.

features.name: Malicious Priorities
features.description: Your influence has made your Pokémon more eager to set up your opponent’s Pokémon for failure. After an hour with one of your Pokémon who has an attack that does not deal damage on hit, you may teach that Pokémon the Passive, Prankster. If the Pokémon already has four passives, you must replace one of them with Prankster. Prankster (Your attacks that do not have power dice have Priority.)

features.name: Sleight of Pokémon
features.description: You begin to teach your Pokémon to physically manipulate individuals and not only the ground the battle is on. 1/day, after an hour of work with one of your Pokémon, you can teach them the passives, Magician or Pickpocket; or the move Switcheroo. Each of your Pokémon may only be taught one of these three things with the Slight of Pokémon feature. Magician (When hitting with a melee attack, you steal the target’s held item, if any.) Pickpocket (When you are hit by a melee attack, you steal the offender’s held item, if any.) Switcheroo - 1/day Melee Dark Effect. On hit, you and the target trade any held items. If only one of you has an item, take or give the item and exchange who has possession of the item.

features.name: Brute Strategy
features.description: You teach your Pokémon their final lesson; when all else fails put everything you’ve got into your final attack. 3/day you may choose one of your attacking Pokémon. During their attack, the attack gets +2d20 power, has +5 during AC, and is not resisted if it would be. Then, that Pokémon must Recharge.

name: Tag Battler
flavorText:
Working with two Pokémon in harmony, to outmaneuver 
foes. 
 Tag Battlers keep a split mind whenever possible. By 
attacking with two Pokémon simultaneously, they 
overwhelm foes through coordination and teamwork.

features.name: Sync Move
features.description: Working together comes naturally under your command. 1/day, any two adjacent Pokémon you’ve owned for at least a week can make a Sync Move attack during the faster of the two’s turn. Either Pokémon involved in the Sync Move attack may move in order to arrive at the point of the Sync Move (this doesn’t count as having more than one Pokémon act during the round). Sync Move – 1/day Physical -or- Special Ranged(30ft beam): [Variable] 3d12. [Special] When using Sync Move, chose whether it is a physical or special attack. Sync Move’s attackers apply both Attack or both Special Attack modifiers to Sync Move’s power. Sync Move deals at least 12 damage to any targets it hits. If both partners using Sync Move share a type, Sync Move is one of those types. If neither attacking partner share a type, Sync Move has no type so it cannot be resisted or super-effective. Add the higher relevant attack bonus of the two Pokémon to Sync Move’s AC. Any Pokémon who participates in Sync Move may not take additional turns this round.

features.name: Team Spirit
features.description: Your Pokémon influence each other’s flow on the field of battle, encouraging better performance out of both of them. 3/day you may target two of your active Pokémon as your action. Each of them gets either Attack▲, SpAttack▲, Defense▲, SpDefense▲, or Speed▲ depending on what the other of the two’s highest stat is.

features.name: Brace Allies
features.description: You train your Pokémon to better support allies from being manipulated around the field of battle. If any of your Pokémon are adjacent to any ally who would be moved by a foe’s attack or a feature’s effect, you may have your Pokémon brace that ally and ignore the effects of that ability. This may be used to stop an ally while they are being moved by a foe as well to safely stop them without allowing collisions.

features.name: Helping Out
features.description: You begin teaching Pokémon how to help with an attack without the use of a Sync Move. You may spend an hour with a Pokémon to teach it the move Helping Hand. Helping Hand - 3/day Melee Normal Effect. Target ally’s next attack has advantage. If it deals damage, it gets +2d power.

features.name: Ally Sync
features.description: Your Pokémon begin to really figure out synced attacks and with little preparation, you can improvise an attack with yours and an ally’s Pokémon. With permission from the owner, you may issue a command to your Pokémon and an adjacent ally Pokémon to make a Sync Move attack during the faster of the two’s turn. In addition, you may issue a Sync Move command twice per day, through either your Sync Move or Ally Sync features.

features.name: Combination Tactics
features.description: You spend time studying combination tactics and teach your Pokémon to use them in combat. 1/day, you may spend an hour with one of your Pokémon to teach it the move Assurance, Instruct, or Round. Each of your Pokémon may only be taught one of these three moves with the Combination Tactics feature. Assurance - 3/day Physical Melee: Dark 3d8. Assurance has +1d8 power per SpDefense▼ on the target. Instruct - 3/day Ranged(15ft) Psychic Effect. Targeted ally may immediately act as if they haven’t this round. Round - 3/day Special Ranged(15ft burst): Normal 2d8. If an ally used Round this round, Round gets +1d10 power. Round does not damage allies. Sound.

features.name: Entwining Beam
features.description: You’ve trained your Pokémon to bring forth themselves into the Sync Moves they make. You may choose a type that each participant in a Sync Move has and apply both different types to the Sync Move, applying all weaknesses and resistances to both types during the attack and ignoring any immunities that defenders may have. In addition, you may issue a Sync Move command three times per day, through either your Sync Move or Ally Sync features.

features.name: Impossible Combination
features.description: Your creative strategies become mindbogglingly unstoppable. Whenever one of your Pokémon attacks, while adjacent to another one of your Pokémon who shares no types with the first, the first Pokémon may make an attack while ignoring immunities of any targets, instead treating those immunities as resistances.

features.name: Unity Attack
features.description: You’ve managed to make room for even more in your powerful Sync Move attacks. You can command a third adjacent participant to attack during a Sync Move command all three of them acting during the fastest participant’s turn. If you do, Sync Move has +2d12 power. All three participants must either be your own Pokémon or allied trainer’s Pokémon, but at least one must be your own Pokémon. If using three Pokémon during a Move Sync, you cannot benefit from your Entwining Beam feature. In addition, you may issue a Sync Move command four times per day, through either your Sync Move, Ally Sync, or Unity Attakc features.

features.name: Dual Wielding
features.description: You’ve planned out field tactics and can issue commands like a pro. 3/day you may issue two different commands to two of your active Pokémon. Neither one of those commands can be a Sync Move.

features.name: Friendly Fireproof
features.description: Your Pokémon are in sync with each other’s movements and anticipate each other’s attacks, making way whenever they would other be harmed. Your Pokémon do not take damage from your own Pokémon’s attacks, or any effects. This includes effects from Weather, attacks with an area of effect, or even a misguided Thrash.

features.name: One Heart
features.description: Your Pokémon’s training has unified the energy of each of their beings. The trust they have in each other manifests as an ultimate Sync Move. Whenever you issue a Sync Move command that involves only your Pokémon, the attack is treated as super-effective regardless of the types the Sync Move may be. In addition, you may issue a Sync Move command five times per day, through either your Sync Move, Ally sync, or Unity Attack.

name: Type Ace
flavorText:
An undying love for an element that drives them. 
 Like countless gym leaders, Type Aces have worn a 
favorite type like a badge of honor. Even if it doesn’t make 
up a majority of their team, the Type Ace will drive the 
message into their Pokémon that there is a better way 
and often their Pokémon change for the better.

features.name: Favored Type
features.description: When you become a Type Ace, you will select either Bug, Dark, Dragon, Electric, Fairy, Fighting, Fire, Flying, Ghost, Grass, Ground, Ice, Normal, Poison, Psychic, Rock, Steel, or Water. This is relevant to all of your Type Ace Features that refer to your favored type. Unlike other Advanced Classes, you may take Type Ace more than once when gaining an Advanced Class but you must choose a different Favored Type each time.

features.name: Improved Type Attacks
features.description: Your Pokémon have a shared love of your favorite type and match it with extra power whenever they get to fire off an attack of that type. Your Pokémon you’ve owned for at least one week deal +4 damage with any damaging attack when the attack’s type is your Favored Type.

features.name: Type Resistance
features.description: Your Pokémon have become used to practicing with your favorite type and have learned to let attacks of that type roll off of them, inflicting less damage. Whenever your Pokémon is hit by an attack that is your Favored Type, they take -X damage where X is equal to your Attack or Special Attack modifier.

features.name: Elemental Metamorphosis
features.description: Your bond with the elemental type you love can influence your Pokémon to embrace the type permanently. Once per week, after eight hours of uninterrupted meditation with one of your Pokémon, they will permanently gain your Favored Type and gain move proficiency in your Favored Type. If your Pokémon has only one type, it gains a second type. If your Pokémon has two types, permanently replace one of its types. Your Pokémon’s physical appearance is altered appropriately and may continue to change over the next two weeks to adjust to its new typing. Your Pokémon’s change will only be successful if your Pokémon has at least loyalty 3. Without your influence, a Pokémon who underwent Elemental Metamorphosis will revert to their regular typing in the care of another trainer over time.

features.name: Elemental Grit
features.description: People always think they know exactly how to take you down, but you’re prepared for the worst. 3/day if your Pokémon with your Favored Type is hit by a super-effective or extremely-effective attack, the attack is treated as a resisted attack.

features.name: Type Immunity
features.description: Your Pokémon can shake off what you’ve drilled into them with your encouragement. 3/day when one of your Pokémon who you’ve owned for at least one week are hit by an attack that is your Favored Type, you can make your Pokémon take no damage from the attack as a free action. Any other effects of the attack may be ignored.

features.name: Type Loyalty
features.description: By spending more time around similar Pokémon, you increase how comfortable your Pokémon feel in your care. If at least four Pokémon in your team share your favored type, your team’s interactions with each other are never hostile. In addition, your team’s loyalty is easier to improve, your interaction with your Pokémon more often ends with positive results, and it takes intentional and malicious mistreatment to lower your Pokémon's loyalty.

features.name: Resistance Piercing
features.description: Your training has empowered your Pokémon’s attacks to break through your foe’s natural resistances. 3/day when your Pokémon hits with an attack with the same type as your favored type, the attack ignores any resistances or immunities. (If a Pokémon is benefiting from the Ace Trainer feature: Type Immunity, your Pokémon’s attack is treated as resisted in this case.)

features.name: Bread and Butter
features.description: You begin to teach your Pokémon how to use a unique move that you’ve developed in your training. Once per week after training with one of your Pokémon who shares a type with your favored type for three hours, you teach them one of the following attacks. [Type] Smasher – 3/day Physical Melee: [Variable] 3d10. You get Attack▲. [Type] Flash - 3/day Special Ranged(30ft): [Variable] 3d10. You get SpAttack▲. In the move names for Type Smasher and Type Flash, replace the word “Type” with your favored type. Type Smasher and Type Flash’s type are your favored type.

features.name: Move Molding
features.description: You begin to apply your special move’s theorem to other attacks your Pokémon knows. 3/week after training with one of your Pokémon who shares a type with your favored type for three hours, you may permanently change the type of one of that Pokémon’s moves to your Favored Type.

features.name: Type Embrace
features.description: When your Pokémon are hit by a familiar attack, they accept it like a warm hug. 3/day when one of your Pokémon that you’ve owned for at least one week are hit by an attack that is your Favored Type, they take no damage and ignore any other effects of the attack, then are healed hit points equal to the amount of damage they would have taken.

features.name: Elemental Surge
features.description: Your masterful training has perfected the essence of your elemental affinity and you can push Pokémon to unleash their inner strength to defeat any foe. 3/day when a Pokémon who shares a type with your Favored Type hits with an attack that matches your Favored Type, the attack is treated as extremely effective.

name: Underdog
flavorText:
Size is not everything, ever.
 Underdogs can see the potential in their Pokémon and 
bring it out of them while maintaining the Pokémon's 
nimbleness and most importantly, their cute looks. 
Underdogs don’t forbid their Pokémon from evolving, but 
their encouragement can convince a Pokémon that 
change isn’t needed to prove their worth.

features.name: Eversoul
features.description: Through will alone, your Pokémon are able to ward off the lure of evolution. While straining to resist evolution is something that any Pokémon is capable of, your Pokémon never feel exhausted while doing so, instead it is as if they are always holding an Everstone. Your Pokémon are considered Underdog Pokémon for class features if they’ve been your Pokémon for at least one week and are in one of the three following categories: - Has never evolved, can still evolve. (Bulbasaur, Taillow, Nincada, etc.) - Can still evolve, even if it has evolved. (Ivysaur, Pikachu, Duosion, etc.) - Cannot evolve, but never evolved. (Kangaskhan, Torkoal, Maractus, etc.)

features.name: Hidden Strength
features.description: Your training brings out the best of your enthusiastic Pokémon. 3/day you can issue an attack command to use a Move that your Pokémon’s knows naturally upon evolution. The move may come from your Pokémon’s next evolution, or its final evolution. Even though they may temporarily use the move, your Pokémon must still follow the move’s frequency limits.

features.name: The Bigger They Are
features.description: Your guidance has instilled a confidence in your Pokémon, they never feel outmatched. Whenever your Underdog Pokémon hits an evolved Pokémon or a Pokémon that is at least two sizes larger with an attack that deals damage, it deals an additional 4 damage.

features.name: Versatile Technique
features.description: Your Pokémon feel their potential within themselves. When attacking, your Underdog Pokémon benefit from the same-type attack bonus as if they were any of the types of their potential evolved forms, even if they have branch evolutions. (STAB is always +4 damage)

features.name: Passive Improvement
features.description: Your Pokémon begin to mature in ways that are unique to their evolutionary stage. Pokémon that you’ve owned for at least one week may have up to six passives and may immediately gain passives from any of their possible evolutions. In addition, those Pokémon can use the skills of any of their evolved forms (You may need to get creative with your narratives, for example, if your Pokémon lacks wings but gains Flight with this feature, maybe they flap their arms really hard or only do controlled jumps and falling instead of true flight).

features.name: Champ in the Making
features.description: Your intensive training has improved the general being of your underdog Pokémon. 3/day as an action choose one of your Underdog Pokémon that has not been targeted by this feature today gains 12 temporary HP.

features.name: Young Luck
features.description: Your intuition in battle has given your underdogs a great deal of confidence, at times they feel as if everything is in their favor. 3/day when one of your Underdog Pokémon misses an attack against an evolved Pokémon, you may reroll the accuracy check.

features.name: Perfect as Is
features.description: Your intensive training has improved the general being of your underdog Pokémon. Any of your Underdog Pokémon that you’ve had for at least a week have their Attack, Special Attack, and Speed permanently raised by 2; and their Defense and Special Defense raised by 1.

features.name: Underdog Tactics
features.description: After some studying and planning, you begin tutoring your team to employ tactics to edge out victories in tight spots. After an hour with one of your Pokémon, you can teach them one of the moves, Endeavor, Endure, Flail, Laser Focus, Lock-On, or Quick Attack. Each of your Pokémon may only be taught one of these moves with the Underdog Tactics feature. Endeavor - 3/day Physical Melee: Normal. On hit, if the target has more HP than you, the target’s HP is set to equal your HP. Endure - 1/day Self Normal Effect. Reaction [When you are hit by an attack that would knock you out]. You are instead left with 1 HP. Flail - 1/day Physical Melee: Normal 1d . If you are at less than half of your Max HP, Flail has +2d power. If you are at less than 5 HP, Flail has +4d power instead. Laser Focus - 1/day Ranged(30ft) Normal Effect. Your next attack against the same target will be a Critical Hit if it hits. Lock-On - 1/day Ranged(40ft) Normal Effect. Your next attack against the same target cannot miss. Quick Attack - At-Will Physical Melee: Normal 2d4. Quick Attack has Priority.

features.name: Superior Defiance
features.description: Your Pokémon outwardly deny expectations and fight against those that others might think have the upper hand. 3/day when one of your Underdog Pokémon are hit by an attack by a fully evolved Pokémon, that Underdog Pokémon gets Attack▲▲ or SpAttack▲▲.

features.name: Rising Up
features.description: The stronger an opponent is, the more your Pokémon can rise up to meet their foes. 3/day, as an action, you may choose one stat and a foe’s evolved Pokémon. One of your Underdog Pokémon’s stat is changed to equal that foe’s evolved Pokémon’s stat if it is higher than your Pokémon’s stat until the end of combat.

features.name: Underdog Comeback
features.description: Your Pokémon have grown to dominate the field of battle and can overcome anything with your inspiring leadership. 1/day, when one of your Underdog Pokémon are knocked out, instead they recover to half of their max HP.

name: Breeder
flavorText:
Guidance, Family, Love
 Raising a Pokémon from birth and imbuing them with 
your care and nurturing is powerfully rewarding. Many 
Breeders spend hours caring for eggs and then the 
Pokémon who hatches from it. They teach it everything it 
needs to know and more in ways that other trainers might 
fall short while encouraging its growth and maturity. 
Breeders who take more care into their work might find 
themselves inventing things to teach their Pokémon, 
taking a special interest in their medical care, or even by 
revealing extremely powerful bonds through new 
evolutions.

features.name: Hatcher
features.description: Your loving care of the eggs you receive brings out your new Pokémon with particular haste. Your eggs in your care never take longer than 72 hours to hatch.

features.name: Natural Edge
features.description: Your Pokémon are born with a natural lead on other trainer’s Pokémon, your caring watch has given them a reason to be more, for you. Whenever you hatch an egg, after you know the Pokémon’s nature, choose one of Attack, Defense, Special Attack, Special Defense, or Speed. That Pokémon’s chosen stat is permanently raised X, where X is half of either your Defense or Special Defense modifier.

features.name: Philoprogenitive
features.description: You put your Pokémon children before yourself. Whenever one of your hatched Pokémon is targeted with an attack and hit, if they are within 10ft of you, you may move to your Pokémon and take the damage and effects they would have taken for them as a free action. You may use this feature as many times as you would like within the same round, regardless of turn order and regardless of whether or not you have already acted.

features.name: Stat Increase and Advanced Class
features.description: Choose two different Trainer Stats to increase by 1, then gain 1d4 max HP. You only gain new stats at levels 3, 7, and 11. Choose a Breeder Advanced Class or a different base Class. You can only ever gain a single Class or Advanced Class at a time, when leveling up.

features.name: Rudimentary Tutoring
features.description: There are some pretty basic things you understand about young Pokémon and can teach your Pokémon to use what they got to shine from a young age. 1/day, after spending one hour working with one of your hatched Pokémon, you may teach one of the following moves. Moves taught with the Rudimentary Tutoring feature must still fit the Pokémon’s proficiencies. For each move, choose Physical or Special, then Melee or Ranged(10ft), when tutoring to determine damage type and range. Air Dart - At-Will [Variable] [Variable]: Flying 2d6. Bug Lash - At-Will [Variable] [Variable]: Bug 2d6. Clay Slap - At-Will [Variable] [Variable]: Ground 2d6. Drake Gale - At-Will [Variable] [Variable]: Dragon 2d6. Flicker Flame - At-Will [Variable] [Variable]: Fire 2d6. Frosty Wind - At-Will [Variable] [Variable]: Ice 2d6. Glimmer - At-Will [Variable] [Variable]: Fairy 2d6. Iron Chop - At-Will [Variable] [Variable]: Steel 2d6. Low Blow - At-Will [Variable] [Variable]: Dark 2d6. Mind Push - At-Will [Variable] [Variable]: Psychic 2d6. Nox Spray - At-Will [Variable] [Variable]: Poison 2d6. Seed Toss - At-Will [Variable] [Variable]: Grass 2d6. Slap Chop - At-Will [Variable] [Variable]: Fighting 2d6. Smack - At-Will [Variable] [Variable]: Normal 2d6. Spook - At-Will [Variable] [Variable]: Ghost 2d6. Stone Shot - At-Will [Variable] [Variable]: Rock 2d6. Thunder Jolt - At-Will [Variable] [Variable]: Electric 2d6. Water Spray - At-Will [Variable] [Variable]: Water 2d6.

features.name: Unexpected Hatch
features.description: Your eggs begin to hatch across species!? Whenever you hatch an egg that you found after making an Breeding Check, you may flip a coin. If you win the flip, you may choose to have the egg hatch as a Pokémon of the father’s species instead of the default mother’s species. Additionally, whenever you hatch your eggs, choose any one move from either parent and give it to your baby Pokémon.

features.name: Natural Breeder
features.description: You’ve learned just how to influence your baby Pokémon’s first moments of life. When you hatch an egg, you may choose which of Attack, Defense, Special Attack, Special Defense, or Speed is positively or negatively influenced by nature. The nature is still randomized, but will be a nature that matches your preference when using Natural Breeder. In addition, if you don’t choose to influence the Pokémon’s nature you can pick its sex.

features.name: Stat Increase and Advanced Class
features.description: Choose two different Trainer Stats to increase by 1, then gain 1d4 max HP. You only gain new stats at levels 3, 7, and 11. Choose a Breeder Advanced Class or a different base Class. You can only ever gain a single Class or Advanced Class at a time, when leveling up.

features.name: Parental Hyperlexia
features.description: You begin to pick on the slightest hints, differences in tone, and micro expressions from your Pokémon as if they are speaking to you in a human language. You can understand any Pokémon that you hatched with a loyalty of 3 or higher, when it tries to speak to you in its own Pokémon languages. If the Pokémon’s unable to speak to you in a comprehensible sense, you still understand it’s general needs and you still understand anything it might be trying to communicate to you.

features.name: Viviparity
features.description: No egg, no mess, just a new baby family member. 3/week after succeeding a Breeding Check, your Pokémon produce an already-hatched baby Pokémon. Despite already being hatched, it still benefits from all of your features that mention hatched Pokémon.

features.name: Prolific Parents
features.description: Pokémon parents grow stronger alongside their children, gaining new strength and wisdom as the next generation learns and evolves. For each of your Pokémon who have produced at least three offspring while in your care, choose one of Attack, Defense, Special Attack, Special Defense, or Speed. That Pokémon’s chosen stat is permanently raised X, where X is half of either your Defense or Special Defense modifier. Additionally, your Pokémon who have produced at least three offspring while in your care may (once per Pokémon) learn a move from one of their mates that they do not know after 1 hour of training.

features.name: Stat Increase and Advanced Class
features.description: Choose two different Trainer Stats to increase by 1, then gain 1d4 max HP. You only gain new stats at levels 3, 7, and 11. Choose a Breeder Advanced Class or a different base Class. You can only ever gain a single Class or Advanced Class at a time, when leveling up.

features.name: Unlikely Pairings
features.description: The mysterious ways that Pokémon create eggs are still unclear to you, but you’ve figured out a way to coerce eggs from Pokémon that otherwise would never make an egg. When trying to have Pokémon make Pokémon eggs in privacy, they do not need to have a matching egg group.

features.name: Familial Bond
features.description: Your Pokémon treat you as if you were their actual parent. Any Pokémon you’ve hatched starts at loyalty 3 with you. It takes intentional and malicious mistreatment to lower these Pokémon’s loyalties. In addition, any Pokémon you obtain are quick to warm up to you and not treat you as a hostile, in no more than one week any Pokémon you obtain reach loyalty 3. Additionally, any of your Pokémon that you’ve had for at least a week can benefit from your features Natural Edge, Philoprogenitive, Rudimentary Tutoring, and Parental Hyperlexia as if it hatched under your care.

features.name: Gleaming Eggs
features.description: Your warm influence brings out a rare quality on occasion from your baby Pokémon. Whenever you hatch one of your eggs, roll 1d20 and add your Defense or Special Defense modifier. On 20 or higher, the Pokémon that hatches is shiny.

features.name: Matchmaker
features.description: You’ve become a master Breeder and can guarantee the Pokémon eggs that you desire. 1/day, when you make an Breeding Check for two Pokémon, of which at least one of the two is your Pokémon, you are guaranteed to find an egg (or baby Pokémon with your Vivipartiy feature). When the egg hatches, you pick which species of the two parents the Pokémon is, which sex the Pokémon has, and which nature the Pokémon has.

name: Botanist
flavorText:
Raising life is not limited to raising Pokémon.
 Through similar special care and attention, the Botanist 
raising various miniature plants in order to provide 
another avenue of kindness in the Pokémon world.

features.name: Berry Mixer
features.description: When it comes to berry treats, you’re an expert. Whenever you’re making any kind of food or item that requires berries, you are considered a certified expert and can supply your wares to specialty stores (usually at half their value), or to strangers willing to pay for your expertise.

features.name: Botanical Encyclopedia
features.description: You’ve memorized every book there is on botany in the Pokémon world. You can instantly identify any berries, plants, or fungi and know any of their special properties. You also can tell if any of them have been modified to have unique attributes. In addition, you can identify any Grass-type Pokémon on sight, or any Pokémon known to work with, or that pretends to be, flora.

features.name: Berry Finder
features.description: You apply your encyclopedic knowledge to the field and know where to best find berries. Whenever you make any skill checks related to berries, or finding them randomly, you may roll twice and use the better result. Additionally, you may attempt to find the following common berries specifically when you make your skill check. If you do, only roll once on your skill check. If you succeed, you find one of the follow berries of your choice: Oran Aspear Cheri Chesto Pecha Persim Rawst Belue Bluk Cornn Durin Magost Nanab Nomel Pamtre Pinap Rabuta Razz Spelon Watmel Wepear

features.name: Berry Booster
features.description: Your care for your plants is evident by the particular energy they release when consumed. Whenever a Pokémon consumes berries that you’ve grown, double any numerical effect the berry might have.

features.name: Growth Spurt
features.description: You’ve started to apply a special fertilizer to your plants, promising quick results. Whenever you plant berries, including in a portable planter, it will never take more than 48 hours for the plant to produce fruit. In addition, if you roll under 6 while making Nature checks while caring for Berry plants, treat the roll as a 6.

features.name: Berry Juicing
features.description: You apply your knowledge of berries to make potable drinks for trainers. 3/day you can destroy a berry to create a juice that has the same effect as the berry, but is usable by humans. Call the drink whatever you’d like. The drink loses any abilities after one week.

features.name: Berry Combination
features.description: You begin to practice with the qualities of berries by extracting and injecting different berries together. 1/day, after spending an hour with two of your berries, you destroy one and give its flavor and effects to the other berry to create one berry with the effects of both. Call the combination whatever you’d like. You may not combine a berry with an already combined berry.

features.name: Hybridization
features.description: You begin to apply your studies to a berry plant itself. Whenever you plant a berry, you can plant two berries together to produce a tree that grows berries with the flavors and effects of both of the planted berries. This includes berries you may plant in a portable planter. Call the resulting combination whatever you’d like. You may not hybridize a berry with an already hybridized or combined berry.

features.name: Fruit Seeker
features.description: You find unusual signs of rarer berries and apricorns by exploring the space around you to find those unusual and lesser seen fruits. Whenever you make any skill checks related finding berries, you may attempt to find an uncommon berry or apricorn. If you do, only roll once on your skill check. If you succeed, you find one of the follow berries of your choice: Pomeg Kelpsy Qualot Hondew Grepa Tamato Occa Passho Wacan Rindo Yache Chople Kebia Shuca Coba Payapa Tanga Charti Kasib Haban Colbur Babiri Chilan Roseli Sitrus Lum Aguav Figy Iapapa Mago Wiki Blue Green Pink Black Red Orange White

features.name: Miniature Specimen
features.description: You apply a theory towards creating smaller, but still just as effective berry plants. You can grow two plants in a portable planter at the same time, and the berries these plants produce are small enough to fit in the palm of your hand. Berries produced with the miniature specimen feature cannot be stolen from any Pokémon who is holding onto one during battle.

features.name: Rare Berry Seeker
features.description: You may apply your vast knowledge base to explore wild space and locate treasures in the berry collecting world. Whenever you make any skill checks related finding berries, you may attempt to find a rare berry. If you do, only roll once on your skill check. If you succeed, you find one of the follow berries of your choice: Liechi Ganlon Salac Petaya Apicot Lansat Starf Enigma Micle Custap Joboca Rowap Kee Maranga Leppa

features.name: Berry Monstrosities
features.description: You’ve mastered the hybridizations and combination of natural berries and put it to unbelievable use and execution. When using your Berry Combination or Hybridization features, the berries you make can have a total of five different qualities from different berries. This will combine all flavors and all effects. If you combine or hybridize a sixth berries into your monstrosities, chose another berry’s flavor and effects to replace in said monstrosity. Call the combination whatever you’d like.

name: Chef
flavorText:
You’ve never eaten anything better. 
 The Chef is so giving to those they travel with. Your 
friends and family of Pokémon eat like kings and are 
always happy to smell what you’re cooking up next.

features.name: Energy Shot
features.description: You’ve concocted a drink that really gives you an adrenaline rush, it could be useful out there in the wilds. 1/day, after one hour of work in on it, you create one pint of an energy drink for trainers. Call it whatever you’d like. You have enough for four servings of the drink. When one serving is consumed, it gives a trainer temporary hit points equal the sum of your Defense and Special Defense stat. The drink’s effect wears off after an hour. Drinking multiple servings will remove any temporary hit points gained by the drink. The drink’s potency wears off after 24 hours and then becomes a regular drink.

features.name: Soul Food
features.description: You’re a great chef and have loads of experience whipping up meals. When looking for edible food in the wild, you can add your Defense or Special defense modifiers while making skill checks. It takes you less than 20 mins to create a soulful meal out of any edible ingredients for ten people and/or Pokémon. Whenever a Pokémon consumes a soulful meal within an hour of its creation, they are relaxed unless they are agitated again (it takes at least 5 mins to consume a meal). Your Pokémon quickly gain loyalty to you if you’re feeding them often and are very unlikely to lose loyalty unless there’s any intentional mistreatment.

features.name: Wild Bait
features.description: You can create powerful aromas that attract various wilds to a place of your choosing. After 30 mins of work, you create a dish of wild bait. The bait has a powerful smell that will lure wild Pokémon to its location once you ready it. If you and your party are not sufficiently hidden, wilds may approach but then flee if any wilds detect you or your party.

features.name: Sugar Rush
features.description: You can produce treats that energize your Pokémon like nothing else. 1/day, after thirty minutes of working on it, you create one serving of a sugary energy drink for Pokémon. Call it whatever you’d like. When it is consumed, it gives a Pokémon temporary hit points equal the sum of your Defense and Special Defense stat. The drink’s effect wears off after an hour. Drinking multiple servings will remove any temporary hit points gained by the drink. The drink’s potency wears off after 72 hours and then becomes a regular drink.

features.name: Pâtissier
features.description: You begin practicing the arts of desserts and can spend time to create delicious replicas of famous treats. 1/day, after 30 mins of work you can create two of any of the following treats. Unlike real versions of these treats, your food made with the Pâtissier feature do not have their effects after 48 hours, instead only tasting delicious. Treats that heal 10 HP (Pokémon) when eaten: Big Malasada Casteliacone Lava Cookie Rage Candy Bar Sweet Heart Canari Bread Treats that cure any affliction when eaten: Berry Juice Lumiose Galette Old Gateau Pewter Crunchies Shalour Sable

features.name: Herbal Medicine
features.description: You improve several qualities of the treats you can make, but less people would call them treats now. 1/day, after 10 mins of work you can create one of the following medicines. Your Pokémon are not repulsed by your Herbal Medicine, but another trainer’s Pokémon or wild Pokémon will be disgusted. Heal Powder Removes any affliction Energy Powder Recovers 25 HP (Pokémon)

features.name: Vile Cook
features.description: You figure out how to creates food that hide undesirable effects underneath delicious disguises. Whenever you make food, or an edible item, you may make the food Poison the consumer, Paralyze the consumer or make the consumer Drowsy. The tampered food loses its potency after one hour and becomes regular edible food.

features.name: Palette Pleaser
features.description: You’ve mastered flavor in every form. Whenever you make a meal, or mix any ingredients to make a food item with any effects, you make it in a way that is pleasing to anyone or any Pokémon who consumes it regardless of their nature, preferred flavors, or disliked flavors. You may also change the flavors of any food you create to affect Contest Stats differently.

features.name: Power Recovery
features.description: Your soul food becomes invigorating and empowers your Pokémon to unleash powerful attacks as if they’ve rested for hours. Pokémon who have eaten your Soul Food may again use their 3/day or 1/day moves as if they have rested for 8 hours. Pokémon may not benefit from the Power Recovery feature multiple times per day.

features.name: Powerful Herbs
features.description: You’ve strengthened your foul-smelling recipes. 1/day, after one hour of work you can create one of the following medicines. Your Pokémon are not repulsed by your Powerful Herbs, but another trainer’s Pokémon or wild Pokémon will be disgusted. Energy Root Recovers 50 Hit Points (Pokémon) Revival Herb Recovers an unconscious Pokémon to half of their max HP.

features.name: Leftovers
features.description: Through your practice, you discovered a way to create a meal that continues to heal a Pokémon after it’s consumed. 1/day, after working for one hour you create a serving of Leftovers. Leftovers - As an action, consume and destroy Leftovers. Regain 1d6 HP after acting until you are at max HP.

features.name: Signature Dish
features.description: You’ve proven yourself to be an unmatched chef. You can spend four hours designing a unique Signature Dish. You can name the dish whatever you like and keep a list of up to five Signature Dishes (if you create a sixth, remove one of your other five from your list). 1/day you can spend one hour making one of your Signature Dishes. Your Signature Dishes can be made of anything and will have any two effects of your choice, either from something that you’ve made before, anything you’ve consumed, or anything one of your Pokémon consumed. The dish can affect either Pokémon or humans. Additionally, all of your dishes retain their potency indefinitely.

name: Evolver
flavorText:
Mega evolution reveals a powerful bond with your 
Pokémon.
 Evolvers create highly sought after mega stones 
exclusively for their Pokémon. By empowering your 
Pokémon, you give them an additional edge in battle, as if 
your guidance wasn’t enough of an edge.

features.name: Early Evolution
features.description: Every Pokémon has different triggers that encourage evolution and you’ve learned to nurture these different influences and induce evolution. Your Pokémon are unhindered by any natural timing to evolve and can evolve regardless of day or night time constraints. Your Pokémon whose evolutions that require environmental influences may evolve anywhere. Pokémon who need to evolve based solely on loyalty or their relationship with you evolve much faster, even if they are barely a week old. In addition, in rare occasions, your Pokémon may evolve twice rapidly into its final evolution if given the opportunity.

features.name: Mega Stone Smith
features.description: After studying mega stones, you’ve figured out how to imbue simple marbles with the mysterious spirit that enables Pokémon to mega evolve. Once per week, after six hours of work, you create a Keystone exclusively for your use or you create a Mega Stone exclusively for one of your fully-evolved Pokémon. When creating a Mega Stone, decide which stats are boosted while the Pokémon is using the created Mega Stone. You can modify Attack, Defense, Special Attack, Special Defense, or Speed by a total of 4 points, but no individual stat can be modified by more than 2. You may not affect any stats negatively. You choose how your Pokémon’s physical appearance changes appropriately. ***Special*** Mega Evolution is done 1/day by activating your Keystone with one of your Pokémon who has a Mega Stone. It lasts for 10 minutes.

features.name: Elemental Evolution
features.description: Working with some theories about the effects of elemental stones on Pokémon, you’ve figured out how to induce elemental evolution. 1/day, you may spend one hour with a Pokémon who can evolve with the use of any evolution stone and they will evolve at the end of that hour. In addition, you’ve figured out how to repress evolution in a Pokémon and after spending one hour with one of your Pokémon, you can abate evolution for 48 hours without the use of an Everstone.

features.name: Evolution Guidance
features.description: Your training and care helps to mold your Pokémon’s futures and helps their paths of evolution. If your Pokémon has a branched evolution, when it evolves you may choose what it evolves into regardless of any other factors in its evolution. The Evolution Guidance feature overrides requirements during evolutions such as gendered evolutions (Gallade, Vespiquen), evolutions that differ based on time of day (Cascoon, Lycanroc), environment influenced evolutions (Wormadam S, Weezing A), stone evolutions (Bellossom, Vaporeon), or stat based evolutions (Hitmonchan, Gorebyss). This means you could have a male Nidorina, a night time Silcoon, a Fairy type Rapidash from a Fire type Ponyta, a Glaceon from a Moon Stone, or any other unusual evolution. In the Pokédex, familial species that are connected by Evolution Guidance will have this icon.

features.name: Keystone Burst
features.description: Keystones usually need time to regain their ambient energy after use, however you’ve trained your Pokémon to only dip into the Key Stone’s power with their Mega Stones instead of draining it completely. Your Keystone may be used twice per day or three times per day if you only Mega Evolve the same Pokémon each time. You may still only have one Mega Pokémon at a time.

features.name: Mega Stone Shift
features.description: Spending some time with your Mega Stones can give you some insight to their magical properties; with a little bit of focus you can change how your Mega Stones change your Pokémon. After two hours of work, one of your unique Mega Stones will alter your Pokémon’s types by replacing one type or by adding one type while the Pokémon is Mega Evolved. You choose how your Pokémon’s physical appearance changes appropriately.

features.name: Key Stone Stretch
features.description: Keystones ring while your Pokémon are Mega Evolved, but you’ve learned to quell that into a hum, prolonging a Mega Evolution’s stay. Your Pokémon’s Mega Evolutions can retain their form for up to one hour, even if returned to their Poke Ball. This effect ends if they are knocked out.

features.name: Peak Form
features.description: Raising your Pokémon through their evolutions and keeping them in top shape has increased their performance. When one of your Pokémon evolves into its final stage of evolution, choose two of Attack, Defense, Special Attack, Special Defense, or Speed and permanently add 1 to that Pokémon’s stats. Additionally, for any of your fully-evolved Pokémon that you’ve owned for at least one week who haven’t benefited from Peak Form yet, choose two of Attack, Defense, Special Attack, Special Defense, or Speed and permanently add 1 to that Pokémon’s stats.

features.name: Keystone Overflow
features.description: Your Pokémon have grown to use the flow of energy from the Key Stone and can even borrow its energy from each other when standing together in battle! You may have two Mega Pokémon at the same time.

features.name: Potential Break
features.description: Mega Stones bring Pokémon to unreal levels of power, but to most you need to already be strong to use a Mega Stone with your Key Stone. However, you’ve figured out a way to induce Mega Evolution with unreal results. If you own a Mega Stone that corresponds to a Mega Evolution that appears in the Pokédex, your not-fully-evolved Pokémon that will eventually be fully compatible with a Mega Stone may already use the Mega Stone. For example, if you own Blazikenite or have created a Mega Stone to Mega Evolve Blaziken, your Torchic or Combusken could use it to turn into Mega Blaziken.

features.name: Evolution Shift
features.description: Pokémon have their previous selves, potential selves, and sometimes impossible selves within and you’ve developed a way to manipulate and work with your Pokémon to bring out any hidden part. 1/day, after working for five hours with one of your Pokémon you may return it to its previous stage of evolution or change its evolution to another in its branch of evolutions. You could for example change your Rapidash into a Rapidash (Forest Glade), your Purrserker into a Persian, or your Poliwrath into a Politoed. Evolution Shift removes any benefits given to your Pokémon by Peak Form if they are unevolved during Evolution Shift until that Pokémon evolves again. In the Pokédex, familial species that are connected by Evolution Shift will have this icon with information on the potential branch evolutions available.

features.name: Keystone Kaleidoscope
features.description: Evolution is different for every Pokémon and can continue to change and create new surprises for everyone. Whenever you Mega Evolve a Pokémon, you may choose which of its stats are modified by its Mega Stone and which types it becomes (you may choose different stats and types each time). You must still follow the Mega Stone rules of the features Mega Stone Smith and Mega Stone Shift while Mega Evolving your Pokémon.

name: Medic
flavorText:
Medical precision on the field of battle.
 Not content to wait for the next visit to a Pokémon 
center, Medics study human and Pokémon anatomy to 
save lives or just keep someone around in battle.

features.name: Muscle Relaxants
features.description: While they may only help without cure sometimes, your careful application of injected relaxants is a sure fix for any paralyzed ally. 3/day you may use your medical field kit as an action to cure any adjacent trainer or Pokémon of Paralysis.

features.name: Treat Minor Wound
features.description: Your study of medicine has led to more effective use of your kit to heal the broken, damaged, and hurt. 3/day you may use your medical field kit as an action to heal any adjacent trainer or Pokémon 10 hit points, then give them 5 temporary hit points. In addition, you may not use your Medic features on unwilling, conscious targets. (A Pokémon who is healed this way cannot use a Move during the same round)

features.name: Medicinal Expert
features.description: Your training and practice has led you to some improved procedures that help will your friends in a pinch. Whenever you use a restorative item such as an Antidote or Potion, or a Medic feature on an allied trainer or Pokémon, heal the target additional hit points equal to your Defense or Special Defense modifier.

features.name: Better Living Through Medicine
features.description: Careful study and repetition has given your hands the precision and skill to move rapidly and help those in need. During your turn, you may use two Medic features on adjacent targets during the same turn as one action. You still deplete your uses per day on any of your Medic features used.

features.name: Treat Wound
features.description: Your continuous practice of medicine has led to more effective use of your kit to heal the injured. 3/ day you may use your medical field kit as an action to heal any adjacent trainer or Pokémon 20 hit points, then give them 10 temporary hit points which last for 10 mins. (A Pokémon who is healed this way cannot use a Move during the same round)

features.name: Affliction Therapy
features.description: After modifying the available drugs and micro defibrillator in your kit, you’ve created treatments to help friends in a tight spot. 3/day you may use your medical field kit as an action to cure any adjacent trainer or Pokémon of Burns, Poisoned, Toxified, Drowsy, or Frostbite. (A Pokémon who is healed this way cannot use a Move during the same round)

features.name: Battle Medicine
features.description: While collecting herbs and studying your medicines, you’ve figured out how to replicate powerful herbs used in Pokémon battles. 1/day you may spend 1 hour making a Mental Herb, Mirror Herb, Power Herb, or White Herb. These items made by you lose their potency after 1 week and become useless. Mental Herb - As a free action, consume and destroy Mental Herb. If a foe does anything to try and prevent you from using any of your moves, it fails. Mirror Herb - As a free Reaction [When a foe gets ▲], consume and destroy Mental Herb. Gain the same ▲ that the foe just gained. Power Herb - As a free Reaction [When you use a move with multiple turns], consume and destroy Power Herb. Skip the first turn of the move and immediately do the second turn of the move. White Herb - As a free action, consume and destroy White Herb. Get rid of any ▼ that you have.

features.name: Restore Strength
features.description: By using a combination of energy recovering drugs and adrenaline, you’ve given your Pokémon a chance at pushing out more power in a tight spot. 3/day you may use your medical field kit as an action to restore an adjacent Pokémon’s use of 1/day or 3/day frequency moves as if they have rested for 8 hours. (A Pokémon who is healed this way cannot use a Move during the same round)

features.name: Treat Major Wound
features.description: Your expertise of medicine has led to efficient use of your kit to repair the injured. 3/day you may use your medical field kit as an action to heal any adjacent trainer or Pokémon 30 hit points, then give them 15 temporary hit points which last for 10 mins. (A Pokémon who is healed this way cannot use a Move during the same round)

features.name: Do No Harm
features.description: Your fervor in battle and willingness to risk your life while protecting others burns brightly as you save lives around you every day. On any turn where you haven’t attacked any targets and have not issued any attack commands to any of your Pokémon, your Treat Minor Wound, Treat Wound, Treat Major Wound and Treat Serious Wound features heal an additional 10 hit points, but grant 10 less temporary hit points. You may not issue attack commands to any Pokémon after benefiting from the Do No Harm feature.

features.name: Treat Serious Wound
features.description: Your mastery of medicine has led to perfect use of your kit to completely heal the injured. 3/ day you may use your medical field as an action kit to heal any adjacent trainer or Pokémon 40 hit points, then give them 20 temporary hit points which last for 10 mins. (A Pokémon who is healed this way cannot use a Move during the same round)

features.name: Won’t Die on Me
features.description: The lives of others are not expendable and your watch guarantees their survival. 1/day, if an adjacent ally fails their final death saving throw, they instead succeed the death saving throw and are set to 1 hit point, then regain consciousness.

name: Move Tutor
flavorText:
More options than thought possible during battle.
 While your Pokémon might not hit harder than another 
trainer’s, your Pokémon have many more diverse options 
in battle. Move Tutors observe a Pokémon and bring out 
the most unusual abilities from where you’d least expect 
it.

features.name: Natural Tutoring
features.description: For a tutor, reteaching Pokémon how to do something they used to do before is a trivial exercise. 1/day, after spending one hour working with one of your Pokémon, you may teach a move to that Pokémon that they’ve known but have since removed from their move list as long as the Pokémon is proficient in its use.

features.name: Practical Application
features.description: Your work and your efforts result in your Pokémon not only learning new tricks, but knowing how to use them effectively. 3/day, as a free action, when one of your Pokémon uses a move that you tutored, it has advantage during AC.

features.name: Passive Tutoring
features.description: By studying some basic field tactics you’ve learned how to teach Pokémon how to improve their odds on the field of battle. 1/day, after spending two hours working with one of your Pokémon, you may teach one of the following passives to that Pokémon. The added Passive must still follow the Passive limit of 4. Power Up (+1 Attack) Thick Hide (+1 Defense) Focused (+1 Special Attack) Vigilant (+1 Special Defense) Nimble (+1 Speed)

features.name: Move Improved
features.description: A tutor’s truest skill is inventing new moves for their Pokémon to use. 1/day, after spending three hours working with one of your Pokémon, add one of the following effects to a move they have. Your Pokémon cannot have more than two moves modified by Move Improved or Move Evolution and each move that you modify can only have one change. If you change a move that’s already been modified, replace the last effect you gave with Move Improved or Move Evolution. - On hit, push the target 10ft away. If it collides, it loses 1d4 HP. - On hit, pull the target 10ft towards you. If you bring the target adjacent to you, it loses 1d4 HP. - On hit, you have +2 during AC during your next turn. - (Melee Range Only) On hit, move 10ft after rolling damage. - (Melee Range Only) On hit, any attacks made against you and the target have advantage until your next turn. - (Melee Range Only) Bind the target to you until your next turn. They may pass an Attack skill check of 12 to move away. - (Melee Range Only) On hit, any ranged attacks made against you by anything other than this attack’s target has -2 during AC. - (Single-target Ranged Only) On hit, 13 or higher during AC increases this attack’s area of effect to (5ft blast). - (Single-target Ranged Only) On hit, for the remainder of combat this attack has x3 range if you didn’t move that round. - (Single-target attack Only) On hit, the space underneath the target becomes difficult terrain.

features.name: Machine Mentor
features.description: By studying the effects of Technical Machines and Technical Records, you’ve learned to replicate their techniques in training. 1/day, after spending six hours working with one of your Pokémon, you may teach that Pokémon any move you’ve previously taught with a Technical Machine or Technical Record. Moves taught with the Machine Mentor feature must still fit the Pokémon’s proficiencies.

features.name: Open Enrollment
features.description: The best move tutors can work with any Pokémon, not just their own, and now you’re ready to teach any Pokémon. You can use any of your Move Tutor features to teach any Pokémon that’s willing to work with you. This includes ally’s Pokémon, stranger’s Pokémon, or even a wild Pokémon. You can potentially barter your tutoring services.

features.name: Class Time
features.description: Putting in the time to tutor Pokémon can be consuming for them, but you can split your attention without problems. While tutoring Pokémon, you can work with two Pokémon at a time and tutor both of them while using different Move Tutor features, or teach the same thing to both Pokémon with the same Move Tutor feature. If you are only tutoring your Pokémon, you can tutor three at a time.

features.name: Move Evolution
features.description: A tutor’s mastery allows them to fundamentally reshape how a move controls the battlefield. 1/day, after spending three hours working with one of your Pokémon, add one of the following effects to a move they have. Your Pokémon cannot have more than two moves modified by Move Improved or Move Evolution and each move that you modify can only have one change. If you change a move that’s already been modified, replace the last effect you gave with Move Improved or Move Evolution. - On hit, push or pull the target 15ft. If the target collides with a creature or solid object, it loses 2d6 HP. - On hit, if the target created Weather, Terrain, or a Zone on their last turn, destroy the Weather, Terrain, and/or Zone. - On hit, the target cannot use a Reaction until your next turn. This effect cannot affect the same target for more than one turn in a row. - On hit, choose one ally within 10ft. That ally may immediately move 10ft. - On hit, this move is Lethal until the end of combat. - [Special] If the target would be immune to this attack, you may still roll AC. On a hit, roll damage as normal and the target instead takes half of that damage. - (Choose Attack, Defense, SpAttack, SpDefense, or Speed while tutoring) On hit, 16 or higher during AC gives the target [Chosen Stat]▼. - (Choose Attack, Defense, SpAttack, SpDefense, or Speed while tutoring) On hit, you get [Chosen Stat]▲ on 12 or higher during AC. - (Melee Ranged Only) On hit, the target must target you on your next turn. On that turn they have advantage and any attack has +1d6 power. - (Single-target Ranged Only) [Special] If you did not move this round, the move has x3 range and ignores hindering terrain penalties.

features.name: Advanced Curriculum
features.description: By spending time your Pokémon and showing them your repertoire of tutor moves, they’ve mastered their ability to extend themselves and their move list. Any of your owned Pokémon can have up to eight moves.

features.name: Tutor Mastery
features.description: You spent enough time practicing move theory. Now, you can apply it however you’d like. 1/day, after spending six hours working with one of your Pokémon, you may teach it any non-legendary move. You may tutor moves that do not fit your Pokémon’s learnable moves description. You may not tutor the same Pokémon twice with Tutor Mastery unless you’re replacing a move previously taught with the Tutor Mastery feature or if the move taught with the Tutor Mastery feature has previously been removed from that Pokémon’s move list. Natural Tutoring does not enable you to reteach moves learned through Tutor Mastery. Your Open Enrollment feature is not compatible with Tutor Mastery.

name: Coordinator
flavorText:
Performer, Daring, Star
 Center stage is the best place to be for a Coordinator. 
Whether its at a contest or on the field of battle, they 
manipulate the audience and their opponents to pay 
attention whether they want to or not– but they really, 
really do. Coordinators have a flair for showing off the 
very best of everyone and when they grow, they become
