fashionistas, award-winning celebrities, and leaders.

features: Put Your Hands in the Air

features.name: Put Your Hands in the Air
features.description: Coordinators are expected to be able to rouse a crowd and you’re able to get them going. 3/day, choose a Star Point category that you already are aware of and add your Special Defense or Speed modifier to an appeal that matches that Star Point category for that appeal’s Heart Point total, or as an action one of your Pokémon within 30ft of you uses the move Helping Hand. Helping Hand - 3/day Melee Normal Effect. Target ally’s next attack has advantage. If it deals damage, it gets +2d power.

features.name: Wonderous Applause
features.description: You’re not one to brag, but you’re quite good at giving people what they want and you’ve trained your Pokémon to do the same. 3/day, once per encounter/contest, you may have your Pokémon’s contest appeal have the Crowd Pleaser effect in addition to whatever effect it usually has, or as an action one of your Pokémon within 30ft of you uses the move Encore. Encore - 3/day Ranged(10ft) Normal Effect. On hit, the target is Encored; they must use the move they used during the previous turn if possible. Encored is a status. Special Many coordinator features modify contest keywords for a move. Trainers can only add 1 more contest keyword to a move at a time. This does not change the move’s initial base appeal. If a Coordinator uses a feature as an action that allows their Pokémon to use a particular move, their Pokémon will only be able to use that move during their next turn. Having that Pokémon take their turn will require the Coordinator's command, as usual.

features.name: Favorite Festival
features.description: When it comes to contests, there is five different core styles to perform. You specialize in your choice of the following contest stats; Cool, Tough, Beauty, Clever, and Cute. Depending on your choice, Coordinator features will work in specific ways. When you get to level 7 and 11, you may choose another favorite contest attribute in addition to the one you chose at level 2. In addition, 3/ day, as an action, grant one of your Pokémon within 30 ft a passive for 10 mins. You can choose between any of the following passives which correspond to your chosen contest types. Attribute Passive Cool Inner Focus (You are immune to being Dazed.) Tough Big Pecks (Foes cannot give you Defense▼.) Beauty Overcoat (You are immune to damage from Weather.) Clever Own Tempo (You are immune to being Confused.) Cute Oblivious (You are immune to Entranced.)

features.name: Stat Increase and Advanced Class
features.description: Choose two different Trainer Stats to increase by 1, then gain 1d4 max HP. You only gain new stats at levels 3, 7, and 11. Choose a Coordinator Advanced Class or a different base Class. You can only ever gain a single Class or Advanced Class at a time, when leveling up.

features.name: Poised Instinct
features.description: When getting up to the stage, a feeling overwhelms you and you know exactly how to impress those in front of you. 1/day, when a contest starts, you are secretly informed of one Star Point category that you do not know. Once you are level 11, you are secretly informed of two Star Point categories. Additionally, whenever you are rolling a Perception check you may add your Special Defense or Speed modifier to your result.

features.name: Appearance
features.description: Coordinators gain fame as they blaze a trail of victory, wearing an aura of charisma that spreads throughout their entourage. 3/day, when an ally next to you rolls a skill check for Bluff, Diplomacy, or Pokémon Handling, they may add your Special Defense or Speed modifier in addition to any other bonuses they may add.

features.name: Steal the Show
features.description: At the drop of a hat, you and your Pokémon can gather a crowd’s attention and perform various talents to entertain and amaze. 3/day, once per encounter/contest: after you make an appeal, all opponents whose appeal qualifies for a Star Point category that your appeal matches get –6 on their appeal that round whether they preformed before or after you that round; or as an action one of your Pokémon within 30ft of you uses the move Follow Me (This is your command). In addition, 1/day you may hold the attention of everyone within 50ft of you while performing anywhere for X minutes where X is the sum of your Special Defense and Speed modifier. Allies are not affected by your antics and others may notice things happening around them with Perception skill checks. Follow Me - 3/day Ranged(30ft burst) Normal Effect. On hit, enemies are Entranced on their next turn.

features.name: Example
features.description: When using Steal the Show during a contest if your appeal scored 8 Heart Points and was relevant to two Star Point Categories [Most HP while using Cool Moves and most HP while using Fire-type Moves], any contestants who use a Fire-type move or a Cool Move during the same round get –6 Heart Points to their appeal for those Star Point categories

features.name: Stat Increase and Advanced Class
features.description: Choose two different Trainer Stats to increase by 1. You only ever will gain new stats at levels 3, 7, and 11. Choose a Coordinator Advanced Class or a different base Class. You can only ever gain a single Class or Advanced Class at a time, when leveling up. Gain 1d4 max HP.

features.name: Character Building
features.description: In order to raise the best contest Pokémon, having a healthy attitude for any given contest is key. 1/day, after spending two hours working with one of your Pokémon, you may change their nature depending on your chosen contest stats for your Favorite Festival feature. Adjust the Pokémon’s relevant stats when you do. You cannot use this feature with the same Pokémon more than once per week. Attribute Nature Options Cool Adamant (+Attack/-Special Attack) Brave (+Attack/-Speed) Lonely (+Attack/-Defense) Naughty (+Attack/-Special Defense) Tough Bold (+Defense/-Attack) Impish (+Defense/-Special Attack) Lax (+Defense/-Special Defense) Relaxed (+Defense/-Speed) Beauty Mild (+Special Attack/-Defense) Modest (+Special Attack/-Attack) Quiet (+Special Attack/-Speed) Rash (+Special Attack/-Special Defense) Clever Calm (+Special Defense/-Attack) Careful (+Special Defense/-Special Attack) Gentle (+Special Defense/-Defense) Sassy (+Special Defense/-Speed) Cute Hasty (+Speed/-Defense) Jolly (+Speed/-Special Attack) Naïve (+Speed/-Special Defense) Timid (+Speed/-Attack)

features.name: Rehearsed Sequence
features.description: Practice makes perfect and your Pokémon’s combination moves shine on the stage. For each of your Pokémon's moves, assign two as “Rehearsed.” 1/Contest, when Rehearsed moves are used consecutively over two rounds of appeal, add +2d4 to the second Rehearsed move. 3/day, during combat, when Rehearsed moves are used consecutively over two rounds of combat, if the second Rehearsed move is an attack it gains one of the following effects depending on the move’s Contest type. Attribute Effect Cool On hit, the target gets Attack▼. Tough On hit, the target gets Defense▼. Beauty On hit, the target gets SpAttack▼. Clever On hit, the target gets SpDefense▼. Cute On hit, the target gets Speed▼.

features.name: It’s How You Carry Yourself
features.description: By spending time with each of your performers, you’ve taught each of them to display talents without displeasing a judge, even when off script during a contest. 3/day, once per contest, when making an appeal to a judge, you can choose to make your Pokémon’s appeal not lower voltage or to make your Pokémon’s appeal raise the voltage regardless of how the voltage would normally be affected. In addition, 3/day, as an action, grant one of your Pokémon within 30 ft a passive for 10 mins. You can choose between any of the following passives which correspond to your chosen contest types. Attribute Option Cool Defiant (If a foe gives you any ▼, you get Attack▲▲.) Tough Battle Armor (Critical hits are treated as normal hits against you.) Beauty Multiscale (When you are at Max HP, you take –8 damage from all attacks.) Clever Filter (Super-effective attacks against you deal –4 damage.) Cute Cute Charm (Whenever you are hit with a melee attack, roll 1d4. On 4, Entrance the attacker.)

features.name: Stat Increase and Advanced Class
features.description: Choose two different Trainer Stats to increase by 1, then gain 1d4 max HP. You only gain new stats at levels 3, 7, and 11. Choose a Coordinator Advanced Class or a different base Class. You can only ever gain a single Class or Advanced Class at a time, when leveling up.

features.name: Poise, Serenity, Style
features.description: Just walking into a space can draw looks and you and your Pokémon know how to make a first impression. The first 2 times you roll a 1 during a contest appeals, reroll those dice. In addition, upon meeting someone new, you have a +2 to any Insight skill checks you make against them. In addition, 3/day, as an action, grant one of your Pokémon within 30 ft a passive for 10 mins. You can choose between any of the following passives which correspond to your chosen contest types. Attribute Option Cool Magician (When hitting with a melee attack, you steal the target’s held item, if any.) Tough No Guard (You cannot miss your attacks, and attacks made against you cannot miss.) Beauty Mirror Armor (If a foe would give you a ▼, instead that foe gets the ▼ they tried to give you.) Clever Download (When using a Physical attack, you have +2 during AC against targets with lower Defense than Special Defense. When using a Special attack, you have +2 during AC against targets with lower Special Defense than Defense.) Cute Hustle (If you miss an attack, you get Attack▲▲.)

features.name: Breathtaking Flourish
features.description: By minimizing destructive battle capabilities and effort, you Pokémon can focus on the glamour of performing two moves simultaneously to woo judges and audience alike. 1/day, one of your Pokémon can perform two moves during the same appeal round and roll for both moves, adding them together for the appeal. In addition, you gain the following options depending on your chosen contest stats. After spending a total of 10 hours with one of your Pokémon who has earned at least 2 corresponding Contest Ribbons, you may teach your Pokémon the following moves. Attribute Option Cool Pack Mon - 1/day Ranged(20ft burst) Dark Effect. On hit, enemies are Entranced on their next turn. Pack Mon cannot miss. All wild Pokémon targets that share an egg group with you follow your lead for 1 hour. Wild Pokémon following you will attack with you, defend with you, help to accomplish tasks, and lead others through wild areas when asked to do so by an allied Trainer. Wild Pokémon following you will not attack their own kind, actively destroy their homes, nor leave the wilds following you into a town or city. Tough Impenetrable Stance - 1/day Self Fighting Effect. Reaction [When you are hit by a foe’s attack within 25ft]. Negate the damage and effects of the attack. Stance: You cannot be given Afflictions, and you do not take damage from enemy moves. If you move, are moved, or use a move, exit this Stance. It also ends after three rounds. Beauty Absolutely Breathtaking - 1/day Ranged(30ft burst) Normal Effect. Absolutely Breathtaking has Turns. [Turn 1, 2, & 3] Move then roll Absolutely Breathtaking’s AC. On hit, all targets are Dazed. Clever Language - 1/day Ranged(20ft) Psychic Effect. On hit, the target becomes Confused. [Special Effect] Language can be learned multiple times. When Language is acquired, chose a human language. You are capable of speaking basic sentences in the chosen languages. If the same human language is chosen by multiple instances of Language, you can speak that language at any level complexity. Cute Cutesy Coercion - 1/day Ranged(15ft) Fairy Effect. If the target is a Pokémon and has not acted yet during this round of combat, you choose where it moves, what it targets, and what attack it uses this round (You may not use the controlled Pokémon to attack a non-Pokémon target; you know the controlled Pokémon’s move list during this turn). If the target uses an attack, half the total damage from its attack after rolling damage.

features.name: Contest Tutoring
features.description: Having seen and studied various moves that make a splash in contests you’ve figured out how to teach those moves to your Pokémon. 1/day, after spending three hours working with one of your Pokémon, you may teach a move that has a contest attribute matching one of your chosen contest stats for your Favorite Festival feature. Moves taught with the Contest Tutoring feature must still fit the Pokémon’s proficiencies. A Pokémon cannot benefit from Contest Tutoring more than once per week.

features.name: Star of the Show
features.description: There isn’t a person in the stadium who isn’t watching you perform, no matter what the event. 1/Contest, after the final appeal during a Contest, but before Star Points are awarded, choose a category from the list below for which a Star Point will be awarded. Your chosen category replaces a Star Point category of your GM’s choice that you do not know. If you know every category for which Star Points will be awarded, you may choose which category to replace. The category you choose may be a category that already is awarding a Star Point, meaning that two Star Points will be awarded for that criteria. In addition, during Pokémon battles, your Pokémon have +3 speed when deciding turn order if they have earned more contest ribbons than any enemy Pokémon. In addition, whenever you use a feature that temporarily grants a Pokémon a passive ability, you can use it to target an allied Pokémon instead of only being able to use it on your own Pokémon. Star Point Category - Most HP while using ‘w’ Moves w = Beauty, Clever, Cool, Cute, or Tough - Most HP while using ‘x’-type Moves x = Bug, Dark, Dragon, Electric, Fairy, Fighting, Fire, Flying, Ghost, Grass, Ground, Ice, Normal, Poison, Psychic, Rock, Steel, or Water - Most HP while dealing damage to a Dummy This can only be chosen if there was a dummy. - Most damage dealt to a Dummy This can only be chosen if there was a dummy. - Highest ‘y’ Stat y = Beauty, Clever, Cool, Cute, or Tough - Most Voltage Raised - Most HP while using ‘z’ Moves z = Physical, Special, Effect, or Style. - Highest total HP while making Appeals - Second highest total HP while making Appeals - Lowest total HP while making Appeals

name: Choreographer
flavorText:
The rhythm of the stage and of battle flow in the same 
ways.
 A Choreographer teaches Pokémon to always move 
with intention to the rhythm of their life. Each step, each 
note, each sound they make grows into a better 
performance, or a way around an incoming attack from 
enemies.

features.name: Base Routine
features.description: Your Pokémon move in rhythmic ways, gracefully making their way across the stage of battle. Whenever your Pokémon do not move their full distance during their turn in combat, they get +1 to their Defense, Special Defense, and Speed the next time they are targeted by an attack.

features.name: Practicing Scales
features.description: You often sing with your Pokémon, as you try to teach them different basic melodies and sounds to make with their voices. When using attacks, your Pokémon’s move can be treated as if they are Sound movesor not regardless of what they naturally are. In addition, 1/day you may spend two hours with one of your Pokémon to teach them the move Soft Song. Soft Song - Ranged(10ft) Normal Effect: 3/day. On hit, target is Drowsy. If the target is already Drowsy, either cure them of Drowsy or they are also Dazed.

features.name: En Point
features.description: You and your Pokémon are not to be frazzled during battle, each step is graceful planned and executed. When you or your Pokémon do not move their full distance during their turn in combat, they cannot be Dazed or moved by a foe’s effects until their next turn.

features.name: Attention to Me
features.description: Coordinators may be able to grab attention with their charms, but you perform like none other. Whenever you make a Perform skill check with that would involve either dance or your voice roll the check three times and use the best result.

features.name: Gradual Rise
features.description: A well-choreographed performance with a gradual rise and climax will astound the audience and judges alike. If during each round of appeals, the Heart Points you earn are each consecutively higher than your previous score, gain 10d4 points after the final appeal. In addition, if your Pokémon would deal less damage during a round of combat than their previous turn during an attack, they may add +1d6 power to that attack once per combat.

features.name: Stage Presence
features.description: Often, judges will be particularly interested in your Pokémon’s appeal because they always seem to add a different flourish or lovely tune while doing so. 3/day, during an appeal, you may replace up to X d4 with d6, where X is your Special Defense or Speed modifier.

features.name: Gentle Footfall
features.description: Poise is important while dancing and in as a byproduct of your training you’ve developed particularly silent footsteps. When making Stealth skill checks, you have advantage. In addition, whenever your Pokémon makes an attack against a foe from behind the foe’s line of sight and was not in the target’s line of sight during that turn, they may add +2 during their AC.

features.name: Enthralling Voices
features.description: Your Pokémon command the attention of others in battle and even influence Pokémon to stop in place, getting lost in your Pokémon’s charms. 3/ day, as an action, you add the effect, “On hit, the target is Entranced,” to one of your Pokémon’s attacks that does not already have an effect that causes an affliction during their next turn. In addition, during the appeal rounds in contests, Pokémon making an appeal immediately after your Pokémon in the same round do not roll one of their d4 for a single appeal unless they have already been affected by your Enthralling Voices feature during that contest.

features.name: Dancing Dodge
features.description: The constant flow of battle has a rhythm of its own and you with your Pokémon can slide around attacks and problems. 1/day, if you would be hit by a Pokémon’s attack that only targeted you, you may dodge it completely. In addition, once per week you may spend 4 hours with once of your Pokémon to teach them the move Detect. Detect - 1/day Self Fighting Effect. Reaction [When you are hit by an attack]. The attacker must reroll their AC at disadvantage. If the attacker still hits, you do not lose your next action.

features.name: As Rehearsed
features.description: Often you’ll spend time with your Pokémon going over their routines for a contest, and sticking to a script often has good payoffs. At the beginning of a contest, you may choose the moves your Pokémon will be performing during each round of appeals (you do not need to commit to any judges to appeal to in your script, only the moves and round order). If you do, your Pokémon’s appeals cannot be negatively affected by other contestant’s displays and once during the contest per judge, you may the judge you are appealing to have their voltage raised once regardless of your appeal’s contest attribute. Additionally, when your Pokémon does not move its full distance during its turn, the next attack it makes during the same round has the following effect: ”On hit, 17 or higher during AC inflicts Dazed.”

features.name: Elemental Flourish
features.description: When moving about passionately, you Pokémon may release energy from themselves that enhance their performances. 3/day, as an action, you may have your Pokémon’s normal-type move change its type to match one of its types until the end of combat. In addition, once per contest you may have one of your Pokémon’s move change its attribute into a different contest attribute of your choice (Beauty, Clever, Cool, Cute, Tough).

features.name: Dazzling the Stage
features.description: Your Pokémon’s appeals are stunning and when perfectly executed your Pokémon’s performances destroy anyone else’s chance at winning. Before rolling your dice during any appeal choose a number. If your result for Heart Points during that appeal matches the chosen number, double the value of your appeal during that round. You cannot pick the same number two rounds in a row. 1/day, when one of your Pokémon has not moved its full distance for three consecutive turns, you may use Dazzling the Stage as an action. The next attack that Pokémon uses cannot miss and is a critical hit.

name: Coach
flavorText:
Let’s kick it up, together everyone!
 Physical training is harsh work, but your Pokémon 
know what you can give to them and they’re into it. By 
pushing your Pokémon they can perform better than ever 
in pokéathalons and help get things done on the field of 
battle.

features.name: Faster
features.description: Kick it up! Really lean into it! Your cheers push your Pokémon to go faster and faster when it matters. 3/ day, as an action, one of your Pokémon within 25 ft gets a temporary bonus to its movement speed (this does not affect its Speed stat). The bonus is equal to 5 feet multiplied by your Speed or Special Defense modifier, and lasts for one hour.

features.name: Stronger
features.description: You’ve got this! Push harder! Your encouragement pushes some extra strength into your Pokémon’s efforts. 3/day, as an action, one of your Pokémon within 25ft are twice as strong and can move objects one size larger or one weight heavier than itself as if they were the same size as them, for the next hour. In addition, those Pokémon deal X more damage when attacking with a Physical move (where X is your Special Defense or Speed modifier). Additionally, if there is a dummy during a contest to attack on stage, your Pokémon deal +4 damage to the dummy during their appeals.

features.name: Work It
features.description: This is nothing new! Get it done! Your direction helps your Pokémon overcome obstacles without issue. 3/ day, as an action, for the next hour, one of your Pokémon within 25ft treats all difficult terrain as normal terrain, can move through enemies without slowing down, and treats vertical terrain (walls/trees/structures) as normal terrain when moving on the terrain.

features.name: Harder
features.description: No! Not yet! Push through it! When your Pokémon hears your concern, it pushes through oncoming attacks. 1/day, when one of your Pokémon would be hit by an attack and the offender rolled the exact value it needed in order to hit, instead the attack misses and that Pokémon moves up to 30ft to avoid any area-of-effect.

features.name: Surf It
features.description: This is nothing! It’s just water! Your careful training has enabled your Pokémon’s movement both in and out of water. 3/day, as an action, motivate one of your Pokémon within 25ft for an hour. They may move at full speed through special terrain (water); they may ignore the Flopper skill (if they have it) to move at full speed out of water; and they do not take damage from damaging Weather (ex. Sandstorm, Hail).

features.name: Hour After Hour
features.description: Keep up with me! We’re not done yet! Repeated work out sessions with your Pokémon maintains them in top shape, ready for anything. As long as your Pokémon spend at least three days every week working out with you, for at least an hour per session, they have +1 to your choice of Attack, Special Attack, or Speed while you continue to exercise with them. Multiple Pokémon can all be working out together at the same time, but no more than six Pokémon can benefit from your Hour After Hour feature at a time. *Your Pokémon could be doing these work out sessions with you before you acquire Hour After Hour, then benefit from Hour After Hour once you have it.

features.name: Bring It
features.description: Come on! Imagine how hard it is for our Pokémon! Do not stop! You’ve got your whole group of friends going. By maintaining a routine of working with you for an hour each day, at least three days per week, your friends can gain an enhanced physique. They must maintain the routine for at least one week, and lose their benefits if they do not work out at least three days per week. They can work out together with your Pokémon through Hour After Hour, but no more than six trainers including yourself can benefit from your Bring It feature at a time. You and the trainers who maintain the routine with you and your Pokémon can pick 3 worth of the following options to earn through exercise (do not pick the same bonus more than once): 1 Each: - You move +10 feet per round of combat. - Your Speed is +3 when determining turn order in combat. - Easily lift your own weight. - You are not hindered by difficult terrain. - You cannot be disarmed or stolen from as long as the item is in your grip. - 1/day, take half the damage you would have taken from fall or collision damage. 2 Each: - You move +20 feet per round of combat. - You can climb and swim at your normal speed. - You can easily lift twice your own weight. - 3/day, you have advantage when initiating a grapple to Bind something. - 3/day, you have advantage when throwing something. - You do not become fatigued from physical labor or activity for up to 8 continuous hours of that physical labor or activity. 3 Each: - You move +45 feet per round of combat. - 3/day you have advantage on an Athletics skill check. - You cannot be pushed and you have advantage when making skill checks to escape being Bound. - 1/day, you have +2 to your Attack or Speed stat for 1 hour (this can ignore any trainer stat caps). - You take -3 damage from Physical attacks. - Unless surprised, your Speed is +10 when determining turn order in combat. *Allied trainers could be doing these work out sessions with you before you acquire Bring It, then benefit from Bring it once you have it.

features.name: Makes Us Stronger
features.description: Everyone put everything you’ve got into it! Your enthusiasm empowers allies to push them forward. When using a Coach feature, instead of targeting just one of your Pokémon, your Coach features affect all of your Pokémon.

features.name: Make It Better
features.description: Great job! Rest up, we’re not done! Quick aid keeps your Pokémon in top shape for more competition. 1/day, after a battle, pokéathalon, or contest, you can spend 10 mins with all of your Pokémon to fully recover the HP they lost during the combat or competition while also giving them the ability to perform 3/day and 1/day frequency moves again as it they had a full rest.

features.name: Never Over
features.description: That’s weak! It’s nothing compared to your strength! Let’s go! Your Pokémon know what your expectations are and they’re holding on for you. As long as they haven’t acted, your Pokémon can give up their turns during a round to survive an attack at 1 hit point if they were at their max hit points before being attacked.

features.name: Face to Face
features.description: Don’t let them get a lead on you! Get there! Your Pokémon can edge out a little more steam when facing a near-match. When determining turn order, if there is a tie, your Pokémon go first. In addition, 1/day, if once of your Pokémon misses an attack by 1 or 2, you can have them successfully hit instead. In addition, if any of your Pokémon are the first Pokémon to act in combat, or if any of your Pokémon hit because of your use of Face to Face, they get Attack▲ or SpAttack▲.

features.name: More Than Ever
features.description: This is what it’s all been for! Don’t any of you give up! Keep on pushing until the very end! Any Pokémon or allied trainers currently benefiting from your Hour After Hour or Bring It features get to reroll their first natural 1 per day. Also, those trainers get 2 more to pick for Bring It’s bonuses. In addition, during appeals in contests, your Pokémon currently benefiting from your Hour After Hour feature treat any rolled 1s as 2.

name: Designer
flavorText:
I know exactly what would look great on you.
 Designers make beautiful works of art, for people to 
wear and accessorize with. With enough work, they 
eventually can surpass manufactured items in both 
appearance and application.

features.name: Accessorize
features.description: With love and a flair of style you create an amazing accessory to beautify your Pokémon. After one hour of work, you create a Pokémon accessory. The accessory can be a piece of clothing, jewelry, or a trinket it holds. Call it whatever you’d like, made out of whatever you’d like. In addition, it takes you one hour to repair any broken item or accessory made by you. Accessory - 1/day, when making an appeal during a contest, add 1d4. A Pokémon can only benefit from one accessory at a time. This Accessory must be maintained by you at least once a week (5 mins) or it breaks.

features.name: Practical Designer
features.description: Creating a perfect something that just makes someone’s look pop can help a person succeed when they least expect it. After one hour of work, you create a trainer accessory. The accessory can be a piece of clothing, jewelry, or a trinket someone holds. Call it whatever you’d like, made out of whatever you like. In addition, you are skilled in making clothing for trainers and can produce a shirt, pants, or dress in about 3 hours out of appropriate materials. Trainer Accessory - 1/day, when you roll a Skill Check for a Skill you are Talented with, you may add +2 to your result. A person can only benefit from one trainer accessory at a time. This Accessory must be maintained by you at least once a week (5 mins) or it breaks.

features.name: Lucky Charm
features.description: Something about the perfect charm on your wrist, or in your hair, or wherever you think someone should place it, just clicks and makes someone’s personality really come out. After two hours of work, you create a Lucky Charm. The charm can be a piece of jewelry, or a trinket you wear. Call it whatever you’d like, made out of whatever you like. Lucky Accessory - 1/day, when you roll a Skill Check for a Skill you are Talented with and fail, you may reroll and use the second result. If you fail again, you fumble in some way and lose 1d10 hit points. A person can only benefit from one trainer accessory at a time. This Accessory must be maintained by you at least once a week (5 mins) or it breaks.

features.name: Bright Charm
features.description: You focus your efforts on an accessory with some kind of gimmick; mundane at first, but with the flick of a wrist a pop of confetti or a flash of smoke appears. After one hour of work, you create a Bright Pokémon Accessory. The accessory can be a piece of clothing, jewelry, or a trinket it holds. Call it whatever you’d like, made out of whatever you’ like. Bright Accessory - 1/day, when appealing to a judge you may raise the judge’s voltage +1. A Pokémon can only benefit from one accessory at a time. This Accessory must be maintained by you at least once a week (5 mins) or it breaks.

features.name: Tactical Design
features.description: It’s not always about looks, but when you do need a glove for climbing or a shoe for running, you can make it and make it look good. After six hours of work you create a clothing equipment for a trainer that has a specific application (running shoes, grip gloves, camouflage cape, etc.). Call it whatever you’d like, made out of whatever you like. Equipment Accessory - Whenever you roll a Skill Check while doing the activity the equipment is made for, you may add +3 to your roll. A person can only benefit from one trainer accessory at a time. This Accessory must be maintained by you at least once a week (5 mins) or it breaks.

features.name: The Look
features.description: Sometimes, you just have to take another person’s design and make it your own. By looking at what someone else is currently wearing you’re able to make the same clothing out of the same material, adjusted for whomever you’re planning to have wear the clothing. It would take 2 hours of work per piece of clothing/ accessory to replicate what the person was wearing when you saw them but cannot replicate any other special properties of the copied outfit. You may apply effects of your Designer features to any individual piece of clothing or accessory throughout the set of things that you are copying. Unskilled individuals cannot determine whether or not your products are an original or a fake.

features.name: Glamorous
features.description: Bold fashion statements can catch the eyes of everyone and it makes it hard not to catch everyone’s gaze when you’re the designer. When making clothing for trainers, you may spend an extra hour making the clothing to give the clothing the following effect: “All non-allied trainer’s Perception and Investigate Skill checks are -3 when you are within their line of sight.”

features.name: Cosplay Designer
features.description: It’s not always practical, but you’re an amazing costume designer. You can spend 30 hours over multiple days to create a medium or smaller Pokémon costume that passes for a real Pokémon unless something makes a successful difficult Investigate skill check at a distance of less than 25ft. You may make it out of whatever you’d like, but the cheaper your materials, the more likely it is for someone else to recognize the costume as a costume (the Investigate skill check will be easier). If you spend over 100 hours on making your costume, it is a very difficult skill check to tell that a person inside the costume is not whatever the costume is disguising them as- at any distance.

features.name: Item Builder
features.description: You’ve spent hours working to figure out how the battle accessories manufactured by professional companies work and you’ve figured a few of them out. 3/ week, you may spend four hours working to build one of the following items. The items made with Item Builder need one hour of your maintenance per two weeks, otherwise they break. Ability Shield - Your passives cannot be disabled or replaced by any foe’s effects during combat. Absorb Bulb - When you are hit by a Water-type attack, Absorb Bulb is destroyed and you get SpAttack▲. Bright Powder - As a free action, destroy Bright Powder. Until your next turn, if you are targeted by an attack, the attacker must roll +2 higher in order to hit you during AC. Cell Battery - When you are hit by a Electric-type attack, Cell Battery is destroyed and you get Attack▲. Clear Amulet - You are immune to getting ▼ from the effects of your foe’s Styles. Covert Cloak - You are immune to the effects of your foe’s held items. Destiny Knot - When you become Entranced, the Pokémon who caused your Entranced becomes Entranced with you as well. Float Stone - If you are Heavy (weight), you are treated as Medium (weight). This is also true for Medium to Light and Light to Featherweight. Focus Band - If you would be knocked out, you may roll 1d20. On 17 or higher, you are instead set to 1 hit point and the Focus Band is destroyed. Grip Claw - If you bind a foe and your foe tries to escape, they must roll +4 higher to escape successfully. Heavy Boots - The first time you would take damage from a Hazard per combat, ignore that damage. Iron Ball - If you are Featherweight (weight), you are treated as Light (weight). This is also true for Light to Medium and Medium to Heavy. Luminous Moss - When you are hit by a Water-type attack, Luminous Moss is destroyed and you get SpDefense▲. Protective Pads - If you would be damaged as a result of making a melee attack against a foe by a foe’s passive or other effect, ignore that damage. Razor Fang - Your Latched attacks deal +2 damage. Ring Target - You lose all of your type immunities. When hit by an attack that you are usually immune to, treat the damage as ineffective. Safety Goggles - You are immune to damaging effects from Weather. Shed Shell - As a free Reaction [When you become Bound by a foe], destroy Shed Shell. You are no longer Bound. Snowball - When you are hit by an Ice-type attack, Snowball is destroyed and you get Attack▲. Sticky Barb - Whenever you move more than 10ft during your turn, you lose 1d4 HP. If you are hit by a melee range attack, give Sticky Barb to the attacker. Throat Spray - Your Sound attacks deal +2 damage. Elemental Boons - Elemental Boons have many different names and each correspond to each Pokémon type (Soft Sand for Ground, Silk Scarf for Normal, Never-Melt-Ice for Ice, etc.). You can name them whatever you’d like and you must define what type it empowers. They each have the following ability: Any of your same-typed attacks, deal an additional +2 damage. Weather, Terrain, and Zone Rocks - These items are named after the Weather, Terrain, or Zone that the held item affects (Sunny Rock, Tricky Rock, Grassy Rock, etc.). They each have the following ability: When you create the corresponding Weather, Terrain, or Zone, destroy this item. The Weather, Terrain, or Zone that you create lasts for five minutes. Weather, Terrain, and Zone Seeds - These items are named after the Weather, Terrain, or Zone that the held item affects (Rainy Seed, Gravity Seed, Electric Seed, etc.). They each have the following ability: When you are in the corresponding Weather, Terrain, or Zone, destroy this item. You get Speed▲.

features.name: Trendsetting Brand
features.description: Your style doesn’t just impress, it defines the moment. Your goods are valuable and others can tell by its looks what your brand is. When trying to sell your created Fashion Designer goods to others, you have advantage on any skill checks while bartering or up-selling your goods. Additionally, 3/day, after you change your outfit you will have advantage on the first skill check you make. In addition, your crafted accessories no longer need constant maintenance.

features.name: Item Manufacturer
features.description: After working to build some of your own, you’ve figured out the rest and can create your own arsenal of items of your Pokémon’s use. 3/week, you may spend four hours working to build one of the following items. Additionally, if your Pokémon or an ally’s Pokémon use any item that you’ve made that is destroyed after use, is is not destroyed. Instead it is only damaged and can’t be used again until you fix it over the course of 1 hour. Adrenaline Orb - If you get Attack▼ or SpAttack▼ from a foe’s effects, you get Speed▲. If you get Attack▼▼ or SpAttack▼▼ from a foe’s effects, you get Speed▲▲. Air Balloon - You are immune to Ground-type attacks. If you are hit by any other type of attack, Air Balloon is destroyed. Assault Vest - Your Special Defense is +2. You may not use moves that do not have power. Big Root - Whenever you would recover HP or gain temporary HP after dealing damage to a foe, gain +1d4 temporary HP. Binding Band - If you use an attack that binds a target, the target loses 1d4 HP at the end of each of your turns if they are still Bound. Choice Band - Your Attack stat is +2. Whenever you use a move, that is the only move you can use for the rest of the encounter. If you can no longer use that move, you may still Struggle. Choice Scarf - Your Speed stat is +2. Whenever you use a move, that is the only move you can use for the rest of the encounter. If you can no longer use that move, you may still Struggle. Choice Specs - Your Special Attack stat is +2. Whenever you use a move, that is the only move you can use for the rest of the encounter. If you can no longer use that move, you may still Struggle. Eviolite - If you can still potentially evolve, your Defense and Special Defense stats are +1. Expert Belt - When you hit with a super-effective or extremely-effective attack, deal an additional +2 damage. Focus Sash - If you would be knocked out from a single attack when you were at max hit points, instead you are set to 1 hit point once per battle. King’s Rock - On your first single-target attack per day, the attack gains the following effect: “18 or higher during AC inflicts Dazed.” Lagging Tail - You act last during each round of combat. Life Orb - Your attacks have +1d6 power. After acting, no matter what actions you take, you lose 1d6 HP. Metronome - Your attacks have +1d4 power for each other time the same attack has been used that encounter (max +3d4). Muscle Band - Your Physical attacks deal +1 damage. Quick Claw - On your first single-target melee attack with at-will frequency per day, the attack gains the following effect: “This attack has Priority.” Razor Claw - On your first single-target melee attack per day, the attack gains the following effect: “This attack is Lethal.” Rocky Helmet - Whenever you are hit by an attack at melee range, the attacker loses 1d4 HP. Scope Lens - On your first single-target ranged attack per day, the attack gains the following effect: “This attack is Lethal.” Shell Bell - Whenever you hit with an attack, you can drop your highest rolled damage result. If you do, recover 1d4 HP. Wide Lens - Your effect moves have +1 during AC. Wise Glasses - Your Special attacks deal +1 damage. Zoom Lens - On your first attack per combat, your attack has +2 during AC and -4 power.

features.name: Endless Versatility
features.description: Accessories, items, clothing- it doesn’t matter; you’ve got a creative itch and you’re ready to make it all. When making something with your Designer features, you only take half of the time to produce whatever it is you’re making. In addition, you can alter the effects of the items you make with the Item Builder and Item Manufacturer features by changing any Pokémon type word, or stat word (for example you could make a Black Sludge item work with Fairy types instead, an Air Balloon that grants immunity to Grass-type attacks, or make an Absorb Bulb activate on a Fire-type attack, then give SpDefense▲). In addition, you can use your Cosplay Designer feature to create costumes of other people you have seen before (pictures work if you have views of their front, sides, and back). In addition, you may make held items with your features that affect trainers instead of Pokémon that are all one-time use items.

name: Groomer
flavorText:
Oh! Aren’t you just the cutest thing? Let’s get you made 
up!
 For a Pokémon, there isn’t much better than being 
pampered by a Groomer. You tend the individual needs of 
Pokémon and fine tune their natural looks to make them 
happier and happier.

features.name: Expert Grooming
features.description: It’s a groomer’s duty to keep their Pokémon’s fur fluffy, feathers dusted, or scales shined. You can spend fifteen mins with one of your Pokémon to give them an Expert Grooming. After the grooming they are relaxed unless they are agitated again, you can emphasize and polish their physical appearance, making them appear to be healthy, sick, or any other physical state within normal variation for their species. Your Pokémon quickly gain loyalty to you if you’re grooming them often and are very unlikely to lose loyalty unless there’s any intentional mistreatment.

features.name: Pokémon Whisperer
features.description: Humans are rarely inclined to start a fight while already in conversation, and neither are Pokémon. After speaking in a calm tone to a Pokémon for at least ten seconds, that Pokémon will refrain from attacking as long as you continue speaking, you and your allies do not approach them or initiate combat, and there is no clear threat to them. If you are already physically but nonviolently handling them as you begin speaking with them, they will allow you to continue to handle them or use your Groomer features on them.

features.name: Touch Up
features.description: With some quick snips, brushing, and balms you fix up your Pokémon. 3/day, after spending a minute working with a Pokémon, choose one of the following types of Grooming for that Pokémon. Other Groomer features improve Touch Up. Apply all benefits related to the type of Grooming you select. Battle Grooming - Restore a single use of a Pokémon’s 3/day move. Comfort Grooming - Heal 4 HP. Performance Grooming - +2 to Attack, Special Attack, or Speed for ten minutes, or until they take damage, whichever comes first. Display Grooming - The first two rolled 1s during contest appeals can be rerolled on the same day.

features.name: Groomer’s Eye
features.description: By working with Pokémon to make them look the best they can all the time, you have insight into a Pokémon's needs when you’re working with them. When making Pokémon Handling checks you have advantage. If you’re grooming or pacifying a Pokémon as you do this, roll three times and use the best result instead. In addition, while grooming a Pokémon, you can determine any stressors that the Pokémon is dealing with (maltreatment, hunger, sickness, etc.), whether or not it is loyal to its trainer, any special traits of its parentage or birth environment, any special needs it may have.

features.name: Contest Coating
features.description: They’re just too much to look at! They’re so amazingly over the top! Your special care really gives your Pokémon an edge during Contests. Your Pokémon can have up to 12 points total contest stats. In addition, loyal Pokémon you’ve had for at least one week that have been cared for with Expert Grooming do not take a penalty to their stat because of their nature. Additionally, Touch Up can now be used 5/day and gives these additional boons while being used: Battle Grooming - Restore a single use of a Pokémon’s 1/day move. Comfort Grooming - The next time you would be attacked today, take -2 damage. Performance Grooming - The next time you receive a ▼ today, ignore it. Display Grooming - Add +4 to your next contest appeal today.

features.name: Quick Cleanse
features.description: Some Pokémon need special attention to take care of a particularly bad day battling and with careful grooming, you’ve got them covered. 3/day, as an action, you can cure a Pokémon of any one affliction, remove any ▼ or ▼▼, or prevent the next affliction the Pokémon would receive that day.

features.name: Attribution Assistance
features.description: All this grooming is supposed to be for showing off a contest, so you’ve begun to focus on what makes a Pokémon pop in a stricter contest setting. 1/day, while Expert Grooming, you may add 1 point to any of the Pokémon’s contest stats, but cannot raise any of their contest stats to a value higher than whichever is the higher value between your Special Defense and Speed stats with this ability. Additionally, Touch Up can now be used 7/day and gives these additional boons while being used: Battle Grooming - Fully restore the use of a 3/day move. Comfort Grooming - The next time a foe gives you an affliction today, you may immediately make two checks to try and cure it. Performance Grooming - You have advantage on the next single-target attack you make today. Display Grooming - If you would raise Voltage, you may add +1 more Voltage one time today.

features.name: Glossy Alteration
features.description: These makeover looks are stunning and have a functional form. 1/day, while Expert Grooming one of your loyal Pokémon, you may have the groomed Pokémon gain one of the following Passives or Skills: Immunity, Limber, Magma Armor, Vital Spirit, or Water Veil; or Alluring, Glow, Repulsive, or Stealth. Each of your Pokémon cannot have more than one passive and/or skill granted by Glossy Alteration at a time. This feature can have a Pokémon exceed the three passive limit. Passives Immunity (You are immune to getting Poisoned and Toxified.) Limber (You are immune to being Paralyzed.) Magma Armor (You are immune to getting Frostbite.) Vital Spirit (You are immune to getting Drowsy.) Water Veil (You are immune to being Burned.) Skills Alluring (attracts others with their appearance) Glow (can produce light) Repulsive (repels others with their appearance) Stealth (can make stealth skill checks)

features.name: Groundbreaking Makeover
features.description: It’s unorthodox, it’s wild, it’s insane but you’ve figured it out and you’ve got the perfect customers- your lovely Pokémon! Once per week, after spending 10 hours working on one of your loyal Pokémon, they become a shiny Pokémon. Choose any color for them to permanently become in whatever pattern you’d like. In addition, during introductory appeals in contests, your shiny Pokémon adds 2d4 to their initial appeal and can replace any of their move’s contest effects with the Attention Grabber or Special Attention effect once per contest.

features.name: Head Turner
features.description: It’s not your expertise, but why not dive into the world of trainer haircuts and styling? You can spend fifteen mins with another trainer to give them a makeover. If you change the trainer’s hair style, hair color, or general amount of make up they might use, it’s possible that they won’t be immediately recognizable. When made over, trainers making Bluff or Diplomacy skill checks within the first 12 hours of your makeover get +3 on their skill check on their first skill check per person they interact with. You may make yourself over, but it takes thirty mins to use Head Turner instead.

features.name: Secured Style
features.description: The contest stage is a battlefield, just as much as the battlefield is a performance stage, and with your beautification, your Pokémon are ready for anything! 1/day, after Expert Grooming a loyal Pokémon or an allied trainer’s loyal Pokémon raise its Defense or Special Defense stat by 2 for 3 hours. Additionally, the Pokémon can ignore the contest effect of one move performed by an opponent during a contest that would affect when your Pokémon performs during appeals, or prevents voltage manipulation of some kind.

features.name: Elite Glamour
features.description: Untouchable beauty for any Pokémon in ten to fifteen minutes. 1/day, after Expert Grooming a loyal Pokémon, they may give them an Elite Coat . The Coat has the following ability: When you take damage from an attack while at max HP, halve the damage. This Coat lasts for 12 hours and does not disappear when a Pokémon with the Elite Coat is returned to a Poké Ball. Groomer contributions by Sol

name: Rising Star
flavorText:
Thank you, thank you! I owe this all to you! My fans!
 The Rising Star knows how to manage their brand and 
climb higher and higher in the social echelon. Whatever 
the talent is that raises them into the spotlight, their 
personal wealth greatly benefits from the fame and 
fandom.

features.name: Incognito
features.description: You chose the path of fame and maintain an online presence that garners thousands if not hundreds of thousands of followers, so it’s a good skill to be able to lay low. When you want to, you can change your clothes or style in some way to become uninteresting. While uninteresting, it’s much harder for others to notice what you’re doing and your Stealth and Sleight of Hand skill checks have +2, however your Bluff, Insight, and Diplomacy skill checks all have -2.

features.name: Influencer
features.description: There’s very little stopping you from getting what you want, just by standing by something or somewhere, others will want to be there buying those things, too. When purchasing items for yourself or your Pokémon, you will get a discount depending on the size of the store or other place of service. A small mom and pop shop will not give you that much of a discount but larger conglomerate stores will give you more generous discounts and even gifts. While all stores are obligated to give you discounts, be aware that any pushy behavior may result in unwelcome behavior from the store’s employees.

features.name: Golden Cheer
features.description: Your exuberance raises the mood of your allies and helps them to succeed whenever you’re cheering them on. 3/day, when an ally makes an attack, or attempts a skill check, they have advantage. If the attack or skill check already is making two or more rolls, add another roll and use the best result.

features.name: Autographs and Selfies
features.description: When you want to flaunt it and catch everyone’s attention, you’re usually able to cause quite a scene by announcing your presence. As long as you are in a region where your fame is known (at least 3 ribbons and/or badges) you can announce your presence and cause a distraction. Non-allied trainers nearby are compelled to either join you, asking for your autograph or a photo with you, or are just distracted by the spectacle of your showmanship. If anyone becomes distracted by something other than you, or are otherwise alerted, they will stop whatever it is they were doing with you earlier than normal, if not immediately.

features.name: Garnered Loyalty
features.description: Your Pokémon love you and if they don’t, they are really easy to win over. Your Pokémon with under 4 loyalty, rapidly gain loyalty. It takes no more than 24 hours to raise one of your Pokémon’s loyalty one stage if they are at loyalty 0, 1, or 2 unless they are already at 2 loyalty. It takes intentional and malicious mistreatment to lower your Pokémon’s loyalties.

features.name: Seat of Celebrity
features.description: Once well known in your expertise, you dominate the personalities in your sphere of influence and others will often go out of their way to make a mutually beneficial deal go through. Depending on the base classes you have, you gain some of the following options, these trainers will likely join you even if they’ve never met you before (it is possible to lose access to the coordinator option): Ace Trainer - You may call upon regionally famous gym leaders, elites, brains or any other famous and powerful trainers to aid you in your efforts in a competition or just for an exhibition match. Breeder - You have access to a regional list of breeders for rare or expensive Pokémon species and can arrange appointments free of charge for your Pokémon to produce eggs with any regionally available Pokémon. Coordinator (only) - As an exclusive coordinator, you have woven your ties in deep throughout your regional community. When joining a contest, you are made aware of any judges and you know what at least one Star Point category is per judge. Ranger - You have access to the captains of the regional ranger union. You can call upon their personal help in any dangerous situations or use your influence to rally many civilians to aid in ranger efforts with little effort. Researcher - You have access to any regional professors and doctors who will meet with you, plan joint research endeavors, and even research things for you (within reason) free of charge.

features.name: Stirring Speech
features.description: When you lead a positively powerful speech, you encourage everyone to get up and finish what they started. 1/day, you may spend 2 mins encouraging your allies. All allies, trainer and Pokémon alike, are healed of any afflictions, then at the start of their next combat encounter, they gain 10 temporary hit points.

features.name: On the List
features.description: By virtue of being who you are, most people will believe you are supposed to be where you say you’re supposed to be, doing what you say you’re supposed to be doing. When making a Bluff skill check, you may roll three times and use the best result. As long as your perform well enough on your skill check, only a person in charge of an entire organization might disagree with your behavior and expose you.

features.name: Platinum Cheer
features.description: You raise a wild energy around you when cheering on your friends’ efforts, making them believe anything is possible! 1/day, as an action, you give an energetic cheer that empowers all allies. For 10 mins, all allies deal +X damage when attacking, all allied skill checks add +2 to their roll, all skill checks made against your allies are -2 during any foe’s roll, and all allies recover X hit points, then gain X temporary hit points. X is equal to your Special Defense or Speed modifier.

features.name: Disheartening Blow
features.description: It’s very unkind and probably beneath you but your presence can be demoralizing when you pair it with a nasty insult. 3/day you may use Vicious Insult. Vicious Insult - 3/day Ranged(25ft) Dark Effect. On hit, the target is Dazed. Then, after the target’s is no longer Dazed they are Confused. Then after they are no longer Confused, they are Dazed one more time. [Special] If you have not spent at least 3 minutes with the target, you have -6 during AC. Sound.

features.name: Empowering Aid
features.description: Your friends are amazing and your friendships are supportive and powerful. When making a skill check, one of your allies can use an action to add their highest modifier to your skill check. When an ally is making a skill check, you may use an action to add your Special Defense or Speed modifier +3 to their skill check.

features.name: Preposterous Wealth
features.description: You’re on top of the world and have many fanatic followers from all over the planet. Your wealth is a non-issue due to your countless endorsements and sponsorships so if something is sold somewhere, you can afford it. You can give money in exchange for goods, but your endorsement and a quick selfie for a store’s wall is usually enough. The limitations of what you’re allowed to obtain/purchase is any kind of Pokémon that are in some way unusual due to being shiny, a strange typing, or having some other oddity about them. You also cannot buy something that is not for sale, for example if a Master Ball is not being sold because it’s a prototype, a collection piece, or out of stock you wouldn’t be able to buy it. If a Pokémon is precious to a trainer, you can’t just take it. Even then, if someone is selling a shiny Pokémon, you can have it, or you could commission a talented smith to create a Master Ball over time. In addition, any Rising Star feature that is limited by regional fame is now expanded to a global range.

name: Ranger
flavorText:
Protector, Servant, Leader
 As the guardians of the Pokémon world’s natural 
spaces, Rangers serve and protect Pokémon, putting 
themselves on the line. Rangers are skilled acrobats, 
navigating all sorts of terrain in order to rescue anyone or 
any Pokémon in need and use their focus and trusty styler 
to harness the help of wild Pokémon, enabling a ranger to 
solve any problem and overcome any obstacle even when 
outnumbered.

features.name: Authority Figure
features.description: Rangers are protectors of the Pokémon world, acting as an intermediary for humans and Pokémon alike and coming to the aid of anyone in need results in a certain attitude from the general public. When making Diplomacy checks, you have advantage. You work with and are generally respected by other Rangers. When requesting assistance from a local Ranger station on an important issue, the station is obligated to lend help in some form except for in extraordinary circumstances.

features.name: Befriend
features.description: A Ranger’s styler isn’t just a symbol of authority, it’s a valuable tool used to work with wild Pokémon and help your causes. 3/day, as an action, a non-agitated wild Pokémon within 25ft becomes Helpful. This Helpful Pokémon will remain under your guidance until the Helpful Pokémon is hit by an attack, severely distracted, or has helped you in a significant manner once, such as by making an attack. The wild Pokémon will act, moving or attacking when you issue it a command during your turn. You do not get a list of any Skills or moves you cannot deduce yourself, and it cannot be taken from the area you found it in or it will run away. You may only have one Helpful Pokémon at a time. In addition, when using Pokémon Handling, you may add your Defense or Speed modifier to your skill check instead of your Special Defense modifier.

features.name: Companion
features.description: After finding a valuable ally, the Ranger may promote a wild and make them a fellow defender of the Pokémon world. 1/day, make a Helpful Pokémon your Companion. You may only have one Companion at a time. If you give a new Pokémon the Companion title, you free your previous Companion and replace it with your new one. This process makes your Companion Pokémon have at least loyalty 2. Your Companion Pokémon will be obedient towards the Ranger, regardless of circumstances before being restrained. The Companion Pokémon cannot participate in official battles or contests. The Pokémon cannot be returned to a Poke Ball. Companions are considered Helpful, but act in combat as if they were owned. Companion Pokémon who are replaced by a new Companion Pokémon are still wild and will likely return to the wild. You may have a Companion Pokémon and a Helpful Pokémon at the same time. In addition, you may now use your Befriend feature 5/day.

features.name: Stat Increase and Advanced Class
features.description: Choose two different Trainer Stats to increase by 1, then gain 1d4 max HP. You only gain new stats at levels 3, 7, and 11. Choose a Ranger Advanced Class or a different base Class. You can only ever gain a single Class or Advanced Class at a time, when leveling up.

features.name: Dizzy
features.description: Using a stylist with some extra effort lets you disorient Pokémon. 3/day, you may use the attack Stylish Spin. Stylish Spin - 3/day Ranged(10ft) Normal Effect. On hit, the target is Confused.

features.name: Part of the Team
features.description: After working with your companion for some time, they’ll smoothly transition onto your team. If you’ve been with your Companion Pokémon for at least three days, you may capture it without having to roll a capture roll.

features.name: Safe Passage
features.description: Rangers find a way to navigate safely in the wild so as not to disturb any wilds. When traveling in the wild out of combat, you have advantage while making Acrobatics, Athletics, Investigate, Perception, or Stealth checks.

features.name: Stat Increase and Advanced Class
features.description: Choose two different Trainer Stats to increase by 1, then gain 1d4 max HP. You only gain new stats at levels 3, 7, and 11. Choose a Ranger Advanced Class or a different base Class. You can only ever gain a single Class or Advanced Class at a time, when leveling up.

features.name: Ward
features.description: Wild Pokémon going on rampages aren’t unheard of and it’s a Ranger’s duty to stop them before anyone gets hurt, including the rampaging Pokémon. 3/day, you may use Befriend on a wild Pokémon even if it is aggressive or rampaging. When you do, it is temporarily pacified and immediately ceases combat, then behaves as a normal Helpful Pokémon. In addition, you may now use your Befriend feature 7/day.

features.name: Herder
features.description: It’s not easy, but by using your styler to restrain multiple wilds, you can control more of them to aid you in your fight to protect the world. Using your Befriend feature, you may have up to two Helpful Pokémon at the same time in addition to a Companion Pokémon.

features.name: Aid of the Wild
features.description: When working to save the Pokémon world, friendly Pokémon can follow your lead with little direction. 3/day, for a number of rounds equal to your Defense or Speed modifiers, a chosen Helpful Pokémon acts on its own in combat, attacking foes or helping to complete a task without requiring orders. The GM controls the Helpful Pokémon under the effect of this feature. The target does not flee or retreat if injured while under the effects of this feature like another Helpful Pokémon.

features.name: Stat Increase and Advanced Class
features.description: Choose two different Trainer Stats to increase by 1, then gain 1d4 max HP. You only gain new stats at levels 3, 7, and 11. Choose a Ranger Advanced Class or a different base Class. You can only ever gain a single Class or Advanced Class at a time, when leveling up.

features.name: Styler Slinger
features.description: Throwing your styler around skillfully has become second nature. As an action, you can use Befriend twice during your turn. You can also use Ward and Befriend as a single action during your turn. If you use Befriend or Ward with your Styler Slinger feature, you still deplete their uses per day. In addition, you may now use your Befriend feature 9/day.

features.name: Natural Leader
features.description: Working with wild Pokémon and studying them has led to a natural well of knowledge- you just know how to work with Pokémon that you lasso with you stylist. You know of any special skills, moves, or unusual typing a wild you’ve made into a Helpful Pokémon. In addition, Helpful Pokémon are only dismissed once you dismiss them (usually Helpful Pokémon are dismissed after being hit by an attack, severely distracted, or after helping you in a significant manner once). You may not force Helpful Pokémon to leave their homes, only your Companion can leave wild areas with you.

features.name: Wild Commander
features.description: Serving the world of Pokémon comes with special responsibilities, but successfully protecting both people and Pokémon alike until renowned carries a sort of aura that makes wild Pokémon join your cause. You may use Befriend as many times as you’d like per day, and you may use Ward up to 7/day. In addition, using your Befriend feature, you may have up to three Helpful Pokémon at the same time in addition to a Companion Pokémon.

features.name: Commander’s Rally
features.description: After serving the world of Pokémon for a long enough time, your presence alone inspires greatness. 1/day, as a free action, all allied trainers and allied Pokémon within 30ft of you get +3 to their Attack, Defense, Special Attack, Special Defense and Speed for X rounds of combat, where X is your Defense or Speed modifier.

name: Invoker
flavorText:
The power of legendary Pokémon imbued in your styler.
 An invoker practices the use of guardian symbols to 
summon forth the power of legendary Pokémon. While 
invokers may not have ever met a legendary or mythical 
Pokémon, they draw forth power by drawing elaborate 
and precise sigils that through the magic of legendary 
Pokémon, manifest in amazing ways.

features.name: Courageous Sign
features.description: The first sign that an Invoker learns to create is the symbol of the legendary beasts, encouraging Pokémon to help. 3/day, when a Helpful Pokémon is dismissed after performing a task for you, you may make it Helpful again as a free action.

features.name: Guardian Sign
features.description: The second sign is the symbol of your legendary protector, helping to defend Pokémon who are in need of aid. 1/day you can use Guardian Sign. Guardian Sign - 1/day Ranged(25ft) Normal Effect. Reaction [Your Pokémon, your Helpful Pokémon, or your Companion Pokémon is hit by an attack]. That Pokémon takes 25 less damage. A Pokémon protected that way remains Helpful even if it lost HP from the attack.

features.name: Valiant Sign
features.description: Signing the symbol of the legendary swords of justice empowers your Pokémon. 3/day, as an action, you can use Boost Sign. Boost Sign - 3/day Ranged(20ft) Normal Effect. The target gets Attack▲ and SpAttack▲.

features.name: Sturdy Sign
features.description: The sign of the legendary golems helps to maintain a Pokémon’s will to keep helping you. 3/day, when a Helpful Pokémon is dismissed by getting attacked by a foe, you may make it Helpful again as a free action.

features.name: Soaring Sign
features.description: The sign of the legendary birds temporarily grants a Pokémon the ability to fly in the air. 3/day, as an action you may target one of your Pokémon, your Helpful Pokémon, or your Companion Pokémon and it is granted wings made of light so it can fly at its regular speed for ten minutes.

features.name: Healing Sign
features.description: Signing the symbol of the legendary guardian deities restores the strength of a Pokémon in need. 3/day, as an action, you can use Life Sign. Life Sign - 3/day Ranged(20ft) Fairy Effect. Heal the target 15 HP.

features.name: Swift Sign
features.description: By quickly signing the symbol of the legendary eon duo, you speed up your Companion. 3/day, as an action, your Companion can be issued a command letting them act on the same turn as another one of your Pokémon or Helpful Pokémon who is also being issued a command.

features.name: Dark Sign
features.description: The sign of the legendary Pokémon of darkness is used to ward off threats. 3/day, you can use Dark Sign. Dark Sign - 3/day Ranged(20ft) Dark Effect. On hit, the target is Drowsy.

features.name: Weather Sign
features.description: By signing the symbol of the legendary forces of nature, you summon a change of weather. 3/day you can use one of the following moves: Defog, Hail, Haze, Mist, Rain Dance, Sandstorm, Snowscape, or Sunny Day. Defog - 3/day Flying Field Effect. Any Hazards, Weather, or Terrains within 30ft are destroyed. Hail - 3/day Ice Field Effect. You create a circle of Hailing Weather with a 60ft diameter. Haze - 3/day Ice Field Effect. You create a circle of Hazy Weather with a 60ft diameter. Mist - 3/day Ice Field Effect. You create a circle of Misty Weather with a 60ft diameter. Rain Dance - 3/day Water Field Effect. You create a circle of Raining Weather with a 60ft diameter. Sandstorm - 3/day Rock Field Effect. You create a circle of Sandstorming Weather with a 60ft diameter. Wind. Snowscape - 3/day Ice Field Effect. You create a circle of Snowing Weather with a 60ft diameter. Sunny Day - 3/day Fire Field Effect. You create a circle of Sunny Weather with a 60ft diameter.

features.name: Decisive Sign
features.description: The symbol of the legendary lake guardians imbues Pokémon with an aura of protection. 3/ day, as an action, you can use Shield Sign. Shield Sign - 3/day Ranged(20ft) Normal Effect. The target gets Defense▲▲ and SpDefense▲▲.

features.name: Smiting Sign
features.description: Calling forth the symbol of the legendary Tao trio, you loose a bolt of energy from your styler. 3/ day, you can use Smite. Smite - 3/day Special Ranged(30ft): 3d8. Smite uses your Special Defense or Speed modifier during AC and damage. Smite cannot be resisted, nor can a target be immune to it. After use, you may not use Invoker features for 1 min.

features.name: Divine Sign
features.description: Signing the symbol of the legendary creator, your Pokémon brings out dormant power within. 1/day, your Pokémon or your Companion Pokémon uses Divine Verdict. Then, you may not use Invoker features for 5 mins. Divine Verdict – 1/day Special Ranged(30ft): [Variable] 4d10. Divine Verdict’s type matches one of you Companion’s types. Divine Verdict uses your Special Defense or Speed modifier during AC and damage After use, you may not use Invoker features for 5 mins.

name: Officer
flavorText:
Gumshoe rangers on the beat. 
 Officers are often more concerned with the city limits 
and making sure that people are just as safe from the 
wilds as they are from each other. Paying close attention 
to the human world around them gives them leads, 
pressing suspicious individuals leads to shadowy 
organizations, and pursuing threads of conspiracies can 
help to take down major threats to the Pokémon world.

features.name: Conspiracy Catcher
features.description: The world of Pokémon is not short of criminal activity and you have a knack for overcoming anyone who’d looking to start trouble for others. Whenever you make a Skill check while confronting or battling any criminal or criminal suspect, add +1 to your rolls. In addition, when using an Insight check against these individuals, you may add your Defense or Speed modifier to your skill check instead of your Special Defense modifier.

features.name: Intuition’s Arsenal
features.description: Officers who serve both city and wild have picked up natural tendencies to remain even more vigilant than other Rangers. You gain the following passive abilities; Infiltrator, Inner Focus, Insomnia, and Keen Eye. Infiltrator (Hindering terrain and Hazards do not affect your accuracy during attacks.) Inner Focus (You are immune to being Dazed.) Insomnia (You are immune to being Drowsy.) Keen Eye (Your accuracy checks cannot be negatively affected by foes.)

features.name: Detective Training
features.description: Keeping on the lookout is tiring, but with some basic training your companion has got your back. After spending one hour with your Companion, they gain the Skills Stealth and Tracker. Your Companion loses these Skills when they are no longer your Companion unless they become your Pokémon. Stealth – Not all Pokémon are allowed to make a stealth check. With stealth, Pokémon may roll a stealth check like a human trainer, adding their Speed modifier, calculated like a human’s, to see if they can silently move during or outside of battle without being detected. (can make stealth skill checks) Tracker - Pokémon with the skill tracker have a strong sense of smell that they can use to follow other Pokémon or people using a Investigate skill check, adding their Special Attack modifier. If the Pokémon has smelled whom they want to track in the past day, or one of their personal belongings, they can pursue that prey with a skill check of 11 or better. To pick up a random scent from nothing, a skill check of 16 or better will allow the Pokémon to follow that scent. To pick up a specific scent from nothing, a skill check of 20 will allow the Pokémon to follow that scent. A Pokémon may only make these checks once per hour. (can follow scents)

features.name: Partner’s Aid
features.description: Your companion has taken a liking to police work and will help any way it can to succeed in bringing down criminals. If your Conspiracy Catcher feature is applicable to a Skill check and your Companion Pokémon is within 10ft of you, add +4 to your Skill Check.

features.name: Disguise
features.description: Sometimes, it’s better if you don’t look like a Ranger. After ten minutes of work, you are unrecognizable unless you reveal who you are to someone else or if they observed you disguising yourself. Your Pokémon, Helpful Pokémon, and Companion Pokémon can recognize you. You may not impersonate anyone with Disguise.

features.name: Stop Right There
features.description: When you’ve got a criminal in your sights, you’ll do everything in your power to apprehend them. While chasing a foe, you may move an additional 20ft per round of combat and you gain +4 while making Acrobatics skill checks.

features.name: Lie Detector
features.description: Catching criminals has revealed various tells that help you understand truth from falsehood. When making Insight skill checks, you have advantage. In addition, if you’ve talked to anyone for more than two minutes, you can tell if they are lying to you.

features.name: Intuition Training
features.description: Your companion has picked up on many of your mannerisms and natural tendencies- after a good training session. After spending three hours with your Companion, they are treated as if they have the following passive abilities; Infiltrator, Inner Focus, Insomnia, and Keen Eye. They do not actually have the passives, but they benefit from their effects as if they have them.

features.name: Restraining Order
features.description: Maneuvering wilds with your styler can help you stop any criminal who might try to get away. 3/day, you may issue a command to any of your Pokémon, your Helpful Pokémon, or your Companion Pokémon to use the move Block. Helpful Pokémon are not compelled to leave your service until Block’s effect ends. Block - At-Will Melee Normal Effect. Stance: Enemies that move into any adjacent space immediately stop moving and enemies who were adjacent to you then moved away from you stop moving after 10ft.

features.name: Master of Disguise
features.description: You’ve studied the trade of infiltration and would say that you’ve mastered impersonation. After one hour of work, you may disguise yourself as a specific person, Pokémon, or even an inanimate object of your size and be unrecognizable as a fake to the eyes of everyone around you. Your voice passes if you succeed a Bluff skill check, but you have advantage during Bluff skill checks while disguised as someone else.

features.name: What’s That Over There
features.description: Misdirection often lets you get by pesky guards, nosy bystanders, or shady civilians and investigate in unorthodox ways. 3/day, you may distract a target human or Pokémon with a trick or a menial chore for X minutes, where X is equal to your Defense or Speed modifier. The target is compelled to complete whatever task you convince them to do. If they become distracted by something other than you or your chore, or are otherwise alerted, they will stop whatever it is they were doing earlier than normal, if not immediately.

features.name: Ultimate Interrogator
features.description: Through whatever means you’ve developed, you’re able to break open any locked lips and find out what you need in order to nab your criminal quarry. After spending twenty minutes with your Companion and a captured criminal foe, they will answer questions you have of them truthfully and as detailed as possible. Ultimate Interrogation must be used in a relatively private space, such as a questioning room in a Ranger Station or a room in a private residence.

name: Rider
flavorText:
Acrobatic prowess on mounts keeps you right in the 
action.
 Riders have mastered their balance and handling to 
stay on top of battle while also managing other trainer’s 
rides and keeping their team in a uniform herd through 
the battlefield. They have a natural way about finding the 
best ways to stay on mounts and keep engaged in the 
action while impressing everyone with their style.

features.name: Battle Capable Riding
features.description: Using a mount in combat means you’re a part of combat, but your Pokémon’s got you covered. Whenever you are hit by an attack while mounted, your mount may automatically intercept the hit as a free action and take the hit for you. If you would have both been hit, only your mount takes damage. Whenever your mount intercepts damage for you, you gain 1 Momentum.

features.name: Mounted Maneuvers
features.description: You’re a natural Pokémon rider and know all the tricks to stay on your mount when riding. As you move around on your mount, you can gain up to 3 Momentum at a time. If you are at rest for more than a minute, you lose your Momentum. Whenever your mount moves as least 20ft during your their actions without turning more than once, you gain 1 Momentum. At any time, you may spend Momentum to do the following maneuvers. 1 Momentum Each: - You automatically succeed on all checks to remain on your mount caused by attacks and status conditions. - You can ride your mounts on their side, while hanging upside down from them, while standing on them, or any other odd way of staying on your mount as if you are riding the mount as normal. - Add another +10ft of movement to your mount’s turn.

features.name: All-Terrain Pokémon
features.description: With careful guidance, you’ve trained your Pokémon to navigate anything from rocky crag or oil-slicked streets. When mounted on one of your Pokémon or your Companion Pokémon, treat all ground terrain as normal terrain. Your All-Terrain Pokémon feature doesn’t work if your mount can’t swim and is in or under water. Whenever one of your mounts ignore difficult terrain for the first time each combat, you gain 1 Momentum.

features.name: Mount Mobility
