features.description: You move as one with your Pokémon and often act in battle simultaneously. At any time, you may spend Momentum to do the following maneuvers. 1 Momentum Each: - Instead of using your Speed to determine your turn order during combat, you may choose to use your mount’s Speed. - If you start your turn adjacent to a foe, your mount can make its attack and then move 15ft.

features.name: Full Speed
features.description: By encouraging your Pokémon, you fly ahead at amazing speeds. The first time your mount acts first during a round per combat, you gain 1 Momentum. At any time, you may spend Momentum to do the following maneuvers. 2 Momentum Each: - As an action, your Pokémon or Companion Pokémon who you are mounted on get Speed▲▲. - Add another +25ft of movement to your mount’s turn. - Wall ride up to 30ft (figure out how to safely return to the ground without falling or risk you and your mount taking damage).

features.name: Mounted Quick Switch
features.description: Training and practice has led to an amazing maneuver allowing you make a small jump in order to change your mounted Pokémon without a moment between. You can switch out Pokémon you are mounted on to another Pokémon in your Poke Balls without dismounting by placing the new Pokémon in the exact place as a Pokémon you are returning, even if your mount is in motion. You may even switch the type of mount while it is moving (sky to land, sea to sky, etc.). You can even do this as a Pokémon you are on is knocked out. Whenever you do, you gain 1 Momentum.

features.name: Ride Pager
features.description: With little effort you can find wilds willing to help you get to where you need to be. While in wild territory you can spend twenty minutes to find a Pokémon who can serve as a mount for yourself or an allied trainer. Once Helpful, the Pokémon will allow itself to be ridden for up to 8 hours or until it has been hit by an attack or given another command that would dismiss it. Additionally, allied trainer’s Pokémon and Helpful Pokémon are treated as your own Pokémon and Companion Pokémon for the purposes of using Rider features.

features.name: Watch and Learn
features.description: By using your styler to steer another Pokémon, you can handle Pokémon you aren’t even riding as well as you handle your own. As long as they are within 10ft of you, you can spend Momentum to give effects to your allies who are also on mounts.

features.name: Charge
features.description: While maneuvering your Pokémon, nothing can stop your advance. As an action, you may spend 2 Momentum if you maneuver a Pokémon you are mounted on through a space occupied by any enemy Pokémon, to have your mount use Charge on Through. You may still make another attack with your mounted Pokémon at the end of their movement. Additonally, as an action, you may spend 2 Momentum to use Submerge. Charge on Through - 2 Physical Normal: Normal 2d6. [Special] Charge on Through can only target enemies whose space you entered while moving this turn. Once per turn Charge On Through is a free action. Submerge - 2 Physical Normal: Normal 3d8. [Special] Submerge can only be used on mounts with Burrow (on land) or Swimmer (in water at least 5ft deep). Submerge has Turns. [Turn 1] Swim or burrow up to 40ft down. Until your next turn, you and your mount may not be targeted. [Turn 2] Return to the surface, move up to twice your speed +25ft, then you may roll Submerge’s AC and power.

features.name: Signature Riding
features.description: Your mounted expertise knows no bounds in air, land or sea. As you move around on your mount, you can now gain up to 5 Momentum at a time. At any time, you may spend Momentum to do the following maneuvers. 3 Momentum Each: - If someone tries to use a Reaction in response to your mount’s action, interrupt them and negate their Reaction. - If an ally within 15ft of you and your mount is about to take damage from a successful single-target attack, your mount may intercept the attack and take the damage and effects (this gains 1 Momentum).

features.name: Form Up
features.description: On your signal, your ally’s mounted Pokémon group up with you for better maneuvering and mounted combat at your lead. 3/day, you may use Form Up as your action in order to move all allied mounted Pokémon up to 25ft closer to you. Form Up does not take away those Pokémon’s ability to move during their turns. For each mounted ally who gets within 15ft of you after use, gain 1 Momentum.

features.name: Overrun
features.description: Ready to vanquish any opposition, you and your allies charge forward and destroy any obstacle. As an action, you may spend 3 Momentum, so that you, your mount, and each allied mounted Pokémon within 10ft moves forward with you while using your mounted Pokémon’s attack; Stampede. Stampede - 3 Physical Normal: Normal 3d12. Stampede has +1d12 power for every allied mounted Pokémon that is moving with you. [Special] Stampede can only be made against enemies that you passed through while moving during your turn. While moving with Stampede, it rolls an AC to hit every foe you and any allied mounted Pokémon moves through with you. If all mounted Pokémon moving with Stampede share a type, Stampede’s type may be changed from Normal to that type. Any Pokémon involved in making this attack may still use a move during their turn.

name: Special Operative
flavorText:
Protecting the Pokémon world by force.
 Gearing up for serious conflict and special missions 
requires a license to wield more complicated ranger gear 
that also comes with more responsibility. As a special 
operations member, rangers will be able to use all sorts of 
powerful tactical tools . Special operatives are sometimes 
looked on with caution and uncertainty by the general 
public– it’s your responsibility to prove yourself to the 
people you’ve sworn to protect.

features.name: Operation Gear I
features.description: When promoted to a special operative in the ranger union, you’re given access to the spec. ops. lockers and you may borrow any gear for yourself from any ranger station. At any time, you may have up to 3 Special Operative gear with you from a ranger station. In order to retrieve a new piece of gear, you can return and exchange Spec. Ops. gear at any Ranger stations. Gear is licensed to you and you’ll need to replace any damaged or stolen equipment which may result in disciplinary action from regional captains. As a newly appointed special operative, you have access to the following 5 pieces of equipment: Coiled Styler Attachment, Ranger’s Rebreather, Scanner, Shield Styler Attachment, and Trauma Suppression Kit.

features.name: Coiled Styler Attachment
features.description: In order to combat criminals who abuse Pokémon into doing their bidding, special stylers are issued to operatives that can be used to temporarily restrain owned Pokémon. 3/day, as an action, use Styler Wrap on an owned enemy Pokémon. Styler Wrap - 3/day Physical Melee: Normal 1d6. On hit, the target is Bound to you. If they are Bound in this way, they cannot move or use attacks unless they beat you in an Athletics skill check or target you with an attack. If you or the Bound target is attacked, the target is freed from Binding.

features.name: Ranger’s Rebreather
features.description: For special underwater missions, the rebreather is a valuable tool when a Pokémon can’t help to take you underwater for extended periods of time. The rebreather allows you to breathe underwater for a maximum of 1 hour. After the rebreather is used for at least half an hour, it must be cleaned and dried, rendering it unable to be used for 1 hour.

features.name: Scanner
features.description: Your specialized goggles help to assess situations when Pokémon are wreaking havoc. 5/day, as a free action, you may reveal target Pokémon’s current hit points as a percentage representing its amount of hit points out of its max hit points. In addition, the googles these scanners are attached to are able to see through fog, smoke, heavy sandstorm, or any other moving non-permanent visual obstruction.

features.name: Shield Styler Attachment
features.description: Sometimes the threat of attack will make you want to have a shield and this attachment expands a shield made of energy to help protect you from enemies. When you or an adjacent ally is attacked, the foe must roll +2 during AC in order to hit. If an opponent fails to hit after attacking you or an adjacent ally your energy shield shatters and must recharge for 1 min before it is reformed. You may not use the Shield Styler Attachment while using Wrap with the Coiled Styler Attachment.

features.name: Trauma Suppression Kit
features.description: In order to protect your allies, you carry a compact medical package stocked with fast-acting coagulants, stimulants, and status-neutralizing compounds approved by the Ranger Union for field use. 3/day, as an action, you may use the Trauma Suppression Kit on yourself or an adjacent ally. Choose one of the following effects: - The target regains HP equal to 1d6 + your Defense modifier - The target is cured of one of the following Afflictions: Burned, Poisoned, or Paralyzed

features.name: Endure
features.description: Special operatives often combat violent threats, so are trained to hold on whenever possible. 1/day, you may use Endure. Endure - 1/day Self Normal Effect. Reaction [When you are hit by an attack that would knock you out]. You are instead left with 1 HP.

features.name: Operation Gear II
features.description: Further promotion allows access to additional equipment within the ranger union. You may now have 4 pieces of Spec. Ops. gear from ranger stations at a time. You also now have access to the following 3 pieces of equipment: Grapple Line Launcher, Magna Capture Net, and Riot Gear.

features.name: Grapple Line Launcher
features.description: Urban environments, cliffside terrain, and fast-moving suspects often demand rapid re-positioning beyond what Pokémon allies alone can provide. Instead of moving, you may rapidly pull yourself toward an anchored surface up to 30ft away. Additionally, 3/day you can use Grapple Reel on a target. Grapple Reel - 3/day Ranged(30ft) Steel Effect. On hit, if the target is the same weight or lighter than you, pull the target to you. If the target is heavier than you, you may pull yourself to the target. If you are adjacent to one of your Pokémon or your Companion, you may include their weight when determining if you can pull your target to you. [Special] If you also have the Coiled Styler Attachment, you may immediately use Styler Wrap as a free action.

features.name: Magna Capture Net
features.description: Designed for the apprehension of highly mobile threats, the Magna Capture Net deploys a weighted, magnetized mesh that rapidly collapses around a target. 3/day, as an action, use Magna Launcher on a target. Magna Launcher - 3/day Ranged(25ft) Steel Effect. On hit, the target gets a Magna Coat with the following effect: “You may not use Flight skills, you may not climb or jump, and your movement Speed is -10ft. You may destroy this Coat on a Athletics skill check of 15 or higher with disadvantage. This Coat is destroyed if you take more than 12 HP of damage in one round.”

features.name: Riot Gear
features.description: If you’re looking for a fight and don’t mind looking like it, armor up in some riot gear. When taking damage from Physical attacks, take 4 less damage.

features.name: Take Down
features.description: Sometimes a reckless tackle is the most reliable tool at your disposal. 3/day, as an action, you may use Take Down. If you are wearing Riot Gear, ignore the move’s effect “On hit, you lose 3d8 HP.” Take Down - 3/day Physical Melee: Normal 3/day 3d10. On hit, you lose 3d8 HP.

features.name: Element of Surprise
features.description: By planning stings and operations in order to maximize chances of success without any harm coming to your allies, you’ve figured out the best means of attack in any given situation. During an ambush, where you and your allies are attacking before being spotted by any enemies, all allies deal +5 damage on hit.

features.name: Operation Gear III
features.description: Further promotion allows access to additional equipment within the ranger union. You may still only have 4 pieces of Spec. Ops. gear from ranger stations at a time. You also now have access to the following 3 pieces of equipment: Control Tactical Launcher - Smoke, Stun, and Weather Suppression. Your newest equipment are launchers that use Ammunition. For each of those pieces of equipment, the Ranger Union allows Spec. Ops. rangers to take three canisters of Ammunition for each launcher and you must return to a ranger station in order to retrieve more after using any Ammunition. Each launcher has its own separate counts of Ammunition. Control Tactical Launcher - Smoke: Smokescreens can be useful to protect yourself and allies while making a quick get away and can cover your escape, or during an offensive raid. As an action, use the move Smoke Launcher. Uses Ammunition. Smoke Launcher - 3/day Ranged(25ft, 20ft blast) Normal Effect. Place Smokescreen Hazard in the targeted area. Moves made into or out of the the Smokescreen Hazard have disadvantage. Control Tactical Launcher - Stun: While not always effective, stun powder grenades can be useful when trying to settle a dangerous situation through force. As an action, use the move Stun Gas. Uses Ammunition. Stun Gas - 3/day Ranged(25ft, 20ft blast) Normal Effect. Place Stunscreen Hazard in the targeted area. Movement into Stunscreen Hazard stops movement for that turn. Movement that starts in Stunscreen Hazard is reduced to 20ft at most. Control Tactical Launcher - Weather Suppression: Uncontrolled weather effects, whether caused by rogue Pokémon, malicious interference, or environmental instability, can rapidly escalate an already dangerous situation. As an action, use the move Defogging Blast. Uses Ammunition. Defogging Blast - 3/day Ranged(25ft, 20ft blast) Flying Effect. Any Hazards, Weather, or Terrains within range are destroyed.

features.name: Retaliate
features.description: A burst of adrenaline can hit you when you see a teammate going down and you’ve learned to channel that surge into a powerful show of force. 1/day, as an action, you may use Retaliate. Retaliate - 1/day Physical Melee: Normal 4d10. Reaction [When an ally is defeated by a foe]: Move 30ft, then if the same foe who defeated your ally is within range, immediately attack and hit them without AC, with Retaliate.

features.name: Creative Application
features.description: Using the tools given to you by the ranger union, you’ve developed unorthodox means of applying their use against enemies of the Pokémon world. Your Ranger Equipment have the following upgrades:

features.name: Coiled Styler Attachment
features.description: 3/day, you, you may use the move Slash as an action. Slash - 3/day Physical Melee: Normal 3d8. Slash is Lethal.

features.name: Ranger’s Rebreather
features.description: Now lasts for 2 hour and can be cleaned and ready to use again in 15 minutes.

features.name: Scanner
features.description: The scanner can be used as night-vision or no-light goggles. Additionally, You may use the move Foresight as an action. Foresight - At-Will Self Normal Effect. Stance: You ignore Ghost-type immunities.

features.name: Shield Styler Attachment
features.description: 3/day, you may use the move Barrier as an action. Barrier - 3/day Self Psychic Effect: Stance: When an enemy hits you, or an ally adjacent to you, with a Physical move, take -8 damage from the attack.

features.name: Grapple Line Launcher
features.description: 1/day, you may use the move Zip Line as an action. Zip Line - 1/day Ranged(30ft) Steel Effect. Reaction [You are hit by a melee attack]. Immediately pull yourself 15ft toward an anchored surface. The attack misses you.

features.name: Magna Capture Net
features.description: 1/day, you may use the move Magna Lock as an action. Magna Lock - 1/day Ranged(25ft) Steel Effect. On hit, the target and a foe adjacent to the target become Bound to each other and fall to the ground, then becomes Bound to that spot. Either foe may escape on a Athletics skill check of 15 or higher with disadvantage. Both are freed of binding if either takes more than 12 HP of damage in one round.

features.name: Riot Gear
features.description: Now, when taking damage from Physical attacks, take 8 less damage. Additionally, when at a Ranger Station, you can modify your Riot Gear by choosing a type. While using your Riot Gear, you resist attacks of that type.

features.name: Operation Gear IV
features.description: Further promotion allows access to additional equipment within the ranger union. You may now have 5 pieces of Spec. Ops. gear from ranger stations at a time. You also now have access to the following 5 pieces of equipment: Suppression Tactical Launcher – Disable, EMP, Foam, Sonic, and Web. Your newest equipment are also launchers that use Ammunition. Each launcher has its own separate counts of Ammunition. Suppression Tactical Launcher – Disable: Reserved for high-risk engagements, this launcher disperses a precision-engineered interference charge that disrupts a Pokémon’s combat instincts and muscle memory. As an action, use the move Compliance Field. Uses Ammunition. Compliance Field - 3/day Ranged(25ft, 20ft burst) Steel Effect. Create a Compliance Hazard in the targeted area. 3/day and 1/day frequency moves cannot be used by Pokémon within the Compliance Hazard . Suppression Tactical Launcher – EMP: Issued to deal with advanced equipment or technologically augmented threats, this launcher deploys a controlled electromagnetic discharge designed to neutralize electronic systems without causing permanent damage. As an action, use the move System Shutdown. Uses Ammunition. System Shutdown - 3/day Ranged(25ft, 20ft burst) Electric Effect. In the targeted area, create a Shutdown Hazard . Any electronic equipment within the Hazard is disabled for 15 minutes (even if the Hazard is destroyed, the equipment with still be disabled). This does not effect Poké Balls. After those 15 minutes end, the equipment can be rebooted with no damage to it provided no physical harm was done to it. Suppression Tactical Launcher – Foam: Developed for containment and area denial, this deploys a rapidly expanding suppression foam that hardens on contact with terrain and obstacles. As an action, use the move Adhesive Field. Uses Ammunition. Adhesive Field - 3/day Ranged(25ft, 20ft burst) Water Effect. In the targeted area, move all targets (up to heavy) away outwards from the center of the targeted area. The targeted area becomes Glue Hazard , which is a mound of blocking terrain that is 15ft at its highest in its center. The Hazard is sticky, making it difficult terrain to traverse. While expanding, the foam will not destroy other blocking terrain, or move heavyweight targets. Instead, it will seal rooms and form around other objects it cannot move. The entire half-sphere of Hazard has 50 HP. [Special] If an effect that destroys Hazards targets the Glue Hazard , the it loses 30 HP instead of automatically being destroyed. . Suppression Tactical Launcher – Sonic: Designed for rapid crowd control, this launcher emits a precisely tuned sonic barrage that overwhelms balance, spatial awareness, and auditory processing. As an action, use the move Acoustic Interference. Uses Ammunition. Sonic Scramble - 3/day Ranged(25ft, 20ft burst) Normal Effect. On hit, all targets are Confused. Suppression Tactical Launcher – Web: This device uses ammunition developed with different products made by Pokémon to hinder the escape of any fleeing criminals. As an action, use the move Spider Webbing. Uses Ammunition. Spider Webbing - 3/day Ranged(20ft) Bug Effect. On hit, the target is Bound in place for 1d4 turns.

features.name: Adrenaline Response
features.description: All of your of high-risk operations have trained you to push past pain and keep fighting to protect others. 1/day, when you would be lowered to half of your max HP or less, immediately recover 15 HP as a free action.

features.name: Quartermaster
features.description: Once appointed the rank of Quartermaster, the Ranger Union assumes your knowledge and responsibility of the use and distribution of advanced Special Operative gear. You may check out and borrow up to 10 different Special Operative gear pieces at a time. Only yourself and other Rangers may use anything you’ve checked out during any given mission and you are responsible for the return of all equipment borrowed by non-Special Operative Rangers.

name: Survivalist
flavorText:
Living in nature has never been so easy.
 A survivalist could disappear into the wilds and 
comfortably live out the rest of their lives in nature. These 
rangers still serve the world they live in but have 
dedicated themselves to preserving the wilds and keeping 
away those who might encroach onto a Pokémon's 
territory or damage the natural spaces around the world.

features.name: Food Scavenger
features.description: Studying nature has led to a knack for surviving in it. After spending twenty minutes in natural, non-artificial terrain, you find enough food and water for a whole day for up to seven humans and/or Pokémon. As long as the terrain is not ecologically spoiled or heavily disrupted, you may use this feature any number of times per day. If the terrain is spoiled, you may only use this feature 1/day.

features.name: Internalized Senses
features.description: Leaving civilization for days at a time is a lot safer now that you have a natural tendency to explore the wild. At any time, you can discern the direction you are facing. You know a complete forecast of the day’s natural weather. You know a rough estimate of the time of day, to the nearest quarter of an hour. In addition, when using Nature, you may add your Defense or Speed modifier to your skill check instead of your Special Attack modifier.

features.name: Freeclimbing
features.description: Overcoming any terrain is a requirement for a ranger so well versed in the wilds of the world. You do not need to make any Skill checks to navigate any natural, non-artificial terrain, and are not hindered by hindering terrain while moving through such terrain.

features.name: Watch the Sky
features.description: Weather can be bad for different reasons, but careful planning helps you and your Pokémon get through the worst nature can throw at you. Your Pokémon, Helpful Pokémon, and Companion Pokémon are treated as if they have the Overcoat passive ability. In addition, you can tell if wild Pokémon nearby have any way to change the weather through the use of moves, passives, or other abilities. Overcoat (You are immune to damage from Weather.)

features.name: Pacifier
features.description: Using your styler to help the wilds comes naturally and easily when you’re not working to fight against another Pokémon. Whenever a Helpful Pokémon leaves your care after aiding you, if you did not give it a command to use an attack at another Pokémon you get back one of your uses per day of Befriend or Ward, depending on how you made that Pokémon Helpful.

features.name: Natural Camouflage
features.description: You are adept at concealing yourself and your campsite in the wild. After spending 1 hour in natural, non-artificial terrain, you gain advantage on Stealth checks as long as you remain in the area. Additionally, while in such an area, you may spend an hour to may build a camouflaged shelter using materials from your surroundings large enough to house up to five Trainers. When you do, make a Stealth check. The result of your check may be used by those within, and characters outside the campsite must beat your check result to find it. Wild Pokémon do not treat these sites as intrusions and will ignore them unless directly provoked. These sites begin to fall apart after 24 hours without your presence.

features.name: Fieldcraft
features.description: You can build what you need and can solve countless problems with what the wilds provide to you. After spending time in natural, non-artificial terrain, you can create the following items out of natural materials you gather: 30 min craft time: - Alarm Trap: 20ft of tripwire that is covered in noise-making objects that rattles, snaps, or clangs loudly when anything passes through it. You could string multiple lines together provided you have crafted more. Once set off, it breaks (You must have made 40ft of light rope to make this). - Anti-Venom Salve: As an action, cures Poisoned or Toxified. Goes bad after one week. - Ball Bearings (Stone): Three stone marbles. For creating distractions, triggering traps, tripping up others, and all other kinds of mischief. - Burn Salve: As an action, cures Burns. Goes bad after one week. - Drag Sled: An efficient sled that can hold a medium sized person easily for snow, sand, or even light-mud terrain. It falls apart after a 12 hours of use. - Drying Rack: Allows you to dry meat, herbs, or other goods safely. Doubles the shelf life of crafted food items made with it. - Field Rations: A single meal for anyone. Goes bad after one week. - Fish Hooks: Five crude hooks. Can be used with rope, string, or vine to fish for water-dwelling Pokémon. Each one breaks with successful use or cracks after one week. - Glue: 2 oz. Holds light to medium loads and can temporarily mend tools, equipment, or shelters. Hardens after one week without use. - Ice Crampons: For safe ice-covered travel. Falls apart after three days without 30 min maintenance. - Personal Care: Soaps, shampoos, toothpastes, and deodorants. Choose a specific hygienic gel, paste, or other bar to make. Each thing you make will have 4 uses before its depleted. - Pitons: Climbing anchors. You make two at a time, but they’re all one-time use. - Sand Shoes: For safe sand-covered travel. Falls apart after three days without 30 min maintenance. - Scent Mask: Leaves a natural smell in your wake while traveling the wilds for up to two hours. Goes bad after one week. - Snowshoes: For safe snow-covered travel. Falls apart after three days without 30 min maintenance. - Torch: Lights the way once set aflame. You make two at a time and they last for three hours. Falls apart without use after one week. - Trail Markers: Makes travel safer for others. You make three at a time. When placed, they give trainers traveling along your marked path advantage on Survival skill checks when they are within a quarter mile of your trail markers. Falls apart after one week. - Water Filter: Creates clean water from any water source, filters up to 5 gallons before breaking. - Writing Utensil: Made from chalk, graphite, charcoal, or maybe even a hollow stick with berry juice. You needed something to write with, after all. 1 hour craft time: - Bedroll: For keeping comfortable at night. Falls apart after three days without 1 hour maintenance. - Blanket: For keeping safely warm at night. Falls apart after three days without 1 hour maintenance. - Cold Storage Cache: A buried container that preserves food for up to four days. - Flotation Pack: Sealed reeds and other buoyant materials patched together. Keeps one Medium creature afloat in water for up to 1 hour. Falls apart after use or after one week without use. - Net Trap: A thin trip wire sets a large net that drops on anything who crosses. It takes 1 whole round to take the Net Trap off yourself. If the victim is medium or smaller, they make all actions at disadvantage and their movement speed is halved. If the victim is large, their movement is halved. If the victim is larger, they are unaffected (You must have made 60ft of heavy rope to make this). - Rope: Nature’s all-purpose tether. 40ft of light rope (half-inch diameter) or 20ft of heavy rope (2 inch diameter). - Signal Whistle: Emits a sharp sound audible up to 350ft in the wild. Cracks after one week. - Smokeless Fire: A campfire to keep warm without giving away your position. - Snare Trap: A thin rope and twig mechanism loops a passing victim. If the victim is medium or larger, they can escape with a medium difficulty strength check. If the victim is small and doesn’t have natural defenses to escape the trap they make all actions at disadvantage and are Bound. (You must have made 40ft of light rope to make this). - String: Thin rope. 60ft of string (1/20th inch diameter). - Type-Specific Repellent: A repellent that makes wild Pokémon stay away. When you make it, choose a type for the repellent to keep away. Wild Pokémon will keep away and avoid you while you use it, but may ignore the smell to protect something precious to them. The repellent works for three hours. Goes bad after one week. - Wild Poultice: As an action, heals 2 HP. Your poultices can only be used once per injury. For example, if someone you are using your poultice on has been attacked by three separate moves, you could use up to three Poultices on them. Goes bad after three days. - Windbreak Screen: A low barrier of woven natural materials that reduces the effects of strong winds and weather on creatures behind it. It lasts up to one day. - Water Collection System: Keeps water drinkable for up to one week without spoiling. Cracks after one week. - Waterskin: Keeps water drinkable for up to one week without spoiling. Cracks after one week. 2 hour craft time: - Brush Cloak: A many-layered cloak of leaves, fibers, and other natural materials. While wearing the cloak where it was made, trainers gain advantage on Stealth checks. The cloak lasts for two days without and hour of maintenance and falls apart if removed from the biome where it was built for more than a day. - Pacifying Sigil: A small carved or natural socket that you infuse with scents, symbols, and natural energy that encourages peace in the surrounding area. While placed above your campsite or resting spot, it reduces hostility from wild Pokémon within a 40ft radius for up to six hours. These only work in the wild space where they were made. While these will prevent hostility, a rampaging Pokémon may unknowingly approach without meaning to. Breaks after one use. - Stone Blade: A weapon to use carefully. You must maintain your blade for 30 mins a week or it breaks. As an action, you can use Knife Cut. Knife Cut - At-Will Melee: Normal 1d6. You have advantage while using Knife Cut. - Stone Hammer: A tool to use wisely. Your hammer is designed for heavy Fieldcraft projects and can eventually break with use. When crafting Fieldcraft items that require at least 2 hours, reduce the crafting time by 25%. After completing the craft, make a Nature check. On a result of 14 or higher, the Stone Hammer does not break. Otherwise, it breaks after use. You cannot use multiple Stone Hammers on Fieldcraft. - Stone Handaxe: A tool to use wisely. Your handaxe is designed for heavy Fieldcraft projects and can eventually break with use. When crafting Fieldcraft items that require at least 2 hours, reduce the crafting time by 25%. After completing the craft, make a Nature check. On a result of 14 or higher, the Stone Handaxe does not break. Otherwise, it breaks after use. You cannot use multiple Stone Handaxes on Fieldcraft. - Weather Cloak: A layered cloak designed to keep the wearer dry and insulated during travel in severe weather. Treat the wearer as if they have the passive Overcoat. This needs 1 hour of repair every three days or it breaks. 4 hour craft time: - Brush Pack: A backpack made from natural materials. When used in the biome it was created it, it does not stand out and will not negatively affect any Stealth skill check. You must spend an hour every three days maintaining it or it can fall apart. - Hidden Cache: A concealed storage compartment. It can be up to 3x3x3ft in size. Items stored are protected from scavengers and weather for up to four months without maintenance (unless you store some kind of food). The cache cannot be recognized except by humans standing immediately adjacent to it on a difficult Perception or Investigation skill check. - Pokémon Call Whistle: A wood or stone whistle, or other noisemaker, carved and tuned for a specific Pokémon call. It imitates a call you’ve heard before and can be heard for at least 100ft. Without half an hour of maintenance every week, it will crack and break. - Shortbow and Arrows: A weapon to use carefully. You can craft 6 arrows per hour. As an action, you can use Arrow Cut. Arrow Cut - 1 Arrow Ranged(30ft): Normal 1d6. You have advantage while using Arrow Cut. - Slingshot/Sling: A weapon to use carefully. You can craft 6 stone ball bearings per hour. As an action, you can use Sling Throw. Sling Throw - 1 Sling Rock Ranged(30ft): Rock 1d6. You have advantage while using Sling Throw. - Stone Whistle: A stone whistle carved and tuned for sharp, carrying notes. It can emit a piercing signal audible up to 500ft in natural terrain. Without half an hour of maintenance every week, it will crack and break. 8 hour craft time: - Observation Platform: An elevated perch built into trees, cliffs, or natural rises. It holds up to two trainers or medium sized Pokémon. While on the platform, you have advantage on Perception checks and cannot be surprised by non-Flying Pokémon approaching from ground level. The platform is naturally camouflaged and cannot be recognized except by creatures standing immediately adjacent to it. It remains intact for up to five days with maintenance. - Grappling Hook (Stone): Just the hook part. Sturdy enough, but still needs rope. - Mortar and Pestle: For easily making pastes, spices, and powders. Can be used for many things, but helps to make your slaves in 10 min instead of 30 min. - Paper: Natural paper made from scratch. Pretty thick and sturdy. 10 “sheets.” - Pickaxe (Stone): A pickaxe to help with digging, unfortunately it wears down quickly against other stone. - Shovel (Stone): An actual shovel, for your digging needs. - Wild Shelter: A semi-permanent shelter reinforced with natural insulation, drainage, and concealment. It can comfortably fit two trainers. For each additional hour you work on this shelter, you can comfortably fit another trainer. The shelter will remain standing without maintenance unless destroyed for up to a week. You may apply Tent Thatcher bonuses to this shelter.

features.name: At Ease in the Wild
features.description: You favor the wilds to human civilization and feel better rested when at your true home. When you and your Pokémon complete a rest of at least 6 hours in natural, non-artificial terrain, you and your Pokémon are considered well rested, even if conditions are harsh. If the rest is taken in a safe, undisturbed location, such as a shelter you constructed, you wake at maximum HP. This benefit applies to you, your Pokémon, any Helpful Pokémon, and your Companion Pokémon. Diseases, broken bones, and lingering injuries are not automatically healed.

features.name: Natural Guide
features.description: Rangers don’t always travel on their own and others don’t inherently work as well in the wild as their guide, except when they’re with you. While in the wild, difficult terrain does not slow you or any of your allies, you and your allies cannot become lost unless they are more than a mile away from you, and you and your allies do not suffer any penalties on Perception skill checks even while engaged in other activities. Additionally, allies have advantage while making climbing Skill checks while you are Freeclimbing ahead of them, 2 human allies can help you create shelter with Tent Thatcher in only 15 mins, and human allies also benefit from your At Ease in the Wild feature.

features.name: Natural Medicine
features.description: The wilds are full of herbs, resins, and other remedies, and your expertise allows you to make use of them in ways others cannot. You may spend one hour foraging for medicinal materials and one hour completing treatment. After this, you can do one of the following: - Heal a Pokémon or human (including yourself) to maximum HP - Close any open serious wounds. - Set broken bones, putting them into casts or splints. Your treatment requires careful attention and natural materials, so it cannot be rushed. If the patient is disturbed, the effect may fail or be partial.

features.name: Wildspeaker
features.description: At times, you are one with the wilds and do not even need your styler to command wild Pokémon. You may issue commands to wild Pokémon as if they are Helpful if the commands are for them to move away from yourself and your allies, to help complete a task related to making shelter, gathering food, or help to work against a natural non-Pokémon disaster. Additionally, you can understand basic needs of any non-violent wild Pokémon or if anything is agitating any Pokémon you’ve made Helpful.

features.name: One with Nature
features.description: You could do anything in the wilds and never need to revisit a city or town ever again. When making any skill checks out of combat in the wild, roll three times and use the best result. When rolling AC in the wild, you, your Pokémon, and your Companion Pokémon have advantage. While targeted by an attack while in the wilds, you have +2 Defense, Special Defense, and Speed. You are immune to afflictions while in the wild.

name: Researcher
flavorText:
Genius, Intuitive, Inventor
 Researchers spend years committing to memory every 
bit of knowledge that they can in order to maximize their 
chances of success in the Pokémon world. Often thought 
of as walking databases, a researcher is a valuable ally 
when navigating through any new situations. Once 
committed to a specialized area of expertise, they rapidly 
grow into professors, engineers, or even into talented 
artists.

features.name: Field Commander
features.description: Your expertise helps to see lines of strategy that might not necessarily need the help from one of your Pokémon in any given moment and by working with your allied trainers, you can help to turn tides and dominate the ever-flowing field of combat. You may issue commands to allied Pokémon who have not already acted during this round of combat. There must be understood consent from the Pokémon’s trainer unless they are unconscious. Pokémon may still only act once per round of an encounter. You still may only issue one command per round.

features.name: Walking Encyclopedia
features.description: You’ve already memorized it all. Every aspect of the Pokédex is lodged away in your head. You may look through the Pokédex books as much as you’d like without having used a Pokédex on a Pokémon.

features.name: Game Plan
features.description: By sharing various plans with teammates to employ while researching in the field, you’re ready to initiate strategies with various signals. 3/day as an action, move yourself, all allied trainers, and allied Pokémon within 30 ft of you, X ft, where X is your Special Attack or Special Defense modifier multiplied by 5. There must be understood consent from any allied Pokémon’s trainer unless they are unconscious. Unconscious or afflicted allied trainers and Pokémon cannot be moved by Game Plan.

features.name: Stat Increase and Advanced Class
features.description: Choose two different Trainer Stats to increase by 1, then gain 1d4 max HP. You only gain new stats at levels 3, 7, and 11. Choose a Researcher Advanced Class or a different base Class. You can only ever gain a single Class or Advanced Class at a time, when leveling up.

features.name: Repel Crafting
features.description: Advanced study of chemistry and an expansive knowledge of Pokémon has enabled you create concoctions repulsive to unfriendly Pokémon. After one hour of work, you can create a Repel. Name the concoction whatever you’d like out of whatever ingredients you’d like. The concoction loses its potency after 24 hours and becomes a useless solution of liquid. Home Made Repel – Wild Pokémon find the smell repulsive for one hour after applied, but may ignore it to protect something precious to them.

features.name: Critical Advice
features.description: By noticing and pointing out a weakness in a foe’s defenses, you help to refocus your group’s efforts to take down a threat. 3/day, once per turn as a free action, choose any target. Until the end of combat, whenever you, an allied Trainer, or an allied Pokémon attacks a chosen target, their attacks are Lethal during AC.

features.name: Demoralize
features.description: Your highbrow banter is particularly harsh and can really ruin your foe’s concentration. 3/day as an action, target yourself and any adjacent allied targets. Until your next turn, any attacks made against yourself, or adjacent allies have -3 during AC.

features.name: Stat Increase and Advanced Class
features.description: Choose two different Trainer Stats to increase by 1, then gain 1d4 max HP. You only gain new stats at levels 3, 7, and 11. Choose a Researcher Advanced Class or a different base Class. You can only ever gain a single Class or Advanced Class at a time, when leveling up.

features.name: Fighting Read
features.description: A quick study of a Pokémon’s behaviors can give away much more about itself than their trainer may want it to. As an action, target a Pokémon within 25ft. You learn the target’s current HP, held items, any unusual things about its typing, or stats. If the target is a wild Pokémon, you know the next action it will be taking on its next turn.

features.name: Investigative Ingenuity
features.description: Intuitive observation skills have served well in combat, but with little focus, you’ve applied your abilities to all occasions. While using your Investigate or Perception skills, you have advantage. Additionally, if your GM is introducing Pokémon that are not in the Pokédex books, you know the species of the Pokémon, its type(s), and any passives and moves they would have in a Pokédex entry.

features.name: Tactical Strike
features.description: Careful timing during the rhythm of battle can save others and turn the tide of battle in your favor. By practicing more signals, your friends can work with you to win in more situations. 3/day, as an action, you may issue a command to an allied Pokémon who has already acted during this round of combat. The command you issue must be to use an At-Will frequency move they know. The Pokémon may not use that At-Will move during their next turn. There must be understood consent from the Pokémon’s trainer unless they are unconscious.

features.name: Stat Increase and Advanced Class
features.description: Choose two different Trainer Stats to increase by 1, then gain 1d4 max HP. You only gain new stats at levels 3, 7, and 11. Choose a Researcher Advanced Class or a different base Class. You can only ever gain a single Class or Advanced Class at a time, when leveling up.

features.name: Walking Doctorate
features.description: Knowledge of the world comes easy and nothing stops your constant intellectual growth. By looking at a Pokémon, you can tell if it has any unusual characteristics that would not be found in a Pokédex book (such as different typing, significantly altered stats, etc.). You also can instantly identify any item, regardless of origin, and know its intended use though you might not be able to efficiently use it as intended. You can also identify any special talents of a trainer just by looking at them (what advanced classes they might have).

features.name: Poké Linguist
features.description: It doesn’t come easy, but with careful study and practice you learn to mimic and vocalize various Pokémon languages. By spending a total of thirty hours studying any species of Pokémon, you can speak to and understand that species of Pokémon in its tongue and all with all of its evolutions or pre-evolutions related to that Pokémon. You can only study one Pokémon language at a time.

features.name: Strategic Sabotage
features.description: Your careful placement and deliberate means of intimidation can set up perfect moments for your entire party. 1/day, as an action, move yourself, all trainers, and Pokémon within 45 ft of you, X multiplied by 5 ft, where X is your Special Attack or Special Defense modifier. Unconscious or afflicted allied trainers and Pokémon cannot be moved by Strategic Sabotage. Strategic Sabotage may be used as the first action of a round of combat regardless of your Speed.

features.name: Grand Strategist
features.description: Obsessive studying and long nights figuring out the optimal means of tactical deployment has molded you into a master strategist. Whenever yourself, an allied trainer, or allied Pokémon within 30ft of you uses an action or attacks, they may move 10ft afterwards. Whenever you issue a command to a Pokémon, the Pokémon gets +2 during its AC. Whenever you use an item on an adjacent ally, using the item is a free action once per turn. Finally, whenever you return a Pokémon to its Poké Ball and send out another Pokémon, it may act last during that round of combat instead of waiting for the next round of combat if you haven’t issued a command yet during that round of combat.

name: Archeologist
flavorText:
The power of history at your disposal. 
 When looking to solve the problems of the present and 
future, archeologists look to the past. They use fossils and 
their knowledge of geology to manipulate whatever they 
can. With enough practice, archeologists can even 
reanimate the long past and create their own Pokémon to 
study in the present.

features.name: Adventuring Historian
features.description: You’ve studied geological history obsessively and know everything there is to know about ancient history and exploring underground. Whenever making a History skill check or any skill check related to digging downwards, exploring underground, or exploring ruins, you have advantage.

features.name: Quick Dig
features.description: Digging and investigating downwards is the best way to find out more about the world’s past and you’re a master excavator. Using any shovel, over the course of ten minutes, you dig a 5ft3 hole in the ground. If anything is revealed in the space you dig up, you uncover it without damaging it. You need breaks to excavate this quickly and without damaging potential specimens. You can spend 3mins concealing any dug holes so it looks like regular ground unless spotted with the Investigate or Perception skills. You can’t use Quick Dig for more than twenty minutes at a time without a 10min break and can’t use Quick Dig for more than 3 hours per day. Additionally, 3/day after moving during an encounter, you may make all of the spaces you moved through into difficult terrain.

features.name: Stone Finder
features.description: Subterranean rock patterns are obvious to you, a studied geologist. Using your genius, you know where to find evolutionary stones or various other treasures! After spending at most half an hour using Quick Dig per day, you find an Evolutionary Stone, Weather Rock, Elemental Plate, valuable stone, or on very rare occasions, Mega Stone or Z-Crystal. Roll 1d100, subtracting your Special Attack or Special Defense modifier from the result and your GM will reveal what you’ve found.

features.name: Historical Resonance
features.description: You have an intuitive and almost magical sense of direction underground. You cannot get lost underground or in any ruins. When discerning direction of where you’d like to go within an unexplored area, you know what direction to go if you know what specific rooms or items you’re looking for. You also will always find any traps, natural or otherwise, while exploring underground or within ruins. Additionally, 1/day when entering a ruin, cave, or other ancient site, you may ask the GM one of the following questions: - What was this place built to protect, contain, or hide? - What danger claimed the most lives here? - What pattern or cycle defined life in this place? - What Pokémon once dominated this area? - What caused this place to be abandoned, destroyed, or sealed? When answering, the GM may be symbolic, fragmented, or cryptic but will still always be truthful.

features.name: Fossil Finder
features.description: Finding terranean tells of preserved specimens below ground has become natural to you, a studied geologist. Using your ingenuity, you know where to find fossils! After spending at most one hour using Quick Dig per day, you find a piece of a preserved Pokémon fossil which you can immediately identify. Roll 1d100, subtracting your Special Attack or Special Defense modifier from the result and your GM will reveal the species of the fossil you’ve found. The fossil will likely reflect the space you’ve excavated in; a water Pokémon near the ocean, a grass Pokémon in a forest, a rock or fire type near a volcano. If you’re lucky you’ll find an ancient fossil or fossils that might not reflect the Pokémon found locally in modern times.

features.name: Fossil Resurrection
features.description: You’ve studied for a long time and finally constructed your very own portable fossil reanimator. You build a Fossil Reanimator! If you lose or break your reanimator, it takes four hours for you to rebuild it or repair it. Your reanimator machine needs weekly maintenance and will break without your care. 1/day you may use your Fossil Reanimator for three hours to create an egg from any fossil that will hatch a Pokémon of the matching species. You may not use the same fossil more than once to create an egg this way. Your Fossil Reanimator can only be used once per day.

features.name: Fossil Tap
features.description: Using your reanimator and a fossil, you create items with powerful effects. 1/day you may use your fossil reanimator for 30 mins to create an Elemental Gem from any fossil. If you use the same fossil more than once a week with Fossil Tap, you destroy it. The Elemental Gem you make depends on the types of the fossilized Pokémon you use. Your Fossil Reanimator can only be used once per day. Elemental Gem - Elemental Gems each correspond to a specific Pokémon type. They each have the following ability: The first time you would use a move with power that matches this gem’s type, give the move +1d power, then destroy this gem. Additionally, 1/day you may use your fossil reanimator for 3 hours to create one of the following items from a fossil. If you use the same fossil more than once a week with Fossil Tap, you destroy it. The item you make depends on the species of the fossilized Pokémon you use. A Pokémon with claws or blades can used to make Grip Claw or Quick Claw while a Pokémon with fangs or sharp teeth can be used to make Razor Fang or Razor Claw. Your Fossil Reanimator can only be used once per day. Grip Claw - If you bind a foe and your foe tries to escape, they must roll +4 higher to escape successfully. Quick Claw - On your first single-target melee attack with at-will frequency per day, the attack gains the following effect: “This attack has Priority.” Razor Claw - On your first single-target melee attack per day, the attack gains the following effect: “This attack is Lethal.” Razor Fang - Your Latched attacks deal +2 damage.

features.name: Memory Machine
features.description: Making history with your mad science, you make a TR from a fossil. 1/day you may use your fossil reanimator for 4 hours to create a TR from any fossil. If you attempt to use Memory Machine on the same fossil twice, you destroy the fossil. The TR you create is based on the fossilized Pokémon you use. Choose a move from that Pokémon’s starting moves in the Pokédex or any previous stage of evolution’s starting moves in the Pokédex. Your Fossil Reanimator can only be used once per day.

features.name: Cave In
features.description: You’ve set your excavated holes with dangerous traps that can cause some major harm. 1/day, after spending 5 mins near one of your holes you’ve made with Quick Dig, you rig it to use one of the following moves on anything that steps over the hole ignoring the move’s range: Arena Trap, Sand Tomb, or Rock Slide. Use your Special Attack or Special Defense modifier while rolling your AC for the moves. The hole is concealed and looks like regular ground unless spotted with the Investigate or Perception skills. Arena Trap - 1/day Ranged(20ft burst) Ground Effect. Place a Quicksand Hazard on the ground in target area. Anyone who ends their turn in the Hazard is then pulled 15ft towards the center. The Quicksand Hazard is difficult terrain. Sand Tomb - 3/day Physical Ranged(10ft): Ground 3d6. Place a Sandtrap Hazard on the ground in target area. Sandtrap Hazard deal 5 damage to characters at the start of their turn and are difficult terrain. Rock Slide - 1/day Physical Ranged(20ft, 10ft wave): Rock 3d10. On hit, 16 or higher during AC inflicts Dazed. The area of Rock Slide becomes difficult terrain.

features.name: Stone Master
features.description: Using your intuition and by simply feeling the earth, you know where to find rare, lost, treasures. After spending at most one hour using Quick Dig per day, you locate a valuable stone, a mega stone, or z-crystal. Roll 1d100, subtracting your Special Attack and Special Defense modifier from the result and your GM will reveal what you’ve found. Alternately, you can search instead for a specific Evolution stone and you will successfully find it after at most one hour using Quick Dig per day.

features.name: Extinct Adaptations
features.description: Your resurrected Pokémon have some additional modifications that you’ve made based on your knowledge of their species in ancient times. When creating an egg with Fossil Resurrection, note one of the following Passives: Ancient Resistance, Hazard Immunity, or Terrain Master. When the Pokémon hatches, it will have that Passive. If they makes a Pokémon have more than three Passives, you must choose and remove one. Ancient Resistance (Rock-type attacks are resisted by you. If you are already resistant to Rock-type, remove an additional damage die.) Hazard Immunity (When you gain Hazard Immunity, choose three types of Hazard. You are unaffected by those three types of Hazard.) Terrain Master (Ignore penalties while moving through hindering or difficult terrain.)

features.name: Lovable Atrocities
features.description: Others may call you insane, but you hold the power of history in your hands! Once per week, you can use any two fossils simultaneously with your portable fossil reanimator. The resulting Pokémon egg will hatch a Pokémon that will not be able to evolve but will have aspects of both fossil’s Pokémon combined (The Pokémon who hatches can be based on any stage in the evolutionary families of each combined fossil, not just the base form– for example Machoke and Alakazam). Its types will be one type from each of the fossil’s species. Each of its stats should be an average of the two fossil’s species stats. It’s passives and moves should be a combination of the basic available passives and moves from each fossil’s species. All other information about the Pokémon and its appearance is up to you. Your Fossil Reanimator can only be used once per day.

name: Ball Smith
flavorText:
Poké Ball mastery opens doors to many new captures.
 Studying the ways of the ball smith has led to your own 
ingenious ball inventions. The ball smith takes every piece 
of technological expertise and combines it with the 
ancient art of transforming apricorns into capture devices. 
Without limits, you can invent any kind of ball for any 
situation.

features.name: Capture Point
features.description: Your specialized knowledge of how to use Poké Balls give you an edge while tossing one at wild Pokémon. Whenever you throw a Poké Ball, subtract your Special Attack or Special Defense modifier from the capture roll.

features.name: Apricorn Ball
features.description: Basic smithing knowledge and practice has yielded excellent results- hand made Poké Balls made by you. After 30 mins of work with your Poké Ball smith kit, change any apricorn into a Basic Ball.

features.name: Basic Ball
features.description: +5 to your capture roll.

features.name: Poké Ball Repair
features.description: Using spare parts from multiple broken Poke Balls means you can recycle Poké Balls for more uses! After 30 mins of work with your Poké Ball smith kit, you can turn two broken Poké Balls into a Basic Ball, or if the broken Poké Balls are the same type of ball, you turn them into one undamaged version of the same Poké Ball.

features.name: Poké Ball Improvements
features.description: Continued work yields better results and your spare time quickly improves every Poké Ball you have laying around. After 1 hour of work with your Poké Ball smith kit, change any Basic Ball into a Great Ball, or a Great Ball into an Ultra Ball.

features.name: Great Ball
features.description: – +0 to your capture roll.

features.name: Ultra Ball
features.description: – -5 from your capture roll.

features.name: Type Mod
features.description: Study, focus, and some great ideas has helped you to invent new ways to capture Pokémon with your home crafted Poké Balls. After 1 hour of work with your Poké Ball smith kit, change any Great Ball or Ultra Ball into a Net Ball, Earth Ball, Umbra Ball, Solid Ball, Heat Ball, Mystic Ball, Zephyr Ball, Vigor Ball, or Fine Ball. The properties of these unique balls are identical to the Net Ball, but instead of affecting Bug and Water types like the Net Ball, these Balls correspond to the following types: Earth Ball, Grass and Ground; Umbra Ball, Dark and Ghost; Solid Ball, Rock and Steel; Heat Ball, Electric and Fire; Mystic Ball, Dragon and Psychic; Zephyr Ball, Flying and Ice; Vigor Ball, Poison and Fighting; Fine Ball, Normal and Fairy.

features.name: Net Ball
features.description: -15 from your capture roll when used against a Bug or Water type Pokémon.

features.name: Time Mod
features.description: Some tweaking on your Poké Ball’s rumble motors have enabled you to create some more advanced Poké Balls. After 1 hour of work with your Poké Ball smith kit, change any Great Ball or Ultra Ball into a Dusk Ball, Quick Ball, Repeat Ball or Timer Ball. You can also make a Day Ball, which has the same effect as the Dusk Ball but works for day time (sunlight) instead.

features.name: Dusk Ball
features.description: -7 from your capture roll if it’s night time (no sunlight).

features.name: Quick Ball
features.description: -16 from your capture roll if thrown as your first action during combat.

features.name: Repeat Ball
features.description: -10 from your capture roll if you’ve already thrown a Poké Ball at the target this encounter.

features.name: Timer Ball
features.description: -10 from your capture roll if the encounter has lasted at least one minute; subtract 25 from your capture roll if the encounter has lasted at least two minutes instead.

features.name: Multiball
features.description: Quick moves and a furious need for capture splits your focus in two ways. 3/day, as an action, you may throw two Poké Balls at two different targets.

features.name: Environment Mod
features.description: The study of the earth’s climates and landscapes have led you to invent more new ways to capture Pokémon with your home crafted Poké Balls. After 1 hour of work with your Poké Ball smith kit, change any Great Ball or Ultra Ball into an Arctic Ball, Mountain Ball, Desert Ball, Grassland Ball, Rainforest Ball, Forest Ball, Tundra Ball, Taiga Ball, Marsh Ball, Beach Ball, Freshwater Ball, Urban Ball or Cave Ball. Environment Ball (Name varies): -12 from your capture roll if used within the matching environment.

features.name: False Swipe
features.description: By training your Pokémon carefully, they have become much better at readying Pokémon for your capture. 1/day while issuing a command to one of your Pokémon who you’ve owned for at least a week, you may add this effect to the move they are using, “This attack cannot be used to knock out a target. Instead, the target will still have 1 HP no matter how much damage it would have dealt.”

features.name: Advanced Design
features.description: You’ve invented, created, and designed many Poké Balls so naturally any store-bought balls are easy to replicate. After 1 hour of work with your Poké Ball smith kit, change any Great Ball or Ultra Ball into a Premier Ball, Fast Ball, Friend Ball, Heal Ball, Heavy Ball, Level Ball, Love Ball, Lure Ball, Luxury Ball, Moon Ball, Nest Ball, Cherish Ball, Dream Ball, Park Ball, Safari Ball, or Sport Ball.

features.name: Cherish Ball
features.description: -5 from your capture roll. Captured Pokémon are more easily befriended.

features.name: Friend Ball
features.description: +0 to your capture roll. Captured Pokémon are more easily befriended.

features.name: Luxury Ball
features.description: -5 from your capture roll. Captured Pokémon are more easily befriended.

features.name: Premier Ball
features.description: -5 from your capture roll. Captured Pokémon are more easily befriended.

features.name: Fast Ball
features.description: -8 from your capture roll on a Pokémon that acts before your Pokémon.

features.name: Heal Ball
features.description: +0 to your capture roll. Captured Pokémon are healed 20 hit points.

features.name: Heavy Ball
features.description: -15 from your capture roll if the Pokémon is Heavy or Superweight.

features.name: Level Ball
features.description: -10 from your capture roll if the Pokémon is fully evolved, and did evolve at least once.

features.name: Nest Ball
features.description: -10 from your capture roll if the Pokémon can evolve, but is not evolved.

features.name: Love Ball
features.description: -10 from your capture roll if the target shares a type with one of your active Pokémon.

features.name: Lure Ball
features.description: -10 from your capture roll if you lured the wild Pokémon into combat.

features.name: Moon Ball
features.description: -10 from your capture roll if the Pokémon evolves with an evolution stone.

features.name: Dream Ball
features.description: -10 from your capture roll if the target is afflicted.

features.name: Park Ball
features.description: -25 from your capture roll against domesticated wild Pokémon.

features.name: Safari Ball
features.description: -25 from your capture roll against domesticated wild Pokémon.

features.name: Sport Ball
features.description: -25 from your capture roll against domesticated wild Pokémon.

features.name: Odd Ball
features.description: With some additional tweaking you’ve made a few more Poké Balls with strange purposes. You’re not even entirely sure what you’re hunting for but this might help to catch it. After a total of 8 hours of work with your Poké Ball smith kit, combine a total of three of your crafted Ultra Balls or modified Poké Balls into one Beast Ball or Strange Ball.

features.name: Beast Ball
features.description: -25 from your capture roll if the Pokémon is from a parallel dimension.

features.name: Strange Ball
features.description: -25 from your capture roll if the Pokémon is temporally displaced.

features.name: Master Mod
features.description: All of your work has led to this design, the absolute strongest Poké Ball that you can make. Once per week, after a total of 20 hours of work with your Poké Ball smith kit, combine a total of twenty of your crafted Ultra Balls or modified Poké Balls into one Master Ball.

features.name: Master Ball
features.description: -100 from your capture roll. The Master Ball can and will often fail when used against legendary or mythical Pokémon.

name: Photographer
flavorText:
An artistic eye for study and observation. 
 A skilled eye and a steady hand makes for an excellent 
photographer. While the camera itself could be basic, 
your expertise brings out the best of any shot. This kind of 
research makes for an alternative to strictly academic 
studies. Who knows? With enough practice you could 
enter pictures into art galleries or even make a living 
selling your goods.

features.name: Camera Flash
features.description: At the right angle, your camera can be used for more than pictures. Once per turn, whenever you use your action to take a picture with your camera, you may also use the move Camera Flash. Camera Flash - At-Will Ranged(5ft) Normal Effect. On hit, the target has disadvantage on AC until your next turn.

features.name: Pester Ball β
features.description: In learning about Poké photography, you studied the mechanics of the pester balls that were used for setting up the perfect pictures. You can make the simplest ones. 3/day, you can spend 30 mins to build a Pester Ball Beta. Pester Ball Beta can be thrown as an action. Your pester balls lose their charges and need to be rebuilt if they are not used within 72 hours. Pester Ball β - At-Will Ranged(10ft) Normal Effect. On hit, the target is Confused until the end of their next turn.

features.name: Rapid Shot
features.description: With a steady, but nimble, shutter finger you can quickly take masterful shot in stressful situations. You can take up to three pictures of different targets during your turn as free actions. Also, you may take a picture of anything during another trainer’s action or a Pokémon’s action as a free Reaction if you have taken less than 3 pictures so far that round. Additionally, your picture-taking has these effects during combat: - Whenever you take a picture of an ally’s Pokémon using an attack, they get +1 during their next AC for each time you’ve taken a picture of that Pokémon this combat (up to +3). - Whenever you take a picture of an ally, they get +1 during their next skill check for each time you’ve taken a picture of them this combat (up to +3). - The first time you take a third picture of any ally in combat, they get +4 temporary HP. - Whenever you take a picture of a foe’s Pokémon using an attack within 10ft, they get -1 during their next AC.

features.name: Pester Ball δ
features.description: The next pester ball you learned to recreate is a bit more dangerous, but could be useful in a pinch. 3/day, you can spend 30 mins to build a Pester Ball Delta. Pester Ball Delta can be thrown as an action. Your pester balls lose their charges and need to be rebuilt if they are not used within 72 hours. Pester Ball δ - At-Will Ranged(10ft) Normal Effect. On hit, the target may only use attacks that target you until the end of their next turn.

features.name: Overexposure
features.description: After many shots of an enemy Pokémon with your camera, you quickly supply your Pokémon with ready advice. Your picture-taking has these effects during combat: - The first time you take a third picture of any enemy Pokémon in combat, choose an allied Pokémon. The next time that ally attacks that enemy Pokémon, their attack gets +1d power. - The first time you take a fifth picture of any foe, the next time an ally targets that foe, they have advantage during AC. - Once you have taken at least three pictures of any foe, you may start using Camera Flash on them with up to 15ft range.

features.name: Close Examination
features.description: Your quick study gives away more than a foe’s strength, it exposes their weaknesses. 3/day, as an action, you may use Center Frame or Negative Development. Center Frame - 3/day Ranged(10ft) Normal Effect. Choose a foe and an ally within range. The next time the targeted ally attacks the targeted foe, they cannot miss. Negative Development - 3/day Ranged(25ft) Normal Effect. Negative Development cannot miss. Choose a foe, one type immunity that foe has, and an ally within range. When the targeted ally makes against the targeted foe, that attack ignores the chosen type immunity.

features.name: Pester Ball λ & φ
features.description: The next pester balls you throw provide cover as you maneuver the field of combat. 3/day, you can spend 30 mins to build a Pester Ball Lambda or Phi. Pester Ball Lambda or Phi can be thrown as an action. Your pester balls lose their charges and need to be rebuilt if they are not used within 72 hours. Pester Ball λ - At-Will Ranged(20ft, 10ft blast) Normal Effect. Place Smokescreen Hazard in the targeted area. Moves made into or out of the the Smokescreen Hazard have disadvantage. Pester Ball φ - At-Will Ranged(20ft, 20ft blast) Normal Effect. Place Lightbloom Hazard in the targeted area. Reactions cannot be made within the Lightbloom Hazard .

features.name: Capture Shot
features.description: Your subjects are more easily captured after a couple of quick shots and some quick studying on the best way to combat and capture Pokémon. Your picture-taking has these effects during combat: - Once you have taken at least three pictures of any wild Pokémon, subtract your Special Attack and Special Defense modifiers from your capture rolls made against that wild Pokémon. - Once you have taken at least three pictures of any allied Pokémon, they may reroll any one die when rolling damage.

features.name: Shutterstorm
features.description: As your camera snaps in rapid succession, you capture the battlefield’s perfect angles, guiding your allies with each decisive shot. 1/day as an action, take up to 3 pictures of different targets. Any trainers or Pokémon adjacent to a photographed target is also affected. Affected allies may add +1d4 to an AC, a damage roll, or a skill check, once this combat. Affected enemies have -2 during their next AC or skill check. If a target is photographed multiple times during Shutterstorm, allies may gain one additional +1d4 bonus, and enemies have -4 to their next AC or skill check. Shutterstorm photographs counts toward your features that track how many times you have captured different subjects in photographs in the same combat.

features.name: Pester Balls Ω, Σ, & Θ
features.description: Building pester balls for special effects during photography has led you to create your very own offensive pester balls. 3/day, you can spend 30 mins to build a Pester Ball Omega, Sigma, or Theta. Pester Ball Omega, Sigma, or Theta can be thrown as an action. Your pester balls lose their charges and need to be rebuilt if they are not used within 72 hours. Pester Ball Ω - At-Will Special Ranged(10ft): Fire 2d6. Create a Cinder Hazard in one of the target’s spaces. Characters who end their turn on a Cinder Hazard are Burned. Pester Ball Σ - At-Will Special Ranged(10ft): Ice 2d6. Create a Frostsnap Hazard in one of the target’s spaces. Characters who end their turn on a Frostsnap Hazard get Frostbite. Pester Ball Θ - At-Will Special Ranged(10ft): Electric 2d6. Create a Zap Hazard in one of the target’s spaces. Characters who end their turn on a Zap Hazard are Paralyzed.

features.name: Photographic Analysis
features.description: A careful study of a photographed foe gives your Pokémon expert advice to completely destroy your enemies. Your picture-taking has these effects during combat: - The first time you take a fifth picture of any enemy Pokémon in combat, choose an allied Pokémon. The next time that ally attacks that enemy Pokémon, their attack gets +3d power . - Once you have taken at nine pictures of any target, you may start using Camera Flash with up to 25ft range.

features.name: Pester Master Ball
features.description: You are a mechanical wizard and you’ve mastered all sorts of technical tricks to make your pester balls work in harmony with your photography while also working over time in battle. It only takes you ten minutes to make pester balls with your Photographer features and may make them as many times as you’d like per day. Your pester balls last for one week, then lose their charges. When making your pester balls, you may combine the effects of two of Pester Balls, although you cannot combine Omega, Sigma, or Theta with each other.

name: Scientist
flavorText:
Various concoctions with variable effects, made to order. 
 The scientist throws formulas together and figures out 
what works, combining all sorts of ingredients to produce 
various items with effects indistinguishable from products 
from stores. While chemistry does come into play, 
scientists seemingly produce incredible result with the 
least expected ingredients over and over again.

features.name: Potion Maker
features.description: Potions aren’t intuitive, but study and practice has led you to be able to brew your own potions. 3/day, after spending 30 mins with your portable chem set, you brew a Potion. Call the concoction whatever you’d like, made out of whatever ingredients you’d like. The concoction loses its potency after 48 hours.

features.name: Potion
features.description: Heals a Pokémon 12 HP.

features.name: Repel Master
features.description: Through trial and error, you’ve developed your own spray repulsive to wild Pokémon. 3/day, after spending 30 mins with your portable chem set, you brew a Super Repel. Call the concoction whatever you’d like, made out of whatever ingredients you’d like. The concoction loses its potency after 48 hours. Super Repel – Wild Pokémon find the smell repulsive for three hours after applied, but may ignore it to protect something precious to them.

features.name: Remedy Brewing
features.description: Antidotes and relaxants among others are basic brews for a chemist, but require your practice and time. 3/day, after spending 30 mins with your portable chem set, roll 1d6. On a result of 1, you brew a Touga Spray; on 2, an Antidote; on 3, a Paralyze Heal; on 4, an Awakening; on 5, a Burn Heal; on 6, an Ice Heal. Call the concoction whatever you’d like, made out of whatever ingredients you’d like. The concoction loses its effects after 48 hours.

features.name: Touga Spray
features.description: Cures Entranced.

features.name: Antidote
features.description: Cures Poisoned or Toxified.

features.name: Awakening
features.description: Cures Drowsy.

features.name: Burn Heal
features.description: Cures Burned.

features.name: Ice Heal
features.description: Cures Frostbite.

features.name: Paralyze Heal
features.description: Cures Paralysis.

features.name: Ether Maker
features.description: While experimenting with your chemist’s set, you’ve created an energy spray that reinvigorates your Pokémon. 3/day, after spending 1 hour with your portable chem set, you create an Ether. Call the concoction whatever you’d like, made out of whatever ingredients you’d like. The concoction loses its potency after 48 hours.

features.name: Ether
features.description: A Pokémon’s strength is partially restored and regains a single use of one of its 3/day moves.

features.name: Performance Enhancers
features.description: Your experiments with different solutions have led you to inventing boosters that work much like those sold in Poké Marts. 3/day, after spending 30 mins of work with your portable chem set, roll 1d8. On a result of 1, you brew an X Attack; on 2, an X Defend; on 3, an X Special; on 4, an X Sp. Def; on 5, an X Speed; on 6, an X Accuracy; on 7, a Dire Hit; on 8, a Guard Spec. Call the concoction whatever you’d like, made out of whatever ingredients you’d like. The concoction loses its potency after 48 hours.

features.name: X Attack
features.description: Gives a Pokémon Attack▲.

features.name: X Defend
features.description: Gives a Pokémon Defense▲.

features.name: X Special
features.description: Gives a Pokémon SpAttack▲. X Sp. Def: Gives a Pokémon SpDefense▲.

features.name: X Speed
features.description: Gives a Pokémon Speed▲.

features.name: X Accuracy
features.description: Increases a Pokémon’s AC by +1.

features.name: Dire Hit
features.description: The next attack the Pokémon makes is Lethal. Guard Spec.: The next time the Pokémon would get ▼ from a foe, ignore it.

features.name: Remedy Solver
features.description: No ailment is able to resist your intellect, your solution fixes anything. 1/day, after spending 1 hour with your portable chem set, you create a Full Heal. Call the concoction whatever you’d like, made out of whatever ingredients you’d like. The concoction loses its potency after 3 days.

features.name: Full Heal
features.description: Cures all afflictions.

features.name: Elixir Mixer
features.description: Powerful energy drinks filled with various spirits and vitamins empower your Pokémon to release their inner strength time and time again. 1/day, after spending 1 hour with your portable chem set, you create an Elixir. Call the concoction whatever you’d like, made out of whatever ingredients you’d like. The concoction loses its potency after 3 days.

features.name: Elixir
features.description: A Pokémon’s strength is partially Restored and regains a single use of one of its 1/day moves.

features.name: Revival Mixer
features.description: Not the easiest to make, but a required mix to have in a chemist’s mind. Through trial and error, you’ve developed a revival pill to rival those in stores. 1/day, after spending 1 hour with your portable chem set, you create an Revive. Call the concoction whatever you’d like, made out of whatever ingredients you’d like. The concoction loses its effects after 3 days.

features.name: Revive
features.description: Restore an unconscious Pokémon to half of its max HP.

features.name: Mint Maker
features.description: Behavior altering medicines are rare and it’s difficult to manipulate their specific effects, but you make them anyway. Once per week, after spending 4 hours with your portable chem set, roll 1d6. On a result of 1, you create a Cinnaleaf Mint; on 2, a Stonebalm Mint; on 3, a Spearmist Mint; on 4, a Calmrest Mint; on 5, a Lightwind Mint; on 6, a Pureleaf Mint. Call the concoction whatever you’d like, made out of whatever ingredients you’d like. The concoction loses its potency after 12 hours.

features.name: Cinnaleaf Mint
features.description: Raise Attack 1 point, then lower Defense, Special Attack, Special Defense or Speed 1 point.

features.name: Stonebalm Mint
features.description: Raise Defense 1 point, then lower Attack, Special Attack, Special Defense or Speed 1 point.

features.name: Spearmist Mint
features.description: Raise Special Attack 1 point, then lower Attack, Defense, Special Defense or Speed 1 point.

features.name: Calmrest Mint
features.description: Raise Special Defense 1 point, then lower Attack, Defense, Special Attack or Speed 1 point.

features.name: Lightwind Mint
features.description: Raise Speed 1 point, then lower Attack, Defense, Special Attack or Special Defense 1 point.

features.name: Pureleaf Mint
features.description: Do not add to or subtract from any stats after removing the effects on stats because of the Pokémon’s nature.

features.name: Vitamin Maker
features.description: The ultimate work of a chemist, the stat-empowering vitamin, is a secret kept with every scientist who develops their own formula. 1/day, after spending 3 hours with your portable chem set, roll 1d6. On a result of 1, you brew an HP Up; on 2, a Protein; on 3, an Iron; on 4, a Calcium; on 5, a Zinc; on 6, a Carbos. Call the concoction whatever you’d like, made out of whatever ingredients you’d like. The concoction loses its potency if it is not used within 12 hours.

features.name: HP Up
features.description: Increase HP by 4 for two weeks.

features.name: Protein
features.description: Increase Attack by 1 for two weeks.

features.name: Iron
features.description: Increase Defense by 1 for two weeks.

features.name: Calcium
features.description: Increase Special Attack by 1 for two weeks.

features.name: Zinc
features.description: Increase Special Defense by 1 for two weeks.

features.name: Carbos
features.description: Increase speed by 1 for two weeks.

features.name: No Expiration Date
features.description: Refining your efforts and minimizing waste you’ve maximized the preservatives in your concoctions.
