Your concoctions made with Scientist features last for X years, where X is your Special Attack or Special Defense modifier. Additionally, 3/day, as an action, you can apply 2 items to a Pokémon at once.

features.name: Master Chemist
features.description: You’ve solved every solution and brewed every beverage and as long as you’ve got the time, you’ll never stop working on your medicines. Your Scientist features can be used as often as you’d like, ignoring any daily frequency limitations. All brews take half the time to produce with Scientist features. Anytime you’d produce something with a Scientist feature at random, instead choose what you produce. When brewing with your features, roll 1d20. On 11 or higher, make two of the item you create at the end of your work.

name: Watcher
flavorText:
Talent with a pencil, patience for the sketch.
 Watchers are field researchers who go out and study, 
track, and locate wild Pokémon. They have a natural calm 
about them and use their passive presence to take in 
information and replicate it with their artistic ability. 
Watchers watch everything and take in information that 
would otherwise go unnoticed by most.

features.name: Close Watch
features.description: Your careful curiosity and love of watching Pokémon has given you the ability to wander through wild Pokémon without disturbing them. You may approach and pass by wild Pokémon without alerting them to your presence as long as you stay 20 feet away from the wild. If you announce your presence, the Pokémon you approach is not instantly provoked but may be startled. You may attempt to befriend the wild if you don’t provoke it. Additionally, if you have observed a Pokémon for at least half an hour and drawn it, its species (not its whole evolutionary line) becomes permanently Cataloged.

features.name: Quick Draw
features.description: You’ve practiced drawing for years and years, but after mastering your ability to draw quickly and accurately, you’re officially a Watcher. You are a master sketch artist. It takes you less than a minute to sketch anything you see. You can flesh out a sketch over thirty minutes to add more detail. After an hour of work, you can draw anything you’ve seen in the last 24 hours with amazing detail. Additionally, each round you may observe a target as a free action. If you have observed a target for two turns in a row, it is Studied for the next hour.

features.name: Discriminating Gaze
features.description: By focusing on a Pokémon, you can figure out what it’s about to do. 3/day, as a free action, target a Studied Pokémon within 25ft. As long as the target is not controlled by another player, you know what actions it will take and any attacks it will attempt on its next turn.

features.name: Field Catalog
features.description: Time spent observing Pokémon is never wasted and your growing catalog helps you find anything you’ve observed before for further study. After 10 minutes in a wild space, you can determine if there are any of your Cataloged species in that wild space within 10 miles. Additionally, you have advantage on skill checks made while attempting to track or locate any Cataloged species.

features.name: Reading the Trainer
features.description: Just like the Pokémon you study, people have tells and your understanding reveals much about those around you. 3/day, as a free action, target a Studied trainer within 25ft. You may find out one of the following things: - Any other Pokémon the trainer has with them in Poké Balls or concealed nearby. - As long as the trainer isn’t another player, what their next action will be and any command that they will issue to a Pokémon on their next turn. - If they are being truthful or lying as long as they remain Studied.

features.name: Species Spotter
features.description: Your growing sketch catalog is improving your ability to intuit the actions of those around you as you apply your knowledge to those you encounter. Any Cataloged Pokémon are immediately considered Studied when you encounter them. Additionally, you and your Pokémon cannot be ambushed or surprised by Cataloged Pokémon. Additionally, whenever a Studied Pokémon uses an attack against you or any of your Pokémon that it has already used this combat, it has -1 during AC.

features.name: Strategic Tells
features.description: People and Pokémon actually have a lot in common when it comes to basic behavior and it’s not surprising that a trainer’s mannerisms are easy to trace in their Pokémon’s actions. Anytime a Studied trainer sends out or reveals one of their Pokémon, their Pokémon immediately counts as Studied. 1/day If a Studied subject tries to use a Reaction against you or your Pokémon, you may roll back your action and make a different action to prevent the use of that Reaction. Additionally, 1/day If a Studied subject tries to use a move with Priority against you or your Pokémon, Priority will not let that Studied subject act before your Pokémon (use Speed to determine turn order as usual).

features.name: Move Mimicry
features.description: Your study has yielded interesting results and even your Pokémon can replicate the things that they see. 1/day, after six hours of training, you may teach one of your Pokémon the move Mimic. Mimic - 3/day Self Normal Effect. For the remainder of the encounter you may not use Mimic and you may instead use the non-Legendary Move last used by a Studied Pokémon as if it was on your move list. You must still follow the borrowed move’s frequency, typing, power and effects as if you know the Move.

features.name: Micro Expressionist
features.description: Communication with others seems so natural after studying many of your friends and Pokémon. You may nonverbally communicate complete sentences with allied trainers, who you’ve traveled with for at least a week, and they will understand you and you will understand them. You also can understand any needs or messages your Pokémon may be trying to communicate to you.

features.name: Living Index
features.description: At this point, you might be more useful than anyone’s Pokédex, as your insight encompasses more than the fact sheet you can look up, it’s a living body of knowledge shaped by pattern, behavior, and firsthand study. For every 25 Pokémon you’ve Cataloged, you, your allied trainers, and any allied Pokémon within 25ft have +1 to your initiatives. Also, any time an allied Pokémon targets a Pokémon that you’ve Cataloged, they have +1 during AC. Additionally, when observing a target as a free action, they are considered Studied immediately and remain that way for the next two hours.

features.name: Shiny Finder
features.description: While observing wilds you’ve learned how to track down the rarest wilds out there- shiny Pokémon. Once per week, after spending six hours studying in the wilds, you locate a shiny wild Pokémon. You may specifically seek Cataloged Pokémon if they are found in the wild where you are. If you announce your presence, the Pokémon you approach is not instantly provoked but may be startled. You may attempt to befriend the wild if you don’t provoke it.

features.name: Behavioral Emulation
features.description: Looks simple enough, and you’ve noted everything worth figuring out, so let’s just give it a try! 1/day, you may use a Feature or imitate and action that you just witnessed another Studied trainer perform. Behavioral Emulation cannot imitate anything that requires some kind of physical component that you do not have (crafting a Poké Ball without a Poké Ball smith kit), some feat that requires a physicality you do not have (lifting a boulder without a similar level of strength), is something that takes longer than 1 hour (building a bike from scraps), or is an action you could not have actually witnessed (determining hidden information by thinking). Behavioral Emulation cannot imitate Features gained from a Pokémon, Legendary sources. Any resources required by the imitated Feature must still be paid, if applicable. Behavioral Emulation also may not be used to grant permanent bonuses or lasting effects beyond one hour. Any rolls made as part of the imitated action are made using your own stats and modifiers. If the imitated Feature requires a check, the GM may increase the DC at their discretion.
